533267|2026-06.headline: Cantabil Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% to INR178.8 crores and EBITDA margin widened to 33.2%, but PAT margin slipped to 9.1%.
533267|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 13% YoY to INR178.8 crores and EBITDA grew 21% to INR59.4 crores, with margin up to 33.2% from 30.8%. PAT grew about 11% to INR16.3 crores, but PAT margin was 9.1% versus 9.2% a year ago. Management attributed the margin gain to product mix and price increases passed to customers, and said July demand was moderate with festive timing shifting into Q3. Management reiterated the INR1,000 crore FY27 revenue target and about 5% SSG for the full year, relying on new stores and a Q2 opening push of 28-30 stores.

financial_highlights.value: 667 stores, 9.42 lakh sq ft retail area

segments.name: Retail stores (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q1 opened 15 stores totalling about 27,000 sq ft; average Q1 opening store size 1,810 sq ft. Average store sales were INR1.26 crore in FY26, with mature stores at about INR1.5 crore and stores under 1-1.5 years near INR1 crore.

segments.name: Online
segments.commentary: Online share fell to about 5% in Q1 from 6% in FY26 because of a software and end-to-end integration change; management targets 8% for FY27 and says online is run above EBITDA level.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR1,000 crores reiterated, implying about 18-19% growth; management split this into 10-12% volume growth plus inflation pass-through.
Full-year SSG target about 5% (management also cited a 5-6% long-term aspiration), with about 3% from price and balance from volume.
Average annual gross margin target of about 60% and EBITDA margin of 30% or more maintained; PAT margin ambition 11-12%.
Store additions of 28-30 in Q2 FY27 and about 55,000-60,000 sq ft; average store size target around 1,500 sq ft by year end.
Working capital cycle guided at 100-105 days; finished goods inventory target 110-120 days.
Management expects volume growth to pick up in Q3 as Diwali falls on about 10 November, and says Q2 volume growth will be limited.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 openings of 15 stores (about 27,000 sq ft); Q2 plan of 28-30 stores and 55,000-60,000 sq ft.
Store sizes are rising: average opening store 1,810 sq ft in Q1 versus about 1,500 sq ft average over the last two years.
Franchise store count fell from 178 (FY23) to 130 as the company moves to larger formats that franchisees find hard to fund in Tier 3 towns.
Around 20-25 stores close each year on performance, market or franchise issues; management calls this normal.
Inventory ageing: about 75% under 1 year, 20% 1-3 years, about 5% over 3 years (mainly surplus factory outlet).
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth of 4.04% in Q1; volume growth about 7-8% against about 13% area growth.
Raw material prices up about 10% (earlier 20-25%); management says the full cost is being passed to customers with no volume impact, though cotton is up 10-15%.
July was moderate; Raksha Bandhan moved to late August (versus 10 August last year), so festive sales shifted and management declined to comment on the current quarter.
Management says it will not pursue premiumisation; ASP is about INR1,100 and is to be held there.
Competition: new-age and D2C brands are said to share about 50-60% of their basic casual and formal ranges with Cantabil; management frames the difference as roughly 40% of the collection.
Repeat customers are close to 50%; management is not launching a points-based loyalty programme for now but will consider it.
Q1 gross margin rose on product mix plus inflation correction; management says gross margin will move up and down by quarter but the annual target holds.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin expand YoY and QoQ, and will it sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of product mix and inflation correction; it expects the average annual gross margin of about 60% to hold, with quarterly swings possible.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Haryana and UP minimum wage hikes hit employee costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; Haryana wages rose about 30-35% and that cost is in Q1. Management said the full quarter's impact is captured and there is no further large impact.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to the INR25 crore loan to a real estate developer?
qa_highlights.answer: INR10 crore was repaid in Q1; the remaining INR15 crore is due by about February. Management said such transactions will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,000 crore revenue target achievable and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is on track, with new stores, SSG and online as drivers, and Q2 openings expected to recover the Q1 shortfall.

qa_highlights.question: Why has ROCE fallen and how are inventory days being managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished goods inventory days fell to 114 in FY26 from 121 in FY25; working capital days fell to about 100 from 110. Management aims for 110-120 days and says ROCE is about 40%.

qa_highlights.question: Why has franchise (FOCO) count declined?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bigger store formats need larger investment, which franchisees in Tier 3 towns are not willing to make, and most stores are in Tier 2 and beyond.

risks_watch: PAT margin flat at 9.1% despite EBITDA margin gain of about 230 bps; watch depreciation and Ind AS effects from larger stores.
Volume growth of about 7-8% lags 13% area growth; management guides for a pickup only in Q3 with Diwali in November.
Festive timing shift (Raksha Bandhan late August) could weigh on Q2 SSG; management declined to comment on the current quarter.
Cotton and raw material cost pressure; management expects prices to correct but gave no basis, and pass-through is assumed to hold.
Franchise store count down from 178 (FY23) to 130 and falling, which slows the asset-light model.
Online share fell to 5% in Q1 during a software integration; the 8% FY27 target depends on this migration.
Working capital cycle guided at 100-105 days; inventory ageing needs monitoring.
Management was not forthcoming on the INR15 crore receivable beyond a February repayment date, and call quality limited several questions.

533269|2026-03.headline: VA Tech Wabag FY26: revenue up ~20%, PAT up 26%, order book INR 17,200 crore (over 4x revenue), net cash ~INR 950 crore.
533269|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue growth of about 20% year-over-year and PAT growth of 26%, with EBITDA margin at 13.3% and ROCE near 20%. Order intake was about INR 7,500 crore versus about INR 5,700 crore last year, taking the order book to INR 17,200 crore, up 26% YoY. Net cash (ex-HAM investment) was about INR 950 crore, up 35% from INR 700 crore, and the company has been net cash positive for 13 consecutive quarters. Management reiterated the 15-20% growth and 13-15% EBITDA guardrails, with a new five-year strategy to be published later in the year. Q&A focused on Middle East pipeline (Kuwait and Saudi orders expected), quarterly India-cluster profitability, lumpy EPC revenue, and the municipal platform and HAM plans.

segments.name: EPC vs O&M revenue mix
segments.commentary: EPC about 83% and O&M about 17% of revenue. O&M is about 40% of order backlog (~INR 6,500 crore), with contracts of 5-20 years; target is to lift O&M to 20% of the mix over 3-5 years.

segments.name: Municipal vs Industrial revenue mix
segments.commentary: Municipal about 80% and industrial about 20% of revenue. Management is adding industrial and mentioned BPCL, Reliance and Aramco-linked pursuits.

segments.name: India vs ROW
segments.commentary: Revenue split about 50:50 India and rest-of-world. Order backlog split about 58-60% India and 40-42% ROW.

segments.name: India cluster
segments.commentary: Key projects include Chennai 45 MLD TTRO (rehab plus O&M, INR 1,000+ crore), Chennai ADB-funded ring main, Kodungaiyur reuse O&M, Perur desalination (Southeast Asia's largest per management), Bangladesh and Nepal projects. Digha-Kankarbagh STP won GWI best wastewater project. Quarterly Indian profit fell from about INR 127 crore to INR 60 crore per the questioner; management said to judge on blended multi-year margins.

segments.name: Middle East and Africa cluster
segments.commentary: Management calls MEA the growth engine; Yanbu desalination mega order won. Al-Haer 200 MLD STP is 83% physically complete. Kuwait order expected to be signed soon (management guided to this quarter); Saudi order may slip to next quarter. Namibia and Senegal in execution; Zambia civil works started.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guardrail of 15-20% CAGR and EBITDA margin of 13-15% reiterated; new five-year strategy and guardrails to be published later this year, expected to be better than current guidance.
Order book to remain above 3x revenue (currently over 4x); ROCE expected to cross 20% within a couple of years; O&M target 20% in 3-5 years.

Management expects revenue to rise in coming periods as new India orders (Kodungaiyur, Chennai ring main, BPCL, Reliance, BWSSB, DJB) convert; CFO said next year could be about 35% higher but is lumpy.
Kuwait order expected in the current quarter; Saudi order may go to the next quarter (management best guess).
Municipal platform (HAM-style) and industrial tenders expected to be finalised over the next quarter; no HAM bids confirmed yet.
capex_capacity: Asia's largest desalination plant (Tamil Nadu, 400 MLD per analyst question) expected to be commissioned around this time next year.
Al-Haer 200 MLD STP (Saudi) at 83% physical progress; commissioning expected after construction completion.
Bio-CNG first project signed; expected to supply around 3,500 homes' cooking gas or about 400 vehicles per day; management said revenue is not very large initially, with plans to replicate.
Modular plant design being used to replicate standard modules for faster build; ceramic membranes being pursued over polymeric membranes.
Asset-light model: management says gross and net block are among the lowest in the sector; technology captive (125+ patents), not licensed.
demand_pricing: Middle East: GCC opportunity estimated at about $5 billion per year over 10 years; management cites Saudi Vision 2030, FIFA World Cup 2034, Oman Vision 2040, and Kuwait pre-selection; UAE first order in progress.
Overall addressable market quoted at $75-100 billion over 5-7 years, plus $4-6 billion future energy (solar PV, semiconductors, data centres, green hydrogen) and about $10 billion O&M.
India: $20-25 billion opportunity cited; SAARC $5-10 billion; India treats only about 28% of sewage generated, per management.
Competitive positioning in Middle East: management claims it wins on life-cycle cost (capex plus opex) because it operates the plants it builds; won 3 of last 6 STPs in MEA.
Price variation clauses: present on most large Indian orders with 2.5-3+ year duration, covering only about 70% of cost; generally absent in international contracts.
Management says desalination water costs about 8 paise per litre and reuse about 5-6 paise per litre.

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue and growth shape up for the next five years, and how does WABAG benchmark against the top two players in India and globally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 15-20% growth and 13-15% EBITDA guardrails; margin levers are scale, a higher international mix (currently 50:50), and O&M rising to 20%. A new strategy with updated guardrails will be published later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is WABAG building capability to move into higher-margin equipment products?
qa_highlights.answer: No, the company will not become an equipment maker; it focuses on process solutions, R&D on membranes and crystallisation, and lowest footprint, totex and power use.

qa_highlights.question: Who wins Middle East bids that involve several top competitors: price or technical?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohan Mittal said L1 pricing alone is not rewarded; PPP projects weigh life-cycle cost, and WABAG's edge is operating data, captive technology and end-to-end build-operate capability, claiming margins well above what competitors bid.

qa_highlights.question: What does asset-light mean for an EPC/O&M company?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said assets are people (about 2,000 engineers) and about 125 patents; the company does not own real estate, equipment or manufacturing, so its capital employed is very low relative to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will size constrain growth beyond INR 8,000 crore revenue, and will there be a strategic pivot?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said no diversification outside water is planned; the market is large enough. A small bolt-on acquisition for technology was confirmed as a possibility ('definitely, short answer is yes').

qa_highlights.question: Status of Kuwait and Saudi orders and FY27 order inflow expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Preferred bidder for both per public tender openings; Kuwait expected in the current quarter, Saudi possibly next quarter. No explicit FY27 order target given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Indian cluster profit fall and revenue look flat year on year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said quarterly segment profit should be judged on blended multi-year margins because projects are in different phases and cost pools are shared with MEA; India backlog is 58% of total and new orders (Kodungaiyur, ring main, BPCL, Reliance, BWSSB, DJB) will drive revenue.

risks_watch: Gulf geopolitical conflict affecting operations and sentiment; management flagged it as a headwind, and Eid timing caused delays in bid decisions.
Quarterly profitability is lumpy: the India cluster's quarterly profit dropped to about INR 60 crore per the questioner, and management asked investors to judge on multi-year blended margins.
Price variation clauses cover only about 70% of costs in large Indian orders and are generally absent in international contracts, leaving cost-inflation exposure.
Order book is more than 4x revenue but the Kuwait and Saudi awards are not yet signed; timing could slip.
Gross cash cited at about INR 10,500 crore on the call conflicts with the INR 950 crore net cash and debt figures stated; verify against the audited balance sheet.
Municipal platform and HAM-style bidding not yet confirmed; timing dependent on next quarter.
Mixed statements on quarterly reporting: investor requested quarterly (Q4) numbers in press releases; management did not commit.

More cautious and deflecting on quarterly segment margins, Indian cluster profitability and exact order timing, which management tied to Gulf conditions and Eid.

533269|2026-06.headline: VA Tech Wabag Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.8% YoY to INR 887 crore, PAT up ~37% to INR 90 crore, order backlog record INR 19,400 crore.
533269|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR 887 crore (+20.8% YoY), EBITDA INR 116 crore (+21.7%, margin just over 13%) and PAT INR 90 crore (+~37%, 10.2% margin). Order intake exceeded INR 3,400 crore, 77% from international markets, taking the order book to a record INR 19,400 crore (over 4x revenue). Management said the company stayed net cash positive for the 14th consecutive quarter, and new wins included a 60 MIGD Kuwait desal plant and the third phase of Ajman STP in the UAE. Management guided 15-20% revenue growth for the year and reiterated a 13-15% medium-term EBITDA margin band, with FY27 more likely at 13-14%.

segments.name: Revenue mix by business
segments.commentary: EPC 82% and O&M 18% of revenue. India 48%, overseas 52%.

segments.name: Order intake
segments.commentary: Q1 order intake over INR 3,400 crore: EPC ~INR 2,960 crore, O&M ~INR 470 crore. International 77%, India 23%.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: Record INR 19,400 crore: 66% EPC, 34% O&M; roughly balanced India vs international. Management put Middle East at about 35-40% of backlog. Two framework orders (~INR 600 crore) were removed as not yet effective.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M revenue grew about 7% YoY in the quarter. Management said it will grow in line with project completions moving into O&M phase (Ghaziabad, Digha-Kankarbagh completed; Perur next year).

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guided at 15-20% for the year; management said it expects to meet it and to deliver above guidance.
EBITDA margin: medium-term blended band 13-15%; FY27 expected at 13-14%, with a stated aspiration of 15% by year end.
Working capital guided to stay in the 100-110 day range despite growth; long-term Wriddhi 2.0 strategy to be presented at the May FY27 investor meet.
Backlog expected to execute over about 36 months; international EPC cycles 24-30 months, India about 36 months.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: management said no capex is needed to take orders and there are no capacity constraints.
Perur desal project (Chennai, JICA-funded): about 75% complete, 1 lakh cubic metres of concreting done, marine works finished; commissioning over the next few quarters.
Kodungaiyur: agreement signed, DPR submitted to the PE; refurbishment (1.5 years) to start any time, followed by 18.5 years of operation.
Kuwait 60 MIGD SWRO (with HEISCO) and Kutaisi (Georgia) project started; Ajman STP phase 3 is a design-build sewage biorefinery.
demand_pricing: Order intake was dominated by international wins: Kuwait desal (first project there), Ajman STP phase 3 in UAE, Vienna Water Works high-end drinking water, plus repeat Indian orders in Bengaluru and Delhi (Byramangala, Bellandur, Mitraon/DJB).
Bid pipeline: management cited about USD 2-3 billion across MEA and India (about INR 20,000-25,000 crore), with India about USD 1-1.5 billion. No order inflow target was given.
Management said the Middle East conflict has had no material impact on projects; it has written force majeure letters to customers covering price and time impacts.
Domestic traction is returning in industrial and municipal segments; management still sees larger deal sizes overseas.
Industrial share of backlog is about 12-13%, with an aim of 20-25% over time; traditional industrial is ~90% oil and gas.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall YoY, and were there one-off provisions in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin differences to project mix (more EPC vs EP). It said other expenses included standard provisions for delay or anticipated default under a tighter policy, which can be reversed on collection. No one-off was described.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share-of-profit from associates (~INR 5.5 crore) and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: It is mainly from HAM projects that moved from construction to O&M. Management said it includes construction-phase risk releases, so it may not recur at the same level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the forex gain operational and how does it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said forex gains arise from transactions (invoices, collections, payments) and are treated as operational; translation gains go through reserves. It said it has a natural hedge and uses PCFC for residual exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the order backlog execute faster outside India?
qa_highlights.answer: International EPC cycles are 24-30 months versus about 36 months in India; the backlog is expected to execute over about 36 months overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is sub-judice, the Supreme Court verdict is in its favour, and it would not give a timeline.

risks_watch: Forex gains formed a significant part of Q1 profit; management says they are operational, but the standalone operating margin excluding forex fell from 15.8% to 8.9% (as cited by an analyst).
Middle East geopolitical exposure: 35-40% of backlog is in the Middle East; execution risk around logistics, imports and prices, with force majeure notices issued.
Rising provisions for delays or defaults in other expenses under the new, more stringent policy.
O&M growth slowed to about 7% YoY; recurring revenue growth depends on project completions moving into O&M.
TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) still in arbitration with no timeline; Kodungaiyur refurbishment start awaits PE approval.

533269|2026-09.headline: VA Tech Wabag Q2 FY27 revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore and PAT over INR 100 crore; order book hit a record INR 20,207 crore.

H1 consolidated revenue rose 20.3% to INR 1,887 crore, EBITDA rose about 21% to INR 261 crore, and PAT rose almost 30% to INR 195 crore. Order book closed H1 at a record INR 20,207 crore on H1 order intake of over INR 5,200 crore, and net cash crossed INR 1,000 crore. Management flagged Middle East shipping and commodity pressures but said these have not yet hit execution timelines or margins.

533274|2026-09.headline: Prestige Q2 FY27 residential sales rose 20% YoY to INR7,225 crore; H1 sales INR13,804 crore; FY27 booking guidance held at INR36,000 crore.
533274|2026-09.overview: Management reported a strong first half of FY27, with Q2 residential sales of INR7,225 crore (up 20% YoY) and Q2 revenue from operations of INR2,222 crore. Q2 PAT was INR256 crore and H1 PAT INR527 crore. Collections were INR5,294 crore in Q2 and INR10,096 crore in H1. The CPP Investments deal for the hospitality platform received its first INR1,500 crore tranche in October 2026, and management reiterated FY27 booking guidance of INR36,000 crore alongside a launch pipeline of over INR45,000 crore for the next two years.

segments.commentary: Q2 sales of 5.84 million sq ft and 3,910 units; H1 sales of 11.88 million sq ft and 7,247 units. Bengaluru 41%, Hyderabad 32%, Mumbai 12%, Chennai 8%, others 7%. Completed 4.27 million sq ft in Q2, taking H1 completions to 5 million sq ft.

segments.commentary: Leased 1.7 million sq ft in H1; exit rental INR884 crore as of September 2026. Commenced construction on three commercial projects (2 million sq ft) in Chennai and Kochi; completed Prestige Trade Center, Delhi Aerocity (800,000 sq ft).

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Q2 gross turnover INR721 crore (+10% YoY), footfall 5.2 million, occupancy 99%, exit rental INR278 crore. Construction started on Forum One OMR, Chennai (1.39 million sq ft).

segments.commentary: H1 occupancy 70%, average room rate INR15,143. Started JW Marriott Sakleshpur and Moxy One OMR Chennai (313 keys, 0.77 million sq ft). CPP Investments committed INR3,000 crore for about 20% of Prestige Hospitality Ventures; INR1,500 crore tranche received in October 2026.

533282|2026-03.headline: Gravita Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR 1,172.76 crore, but adjusted EBITDA grew only 4% to INR 112.91 crore; RML copper acquisition adds a new segment.
533282|2026-03.overview: Gravita reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR 1,172.76 crore (+13% YoY, +15% QoQ), adjusted EBITDA of INR 112.91 crore (+4% YoY, 9.63% margin) and PAT of INR 91.88 crore. For FY26, revenue was INR 4,265 crore (+10%), adjusted EBITDA INR 452.48 crore (+12%, 10.6% margin) and PAT INR 378.80 crore (+21%). Management attributed the weaker EBITDA to West Asia disruption cutting value-added sales to the Middle East (10-12% of sales) and higher inbound logistics costs. The company closed the Rashtriya Metal Industries (RML) copper acquisition in March 2026 and raised its FY26-FY29 capex plan to INR 1,700 crore.

Aluminium volumes fell due to lack of MCX hedging and selective sales; management says volumes will recover once hedging is live.

Management expects the formalisation of informal EPR/scrap supply to speed up through the government EPR exchange (MSTC), a CPCB audit framework, and a proposed reverse-charge mechanism/TDS on battery scrap.

qa_highlights.answer: Copper contributed only a minimal amount in Q4 because it was acquired in March. The drop was from lost Middle East value-added sales and higher inbound logistics and material costs; Q1 impact is expected to persist in the short term.

qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is 90 days in FY26 and guided at 85-90 days; copper is mostly imported. Working-capital debt is expected to peak at INR 800-900 crore once copper starts, up from net debt of about INR 118 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: RML EBITDA is about INR 45,000/MT, rising to INR 65,000-70,000 with backward integration; management says consolidated copper ROCE should be 20%+. Copper capacity is 100,000 tonnes in FY29.

qa_highlights.answer: Lead INR 19-20/kg, copper INR 45/kg rising to INR 60-65/kg after recycling, rubber INR 7-8/kg; aluminium INR 14-15/kg and plastic INR 10-12/kg.

Net interest margin for the year was 2.55%, and management guided it to 2.65-2.70% by FY27 end. qa_highlights.question: Why did the bank's QoQ business and advances growth look subdued in Q1 compared with peers?

qa_highlights.question: Why did net profit fall QoQ, and why did provisions rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the extra provisions (Rs 123.5 crore vs Rs 20 crore in Q4) were proactive ECL build-up, not asset quality deterioration. About Rs 150 crore was ECL provision this quarter, and PCR rose to 92.33%.

qa_highlights.question: Which FY27 ratios are being targeted?

qa_highlights.question: What is the net worth change, and what drove it?

qa_highlights.question: What is the FCNR(B) and overseas borrowing opportunity?

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan trajectory and co-lending mix?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 provisioning is ECL vs normal NPA provisions, and is the credit cost guidance of below 1% realistic?

533295|2026-09.headline: Punjab & Sind Bank Q2 FY27: business up 15.73% to Rs.2,79,231 crore, advances up 19.28%, net profit up nearly 40% to Rs.412 crore.
533295|2026-09.overview: Management reported business growth of 15.73% to Rs.2,79,231 crore, with deposits up 12.97% to Rs.1,53,312 crore and advances up 19.28% to Rs.1,25,919 crore. Operating profit rose 22% YoY to Rs.617 crore and net profit rose nearly 40% to Rs.412 crore, helped by 23.6% growth in core fee income and net interest income up 22%. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.09% and net NPA at 0.61%. Management said treasury performance was muted due to hardening yields and geopolitical factors, and flagged slower co-lending and a planned Rs.7,000 crore capital raise via QIP.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked what drives the upward guidance and what initiatives support credit growth, RAM breakup, and treasury outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Management retained business guidance and said NPA targets could be exceeded; cited digital platforms (12 products on a single QR code), HR transformation, and branch expansion. Treasury is constrained, but management expects margins to improve with rate hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about corporate book visibility, digital spend, and supply chain and co-lending.
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate pipeline of about Rs.20,000 crore built over the last year or two; supply chain system is live with two to three corporates; co-lending has slowed pending RBI-compliant integration, expected in one to two months. Specific digital and HR spend figures were not given.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the chatter on PSB consolidation and the high-level banking reform committee.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had no information on consolidation and that the committee had not yet been formed as far as the bank understood; the government decides.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the ECL transition impact and steady-state credit cost from FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: CRO said the additional impact is about 5% of net worth (around Rs.700 crore), including HTM MTM, with a glide path making CRAR impact negligible; steady-state provisioning of 0.5%-0.6%. SMA 1+2 standard-asset credit cost was not available and will be shared separately.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether the bank will change the corporate vs RAM mix and whether it is active in mid-sized corporates.
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy is to keep increasing RAM share to 65% by March 2027 and about 70% by March 2028; corporate churn continues on pricing, and MSMEs will be supported if pricing is competitive.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about capital raising plans given ECL impact and CD ratio.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said optimum CD ratio of 82%-83% is achievable; Rs.7,000 crore raised for capital, approvals obtained, and QIP is the preferred route, timing subject to market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the TWO book, recovery, technology roadmap, and DPDP/cyber readiness.
qa_highlights.answer: TWO book about Rs.7,344 crore with Rs.247.88 crore recovered so far; recovery tool vendor appointed. Cybersecurity RFP targeted this quarter and Resilience Operations Centre phased by December and March.

533326|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 13.3% to INR1,167 crore, but PAT rose to INR58 crore; INR700 crore contingency provision taken from free reserves.
533326|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR1,167 crore (down 13.3% YoY), with EBITDA of about INR116 crore (~10% margin) and PAT of INR58 crore (5% margin, up 206 bps YoY). FY26 revenue fell 14% to INR4,377 crore, EBITDA was INR450 crore (10.2% margin) and PAT INR194 crore (4.4%). The company created a INR700 crore contingency provision charged to free reserves, which led to a qualified auditor report; management says it has no cash impact. Management also outlined a "Texmaco 2.0" Vision 2030 plan targeting 2x top line and mid-teen-plus EBITDA margins, and disclosed a large South Africa wagon and locomotive order (about INR4,000 crore) with delivery by FY28.

FY26 lower than record prior year

533326|2026-06.headline: Texmaco Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR753 crore but PAT rose 85.9% YoY to INR52 crore; order book INR9,923 crore.

Management said the order book stood at INR9,923 crore at June 30, 2026, with private and export orders at 96.4% of freight car orders in Q1 FY27. Strategic updates covered the leasing JV with Trinity (Texmaco stake to fall from 50% to 34%), the Wabtec air brake JV, a South Africa order of about INR4,100 crore, and a 2030 vision of doubling the top line.

segments.commentary: Revenue lower YoY; EBIT margin turned positive at 1.4% versus an EBIT loss in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Foundry
segments.commentary: Production of 5,148 tonnes in the quarter.

Management expects no Indian Railways wagon tender near term; it expects orders to come from private and export customers.

533333|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 162% to INR314 crore and PAT 118% to INR44 crore, helped by the CrudeChem (CCT) acquisition.
533333|2026-03.overview: Fineotex reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR314 crore, up 162% YoY, with PAT of INR44 crore versus INR20 crore a year earlier, driven by the newly acquired US oilfield chemicals business CrudeChem Technologies Group (CCT). International revenue rose to 70% of the mix and ROIC was stated at 31%. Management said Q4 is the base for future growth, is doubling CCT's manufacturing capacity, and targets a $200 million CCT revenue run-rate before 2028 and a blended EBITDA of 18-20%. Non-CCT textile volumes were said to be recovering, with textile specialty up about 8% YoY in Q4.

segments.commentary: Textile share of total revenue fell to about 35-36%, though textile revenue grew in value. Textile specialty volumes were up about 8% YoY in Q4 and about 15% in volume per a later clarification.

segments.commentary: No segment-specific figures were given on the call; management said other industries grew faster than textile.

533333|2026-06.headline: Fineotex Q1 FY27 total income rose 165% YoY to INR 386.72 crore, with EBITDA of INR 59.14 crore at a 15.70% margin, driven by the US CrudeChem consolidation.
533333|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 consolidated total income was INR 386.72 crore against INR 146.62 crore a year earlier, mainly from a full quarter of the US operations (CrudeChem Technologies Group, CCTL). EBITDA rose 134.7% YoY to INR 59.14 crore, with margin at 15.70% versus 13.93% in the prior quarter, and PAT grew 92.67% to INR 48.21 crore. The Texas plant capacity was expanded to about 148,000 MTPA, with utilisation stated at about 63%. Management declined to give a fixed margin guidance, while reiterating USD 100 million (FY27) and USD 200 million (FY28) targets for the oil and gas segment.

segments.name: Oil and gas specialty chemicals (CCTL, US)
segments.commentary: Management said about 65% of revenue and about 55% of volume come from oil and gas, roughly INR 250 crore in the quarter. The Texas plant is now about 148,000 MTPA, and management said it is utilised at about 63%.

segments.name: Textile specialty chemicals (India, standalone business)
segments.commentary: Management said the base business is about INR 132 crore after deducting CCTL from consolidated revenue, against INR 137 crore in Q1 FY26, a 1-2% dip that it attributed to monsoon seasonality and competition. Management said pricing was passed on and that the textile business is flattish.

guidance_outlook: Oil and gas segment targets of USD 100 million in FY27 and USD 200 million in FY28, which management said are driven by order book and customer expectations rather than crude prices. Management said it expects the target to be reached by December 2028.
Management said it expects the Texas plant to be fully utilised within the coming few quarters, with scope to add a second shift.
Management said it has no fixed consolidated EBITDA margin guidance. It reiterated the aspiration of 18% margin but did not commit to it.
Management said margins are sustainable, with pass-through of raw material and freight costs through war surcharges in the US.
capex_capacity: Texas manufacturing capacity was expanded to about 148,000 MTPA (from about 80,000 MTPA), taking group capacity to about 268,000 MTPA, per an analyst's figure that management did not dispute.
Texas utilisation is about 63%, with management saying another 30-40% could be added on the existing plant.
Management said further capex needed to support growth is about USD 1-2 million, which it does not regard as material.
A second shift is available on the Texas plant, and new high-performance machinery was installed in the expansion.
The new Indian plant at FSPL Specialties, commissioned in August 2025, operates under Section 115BAB at a 15% tax rate.
demand_pricing: Management said it passes on raw material and freight cost increases through a US war surcharge, and that margins are sustainable even if prices fall.
Management said the order book for CCTL is not a fixed tender-based order book. It said demand is perennial once wells are producing, with short weather-related interruptions.
Management said it has started selling to Canada and has won a Saudi business order. It also said a customer has an USD 8 billion Aramco order where Fineotex's specialty package is used.
Management said textile demand is supported by Indian export recovery, with UK, EU and US trade deals improving sentiment.
Management said it competes with US specialty chemical majors on price, and that its performance is equivalent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the top-line and bottom-line growth outlook from the Texas capacity addition, and are there any inorganic targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Texas is at about 63% utilisation, with room to add 30-40%. It said it is evaluating acquisitions with a focus on synergy and value, and will disclose to exchanges once an advanced stage is reached.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD 200 million FY28 oil and gas target dependent on crude prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target depends on order book and customer relationships, not crude price. It said activity continues even at USD 60, and that crude is currently around USD 90-100.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone revenue and EBITDA decline YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the standalone figures exclude FSPL Specialties, the new Indian plant. Combined with FSPL, the dip is not visible, and the difference is an accounting presentation matter.

qa_highlights.question: What is CCTL's ROCE and does it need more capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said oil and gas is not capex-intensive and ROCE is among the best in the industry. Growth needs about USD 1-2 million of capex, and the business runs on one shift today.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15.7% margin sustainable, and can the business reach the 18% level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not guide to a fixed blended margin and that the blended margin is in the 13-14% range or better for CCTL. It said it aspires to better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the CCTL forex gain or loss not clear?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX gains or losses are reported separately as a foreign exchange item, not as other income, and that natural hedging exists through USD raw material purchases. It said the impact is small, around INR 1-2 crore.

Geopolitical volatility and freight and raw material price movements, with management saying pricing changes are unpredictable.

533339|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell 45.2% YoY to Rs.178.1 crore, with operational EBITDA margin at 28.6%; management reaffirms Rs.4,000 crore cumulative revenue for FY27-28.
533339|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs.178.1 crore, flat sequentially but down 45.2% YoY, which management attributed to order-inflow timing with most order book slated for FY27. Management focused its prepared remarks on anti-drone (hard-kill) systems, simulators, and new products launched at Prayagraj, including the HyperStrike interceptor drone and Vrishabh UGV.

533339|2026-06.headline: Zen Technologies Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to Rs.141.6 Cr (vs Rs.158.2 Cr YoY) and operational EBITDA margin to 27.3%, with management guiding to mid-30s for FY27.

Reported PAT was Rs.34.5 Cr after a Rs.3.4 Cr exceptional fire-related loss at a subsidiary; adjusted PAT is about Rs.37 Cr (26.1% margin). Order book stood at Rs.1,239 Cr, with a Rs.177.5 Cr Ministry of Defence simulator order received after quarter end; the group remains debt free with about Rs.1,217 Cr cash.

segments.name: Anti-drone / counter-drone systems
segments.commentary: Demand is tender-gated: management says no anti-drone or simulator tenders have been floated recently, though a fast-track process is expected to bring them. Management cited about Rs.800 Cr of anti-drone orders after Operation Sindoor and expects anti-drone opportunities of at least Rs.2,000 Cr.

segments.commentary: Capacity expanded to about 300,000 units. Management said drone segment orders have slowed; it estimates Rs.300 Cr potential revenue if orders at Rs.10,000 per unit materialise, with about 50% of enquiries from overseas.

segments.name: Robotics / new products
segments.commentary: Vrishabh unmanned ground vehicle has completed internal trials; customer trials pending. Management expects robotics, autonomous vehicles and related products to take at least two to three years to mature.

533344|2026-03.headline: PFS FY26 PAT rose to INR319 crores from INR217 crores, while Q4 sanctions jumped to INR1,004 crores and gross Stage III fell 73% to INR190 crores.
533344|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed a sharp pickup in sanctions (INR3,448 crores, over 4x FY25) and disbursements (INR1,235 crores, up 35%), with PAT up about 47% to INR319 crores. Asset quality improved materially: gross Stage III fell to INR190 crores and net Stage III to INR47 crores, with provision coverage on Stage III at 75%. AUM moderated to INR3,292 crores as low-yield legacy loans prepaid (INR1,105 crores of unscheduled prepayments), and Q4 profitability softened with RoNW at 6.24% and portfolio yield at 10.29%. Leadership change (MD and CEO R. Balaji resigned, effective after 30 June) and the absence of a dividend dominated investor questions.

segments.name: Infrastructure finance (renewable, transmission, DISCOM, oil and gas, roads, CBG, data centre)
segments.commentary: All FY26 disbursements went to private corporate borrowers; sanctions were mainly private, with one or two utility sanctions where returns are acceptable. Structured finance (value chain) is being built to lift yield over the medium term.

segments.name: Stage III / legacy resolution
segments.commentary: Major part of the INR190 crores gross Stage III is Danu Wind Parks, referred to NCLT; promoters have offered an OTS that will be considered on merits. About 73% of gross Stage III accounts by value transitioned out during the year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects at least 30% to 50% YoY AUM growth (disbursements minus repayments), with quality prioritised over quantity.
About INR2,000 crores of sanctioned amount is undisbursed; roughly INR1,500 crores expected in the next two quarters, with major portion in Q2 FY27.
FY27 disbursement target of INR4,000 crores is not yet set; budget is awaiting approval and is framed on yield and RoA, not volume.
Cost of funds expected to fall as fresh borrowings replace older, higher-cost debt; PFS base rate was cut by 60 bps in the last quarter.
No dividend declared; the board will review it next quarter. Management acknowledged a suggestion for a dividend at the annual meeting.
capex_capacity: Sanctions-to-disbursement gap is structural: infrastructure projects run 6 months to 3.5 years, so disbursement follows construction progress.
Liquidity of about INR1,800 crores on balance sheet; borrowing deferred until required, with ALCO matching disbursement needs.
Average tenure of new project loans cited at 5 to 7 years.
Prepayments of INR1,105 crores and total repayments of INR1,441 crores in FY26; prepayments were low-yield legacy loans and are not predictable.
demand_pricing: Management says new disbursements are at higher yields than prepaid loans, so portfolio yield is expected to improve.
Q4 FY26 portfolio yield fell to 10.29% from 11.27%, which management attributed to portfolio dynamics and calibrated growth.
Sole and multiple lending structures are being prioritised over consortium lending, though PFS also participates in consortium and co-lending on a case-by-case basis.
Net NPA stated at 1.49%, with gross NPA INR190 crores and net NPA INR47 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gap between sanctions (about INR3,500 crores) and disbursements (about INR1,200 crores) so large?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said infrastructure projects are disbursed as construction progresses over 1 to 3 years, so sanctions convert to disbursement later. Past lack of a sanctioned pipeline also explains the current low disbursement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did R. Balaji resign, and is the FY27 disbursement vision still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: The company said the resignation was for personal reasons already disclosed; the MD and CEO remains until 30 June and a replacement process has started. The FY27 target of about INR4,000 crores was not committed and is pending budget approval.

qa_highlights.question: Why is borrowing cost high at around 9.5%, and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost of borrowing is below 9.5%, that the treasury is pressing lenders for spread cuts, and that the base rate was cut 60 bps. Cost of funds should fall as new, cheaper borrowings replace older debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company declare a dividend, and what is the NTPC promoter impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend has not been declared; the board will review it next quarter. Management said no formal intimation on the NTPC shareholding change has been received and no adverse impact is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company holding cash rather than disbursing, and is this a fundraising issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds about INR1,800 crores of liquidity, will borrow only when needed to match asset-liability timing, and has about INR2,000 crores of pipeline to disburse over the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the INR190 crores gross Stage III accounts, and what is the status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kalur Srinivas said the major portion is Danu Wind Parks, referred to NCLT, with the promoters having offered an OTS that will be considered on merits; updates will be given to exchanges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for AUM growth over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to at least 30% to 50% YoY AUM growth, stating that AUM means disbursements minus repayments, and said no fresh slippage has occurred in the last eight years of disbursements.

533344|2026-06.headline: PFS Q1 FY27 disbursements fell to INR 117 crores with PAT of INR 40.24 crores; management says Q2 sanctions exceed INR 1,200 crores in month one.
533344|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a muted quarter for PTC India Financial Services, with disbursements of about INR 117 crores and loan assets of INR 2,946 crores. Profit after tax was INR 40.24 crores on net interest income of INR 48.71 crores, with NIM at 4.46%. Management attributed the weak origination to a leadership transition and to delayed construction at some borrowers, and said it is pausing the FI and SME books to focus on infrastructure lending. Management guided to an AUM of about INR 5,000 crores by end-FY27, though no dividend timing was given. The call was dominated by retail shareholder complaints about performance and dividends.

segments.name: Infrastructure lending
segments.commentary: Named as the core growth engine; management wants a balanced book across private sector and PSU borrowers across large, medium and small tickets. Q2 sanctions in month one were above INR 1,200 crores, described as a 13-quarter high.

segments.name: FI and SME books
segments.commentary: Management is pausing new lending in these books to concentrate on infrastructure financing.

guidance_outlook: AUM target of about INR 5,000 crores by end of FY27, per Director Operations Sanjeev Kumar.

Dividend timing: CEO said he cannot answer on dividends today; asked shareholders to be patient for the next 2-3 quarters.
Borrowing costs: some new sanctions for additional facilities are expected by end of next quarter; management is working to reduce existing borrowing costs and keep future costs low.
capex_capacity: Not applicable; PFS is a lender, and the call gave no capacity or capex metrics.

Management says sufficient liquidity exists in the system, and talks with institutions for new facilities are positive, though no sanctions are yet in hand.

Total income was INR114 crores and PAT INR44 crores, with interest spread up to 1.18%. Gross Stage 3 fell to INR126 crores from INR190 crores, though net Stage 3 rose to about INR105 crores because a Danu Wind Parks account was technically written off and Kundli Manesar slipped to NPA with a INR19 crore provision. Customer mix: about 15 lakh customers lost in sub-INR 30,000 tickets, offset by growth in INR 50,000, 1 lakh and 2 lakh tickets; loans above INR 3 lakh are 32% of the book.
Pricing: rates raised by 0.5-1% on certain loan types in the last quarter; management said yields may move up or down and it did not commit to the current level.
Gold import curbs: management said Muthoot does not finance bullion or coins and sees no direct impact; about 25,000-30,000 tonnes of household gold is held as collateral (as stated).

qa_highlights.question: Is the yield increase inclusive of one-off recoveries and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 one-offs were about INR 85 crore (auction INR 50 crore, ARC INR 35 crore). Q3 included about INR 500 crore of interest recovery from GNPA, which is not in Q4. Management attributed the core increase to pricing on higher-gold-price disbursements and did not commit to sustaining the yield.

qa_highlights.question: Why did stage 2 and stage 3 assets rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly due to RBI-mandated borrower-level (rather than loan-level) classification. Stage 3 percentage is 2.34% vs 3.35% a year earlier. Management said stage 3 LTV including interest is about 57-58%, and that gold loans, not non-gold, drove the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Customer count is down about 2% while acquisition is up; is there high-value customer leakage to competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said losses were concentrated in sub-INR 30,000 tickets (about 5 lakh under INR 10,000 and about 8 lakh in INR 10,000-30,000), offset by higher-ticket additions. It described this as normal churn in a mature portfolio, not competitive loss.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cut rates to win customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has different schemes at 12-23% yields and will step up lower-yield lending when needed, but sees no need now. Median-term ROI guidance of around 3.5% was referenced.

qa_highlights.question: AUM guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone AUM guidance of 15%, given in Q1 as always; to be reviewed after Q1 or Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why set up gold lending in a subsidiary (Muthoot Money) rather than expanding the parent after RBI approval requirements were removed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to explain and said it is a board decision for the subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: How does the new RBI LTV framework affect the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has always followed RBI LTV limits, and the new framework allows up to 85% on EMI products. It is building software and has rolled out some products, with strategy to be reviewed after Q1.

533470|2026-03.headline: Rushil Decor FY26 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR 801 million (9.3% margin) after Q1 fire disruption; Q4 margin recovered to 12.4%.
533470|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: a fire at the Andhra Pradesh MDF facility disrupted Q1 production, and resin/raw material inflation, export logistics issues and Middle East shipping disruption weighed on the year. Consolidated FY26 revenue from operations was INR 8,622 million with EBITDA of INR 801 million (9.3%) and PAT of INR 64 million. Q4 FY26 showed sequential recovery, with revenue of INR 2,309 million (up 6.6% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 286 million (12.4% margin). Management implemented MDF price increases of 15% and Laminate price increases of 10% effective 1 April 2026, mainly to recover cost inflation.

Distribution network: 67 new direct distributors and more than 131 retailers and dealers added in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What will capacity utilisation look like in Q1 FY27 across plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 would be in the range of Q4 FY26 levels; MDF exports are under pressure, so domestic sales are being pushed, and a Jumbo facility machinery upgrade completed in April is ramping up.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue or EBITDA guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric guidance; management instead listed four priorities: 50% value-added share, scaling Jumbo, 90% utilisation and cost optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current net debt and FY27-28 debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt (after cash) went from INR 262 crore (Mar 2025) to INR 254 crore (Mar 2026), including about INR 9 crore euro FX impact; about INR 50 crore scheduled repayment in FY27 and no new debt planned.

qa_highlights.question: Jumbo Laminate realisation and potential revenue at full utilisation?

qa_highlights.question: Is the MDF price hike purely cost recovery or margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Purely cost recovery: chemical costs up about 40%, net about 10% of selling price, so total cost up about 11%; no additional margin is being earned.

qa_highlights.answer: Current MDF EBITDA margin about 8%; target 10-12% through higher value-added mix; value-added share missed target slightly in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Jumbo volume, revenue and margin targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation targeted at 60-65% in FY27 and up to 85% in FY28; Laminate-business EBITDA target 10-12% on average, with wide margin range by SKU.

qa_highlights.question: Industry demand-supply and MDF capacity additions?

qa_highlights.question: How exposed is the book to the West Asia conflict (SME, personal loans, rural, tractor, two-wheeler), and is the 20%+ FY27 AUM growth guidance inclusive of these risks?
qa_highlights.answer: No visible West Asia impact yet on SME, Rural Business Finance, tractor or two-wheeler portfolios; caution on Kharif fertiliser supply and urban unsecured lending. 20%+ AUM growth guidance stands but excludes unforeseen later geopolitical shocks.

qa_highlights.question: What are the near-term and Lakshya 2031 cost ratio expectations, and how was the ECL refresh's contingency buffer treated?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex to book guided at 3.75%-4% over Lakshya, reflecting tech and branch investment. Management said the ₹125 Cr macro-prudential provision was subsumed into the ECL model (Stage 1 and 2), not released, and that it will keep building macro-prudential provisions as needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fee income tepid relative to disbursement growth, and will it grow in line with AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income is about 1.7%-1.9% of assets and is range-bound; liquidity income and negative carry sit in interest cost, not MTM. Management guides to the combined NIMs+Fees range of 10%-10.5% rather than standalone fees.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Stage 1 provision at 80 bps apply to incremental FY27 book, and does it change the FY27 credit cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, new Stage 1 build-up will be provided at 80 bps as a permanent assumption change. Management said the FY27 credit cost outlook of 2%-2.2% is unchanged because lower roll-forwards should more than offset higher provisioning on book growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sub-2% credit cost under Lakshya 2031 driven by product mix or by Cyclops, and when does it arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly Cyclops-driven customer selection, applied first to two-wheeler, tractor and SME. Management is confident of reaching 2% or below sometime in FY28, but could not pinpoint the quarter. Two-wheeler prime share is about 90%, up from 65%, and monthly originations rose from ₹650 Cr to about ₹1,000 Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Are disbursement yields above portfolio yields, and what drives yield improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Disbursement yields are higher than portfolio yields. Personal loan yields are 2%-2.5 pp above the industry salaried average. Two-wheeler industry yields are 16%-18%. Yield improvement is coming from mix shift: home loan to LAP mix moved from about 80/20 to 55/45, with gold, micro-LAP and PL accelerating.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: possible fertiliser supply constraint for Kharif, industrial gas tightness hitting SMEs, and higher oil prices pressuring urban unsecured lending (PL and SME).
El Niño risk to the monsoon and rural yields, with knock-on effects on Rural Business Finance and Farmer Finance.
ECL: Stage 1 provisioning now at 80 bps, with PCR on Stage 3 falling to 68% from 73%; further ECL recalibration possible in September 2026 or March 2027, and overlays remain in Stage 3.
Credit cost path: 2.64% in Q4 FY26 must fall to 2%-2.2% by Q4 FY27; Cyclops benefits are early (10-month window, ~₹3,250 Cr book) and not yet seasoned.
SR and wholesale book: ~₹7,000 Cr (₹4,808 Cr SR plus ₹2,220 Cr wholesale) still to resolve over 3-4 years; SR provision cover at 64%. Resolution gains are excluded from RoA/RoE targets.

Execution: 400-500 gold loan branches and 150-200 micro-loan and micro-LAP branches in FY27 (about 1-1.2 gold branches per day); payments platform due by Q2 FY27; Karnataka-type MFI regulatory shocks remain a tail risk.

533519|2026-06.headline: L&T Finance posted record Q1 FY27 PAT of ₹902 Cr (up 29% YoY) with RoA of 2.48% and credit cost easing to 2.54%.

Retail disbursements were ₹23,852 Cr, up 36% YoY, though management said it deliberately let go of about ₹1,000–1,200 Cr of potential disbursements to protect asset quality. Credit cost moderated 10 bps sequentially to 2.54%, and NIMs + Fees was flat QoQ at 10.47%, with NIM down 24 bps offset by higher fee and other income. Management reiterated Lakshya 2031 targets (RoA 3.0–3.2%, RoE 16–18%, credit cost ≤2% over the period) and set a near-term 2.8% RoA goal for Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What guardrails govern Personal loan growth, and why were SME and Gold disbursements slower?

qa_highlights.question: Is the wholesale GS3 increase a risk to credit cost, and what is the SR/ARC position?

qa_highlights.question: How much AI spend is variable, and what is the opex trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not give the variable AI share on the call and offered to follow up offline. Head-count efficiencies are expected to show in FY29–FY30, with the next two to three quarters not very sharp.

The company now runs two verticals, real estate and financial services, with real estate expected to deliver about 80% of group profit. Management guided real estate profits to at least double in FY27 and triple in FY28, though it declined quarterly guidance. 533552|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 6.3% YoY to INR441.5 crore, with volume up 9%, and EBITDA rose 19.8% to INR55 crore as margin expanded 150 bps to 12.5%, helped by Athleisure mix. 533573|2026-09.headline: Alembic Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36% YoY to INR2,603 crore; FY27 growth guidance raised to 20-25% from mid-teens.
533573|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36% YoY to INR2,603 crore and reported EBITDA grew 78% with margin at 22.2%, up about 520 bps YoY. PAT rose 81% YoY to INR335 crore, with effective tax rate near 24%. US Generics grew 72% YoY, with base portfolio growth of 23% excluding new launches including bosutinib. Management raised FY27 consolidated growth guidance to 20-25% on stronger US and API outlook, and said India branded business should reach market-level growth within two to three quarters.

financial_highlights.change: about +520 bps YoY (from 17%); reported EBITDA +78% YoY
EBITDA margin +255 bps; reported EBITDA +51% YoY

segments.name: India branded business
segments.commentary: Grew 14% YoY in Q2; Human Health returned to double-digit growth at 11%. Specialty portfolio grew about 200 bps ahead of the Indian pharmaceutical market, while acute remains a drag.

segments.name: Animal Health
segments.commentary: Grew 23% YoY in Q2 FY27; management cites a CAGR above 20% over the last 5-7 years.

segments.name: US Generics
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 72% YoY; base business grew 23% excluding new launches including bosutinib. Three launches, five ANDAs filed and one approval in the quarter.

segments.name: US Branded (Alembic Therapeutics)
segments.commentary: Contributed close to 3% of total US revenue in Q2; about 4 products, with Pivya in a J-shaped ramp. Breakeven targeted by end-CY2026 or first half of next year.

segments.name: Ex-US
segments.commentary: Grew 12% YoY; direct presence being strengthened in Europe, LatAm and select ASEAN markets.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Volume-led growth of 39% YoY, including certain CMO deliveries to key customers; FY27 guidance raised to at least high-teens growth.

US business now expected to grow up to 40% YoY for FY27.

India branded expected to grow in line with market and get close to double digits; ex-US expected at mid-teens (both unchanged).

US branded dilution of 150-200 bps to margin on a full-year basis, unchanged; drag expected to end in FY28.

US branded field force at about 30-35 reps versus a target of 40-45; India field force held constant.
Line shutdown in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 for ophthalmics capacity expansion caused a minor blip.

Chronic segment grew across almost all divisions; acute still lagging and expected to take a couple of quarters to recover.
Bosutinib sales well ahead of expectations; US exclusivity ends end-November 2026, after which outcome is uncertain.
Management says crude-driven cost increases were broadly offset by rupee depreciation in Q2.
Freight and logistics costs for India-to-US shipments rose from the March quarter as shipping lines and costs expanded.
Ophthalmics described as a strong franchise where Alembic is among the top 1-2 players; derm is more competitive but high EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Ex-bosutinib, how did US sales perform and was bosutinib above expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Base portfolio grew 23% excluding new launches; bosutinib was far above expectations, and Q1 ex-bosutinib growth was in the mid-20s.

qa_highlights.question: Will India move in line with IPM in H2, and what is the cost and margin outlook including Pivya drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Chronic is outpacing IPM and acute should reach IPM within a couple of quarters. Employee and other costs rose on US branded expansion and freight; H1 EBITDA margin about 22% expected to hold in H2; Pivya/US branded drag guided at 150-200 bps for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin move outside the 70-75% range as India mix improves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects gross margin to stay in the 70-75% range; new-launch mix will influence it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the India business and its profitability as growth recovers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to reach IPM in the next couple of quarters with flat field force, which should lift PCPM and gradually improve margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DifGen deal structure and what does Alembic gain?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a licensing deal across 20-plus products on a profit-share basis; DifGen develops and mostly manufactures, while Alembic handles marketing and front-end. Contributions start from FY28; portfolio covers around $5 billion US reference market.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 US growth outlook and branded breakeven timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY28 US growth of about 10-12% if launches pan out. US branded to break even in the first half of next year; the company has an internal branded target but no guidance yet.

533581|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell 10.1% YoY to INR1,717 crore and EBITDA fell 43% to INR131.5 crore, hit by LPG and truck disruptions and rupee depreciation.
533581|2026-03.overview: PG Electroplast's Q4 FY26 was hurt by an LPG shortage in March that cut RAC production at Supa, a truck shortage that deferred dispatches, and about 20% rupee depreciation against the dollar. Management estimated roughly INR420 crore of revenue loss in the quarter and a PBT impact of about INR120 crore. Full-year revenue rose to INR5,288 crore but PAT fell to INR193.6 crore from INR290.9 crore. Management said channel inventory has normalised after April and May sell-out, and guided FY27 to better-than-industry growth with EBITDA margin recovering towards 8%, while declining to give a numeric FY27 revenue or PAT number.

Refrigerant manufacturing plant in Sri City: commercial production targeted by Q4 FY27, meaningful revenue in FY28, tie-up with an anchor customer in place.

Rotary compressor plant at Supa: machinery ordered, installation from August 2026, operations by Q4 FY27; 2 million compressors in phase 1, expandable to 4 million in phase 2. About 60% localised value-add. Management said no external approval or JV is needed. Full capacity targeted in FY28.

Price hikes of about 10-15% industry-wide from December 2025 to April 2026; PG Electroplast took about 10-12% cumulatively, with a further increase in June quarter. Rupee moved from about INR93 to INR95.5 per dollar; management says exchange-rate movement is the main unpassed cost.
Management said FY26 industry-wide weakness was similar to FY23 and that no top-client-specific deterioration occurred. Top 3 client mix unchanged.
El Nino is forecast to intensify from July with a peak in September, which management said could extend the AC season. RAC penetration is below 10% of households.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margins contract, and did the inventory bought cheaply in December and January help?
qa_highlights.answer: Most cheap inventory was consumed by the December quarter sales of about INR932 crore (vs INR516 crore). Price increases in January-March did not fully pass through rupee depreciation or commodity costs. LPG switchover energy costs were also absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the price hike was passed on, and how will gross margins normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10-12% price increase taken cumulatively. Gross margin % in AC will stay lower in FY27, but gross contribution per piece should return to historical averages.

qa_highlights.question: How much forex loss is in the numbers and where does it sit?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex loss sits in other expenses. Unhedged LC and payables were marked to INR94.8 at March-end, and the rupee has since moved to INR95.5. Hedging of $15-20 million was done around INR93.

qa_highlights.question: Will you give FY27 volume or revenue numbers?

qa_highlights.question: Is the compressor project subject to approvals, and is there a Chinese partner?
qa_highlights.answer: No approval is needed and there is no JV; the company is going on its own, having acquired the technical capability. Customer tie-up and product approval are in progress.

qa_highlights.question: Where does inventory stand and how much will it fall?

533581|2026-06.headline: PG Electroplast Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 35.2% YoY to INR2,034 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.7% amid commodity and rupee pressure.
533581|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue crossed INR2,000 crore for the first time, up 35.2% YoY, with EBITDA up 12.1% to INR156.2 crore and net profit up 12.9% to INR75.3 crore. Growth came from double-digit volume growth plus a similar ASP increase as copper, aluminium and resin costs and rupee depreciation were partly passed through. Gross margin percentage softened QoQ and YoY, which management attributed to pass-through mechanics rather than per-unit erosion. The company reports a net cash position, and the compressor, refrigerator and washing machine capacity build-out is the main medium-term theme.

533655|2026-09.headline: Triveni Turbine Q2 FY27 revenue fell 3% YoY to ₹4.91bn and PAT dropped 41.7% to ₹533mn, while record order booking hit ₹7.64bn (+17.2%).
533655|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations was ₹4.91bn, down 3% YoY, as domestic sales rose 51.8% to ₹3.4bn but exports fell 46.6% to ₹1.51bn. EBITDA margin compressed to 17.5% (vs 26.3% a year earlier) and PAT margin to 10.4%, which management attributed to domestic/export mix, product/aftermarket mix and a loss-making NTPC order. Order booking hit a company record of ₹7.64bn, led by exports (+49%) and product orders (+32.5%), and the closing order book rose 10.5% to ₹24.53bn. Management guided to a sharp margin reversion in H2, with Q4 stronger than Q3, but said FY27 profit growth over FY26 would not be significant.

financial_highlights.change: -46.6% YoY; export share 30% vs 55% in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Product (domestic + export)
segments.commentary: Product order booking grew 32.5% to ₹6.01bn in Q2. Domestic order booking was down 2.5% to ₹3.79bn (H1 down 16%), with market share lower in steel while the market grew.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Q2 aftermarket order booking fell 17.8% and was 21% of orders. H1 aftermarket orders rose 12.3% to ₹13.33bn (29% share), and the closing aftermarket order book more than doubled to ₹6.39bn (26% of book vs 14% a year ago). Q2 aftermarket revenue fell 16.7% to ₹1.48bn.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q2 export order booking grew 49% to 48% of quarterly orders (38% a year ago). H1 export orders rose 51.6% to ₹7.5bn (56% share). Export revenue in H1 fell 24%, with deferred shipments to Middle East customers expected in Q3/Q4.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 margins to revert upward on product mix and export/aftermarket contribution; Q4 expected to be stronger than Q3.
Remaining ~15% of NTPC order billing to be spread equally across Q3 and Q4; NTPC losses already provided for, with possible future claims treated as upside.
FY27 profitability expected to grow over FY26 but not significantly; consolidated PBT margin roughly consistent with last year per management.
H2 FY27 revenue growth indicated at around 25%+ (management's indication on questioner's question).
Management expects order booking growth in Q3 and FY28 visibility to support growth; FY28 described as providing greater growth avenue.
No data center order expected to be lumpy; Q2 booking described as regular, not including large one-offs.
capex_capacity: US gas turbine refurbishment/parts contract via South African subsidiary, with a European partner: potential ₹ equivalent of USD 80-90mn over 4-5 years, with only in-year portion booked annually.
Gas turbine product development (for non-power applications) and small gas turbines planned as multi-year R&D programs; no timelines given beyond 'short' development frames for services.
Advanced platforms with significantly better cost structure to be rolled out, expected to positively affect margins in coming quarters.
Combined cycle steam turbine order for US data center-linked application: 2 x 25 MW steam turbine added to pre-existing gas turbine (about 150 MW combined cycle plant).
demand_pricing: Domestic inquiry book flat vs Q1; US inquiry visibility up substantially (data center, combined cycle, energy storage, carbon capture); Central/South America plateauing; Southeast Asia, Europe and India flat.
Management says competition with largest global steam turbine maker (with Indian operations) is unchanged; pricing in India much lower than global markets.
Export pricing lucrative, with margins significantly higher than domestic.
Middle East enquiries expected to rise as war-related disruption eases; drive turbine enquiries from EPCs expected to finalise in Q4.
Aftermarket cycles: spares 3-4 months, servicing about a quarter, refurbishment 5-12 months (complex projects 3-4 quarters); about 80% of opening order book typically executed in the year.
Commodity price increases pushed up material costs in Q1, expected to normalise by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why are domestic order inflows lower in H1 FY27 versus last year, and which sectors are lagging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the market grew, led by steel, but Triveni's share fell, and domestic booking in Q2 roughly doubled from Q1 as cement and steel order finalisation had been delayed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size and timeline of the gas turbine refurbishment contract and the small gas turbine plans?
qa_highlights.answer: The potential is USD 80-90mn over 4-5 years, through a South African subsidiary with a European partner. The gas turbine product is a multi-year effort aimed at non-power applications.

qa_highlights.question: Were the NTPC order losses already accounted for, and can H2 margins exceed 18-19%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NTPC losses are already provided for, with possible claims later. It said H2 margins should be significantly healthier, but gave no specific percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Is the record ₹7-8bn quarterly order booking a sustainable run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 had no lumpy large orders and that booking responds to market demand, with commodity price increases lifting values; it declined to set a steady-state figure.

qa_highlights.question: How does aftermarket order-to-revenue conversion work, given that order inflows have outpaced revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Refurbishment takes 3-4 quarters for complex projects, while spares and servicing are mostly in-year. Management declined to give a full breakup but said 80% of opening order book usually executes in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US data center combined cycle order a repeat of an expected first data-center order, and how is the US pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q2 order was a combined cycle steam turbine add-on to a gas turbine, with the end user a data center. It said less than 5% of the inquiry book is combined cycle.

NTPC BFW/energy storage order (about 15% of value still to bill) executed at low or negative margins, with a commissioning requirement in Q4.
Middle East and export deferrals tied to freight/transport issues and regional war disruption; H1 export revenue down 24%.

533758|2026-03.headline: APL Apollo Q4 FY26: EBITDA per ton above INR5,500 on lower volumes, while management holds FY27 guidance of 15-20% volume and 20-25% EBITDA growth.
533758|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 volume rose 9% YoY and EBITDA per ton ran above INR5,500, with FY26 ROCE at 37% and free cash flow of INR13 billion. Volumes softened from late February after the Middle East crisis, due to steel and gas shortages, labour shortages and channel destocking, and April was slow at about 2.5 lakh tons. Management prioritised margin over volume and said full-year absolute EBITDA targets are unchanged. Net cash rose to about INR1,510 crore by end-March, aided by inventory reduction and better creditor terms.

financial_highlights.change: Above the INR5,300-5,500 guided in Q3 call

qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Gupta said it is too early to separate destocking from demand slowdown; yearly volume and profitability targets are intact, with focus on margin over volume.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA per ton of INR5,500 be sustained given Patra pressure and Dubai weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited market leadership, product innovation and steel shortage; INR5,000-5,500 is a two-year track record, INR6,000+ is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and capital allocation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex around INR500-600 crore per year; INR1,400-1,500 crore pending for 8 million tons, completed in 2-2.5 years. After about INR500 crore of liabilities are cleared, cash may go to dividend or buyback.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA per ton gap versus value-added mix falling to 25% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Anubhav Gupta said the general-segment spread rose to INR3,500+/ton from about INR2,000 on the brand premium and the January 2025 price hike, plus cost rationalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company gained share in the disruption and how will it use its balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Market share rose to 65% in FY26 from 55%; capex is self-funded, with two East India plants, Malur 2 and more SKU and branding spend.

qa_highlights.question: Is the April/May volume outlook and the gas-supply backup plan reflected in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: April 2.5 lakh tons; May about 3 lakh tons; June about 3.5 lakh tons. March LPG disruption lasted 10-15 days; plants moved to alternate fuels and run at about 90%, and guidance factors this in.

533758|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 volume fell ~20% QoQ to 745,000 tons, but EBITDA per ton held near INR5,500 and management reiterates 20% FY27 absolute EBITDA growth.
533758|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 volume of 745,000 tons was below expectations, down roughly 20% QoQ, driven by the UAE disruption (about 25,000 tons lost QoQ), weak SG Premium volumes against secondary steel, an energy crisis hitting rust-proof pipes and roofing (25,000-30,000 tons), and destocking after steel prices rose. Gross profit per ton rose INR1,000 QoQ as management held prices, and EBITDA per ton was flat at above INR5,500. Management says July volumes were up about 20% MoM at over 300,000 tons, and it reiterated 15-20% volume growth and above 20% absolute EBITDA growth for FY27. Working capital days remain below zero and cash was about INR14 billion at June end versus INR15 billion in March 2026.

segments.name: Apollo branded products
segments.commentary: Management targets EBITDA of INR6,000-7,000/ton for Apollo and roofing products combined; the company is at that range currently. Primary and secondary volumes were hit by high prices and channel destocking.

segments.name: SG Premium
segments.commentary: Priced about 6-7% below APL Apollo brand at around INR58,000/ton; EBITDA spread INR0-1,000/ton depending on micro-market. Volumes fell due to the primary-secondary price gap (INR10-12/kg currently).

segments.name: UAE operations
segments.commentary: Dubai volumes fell to 5,000-6,000 tons/month during the disruption; July output was 10,000-12,000 tons, with a target of 16,000-17,000 tons in August and 24,000-25,000 tons in September. About 70,000 tons of inventory is in transit, but raw material for 70,000 tons is not yet lined up. Management expects UAE EBITDA to reach INR5,000-6,000/ton if ramp-up succeeds.

segments.name: Roofing products
segments.commentary: Hit by the energy crisis in India (25,000-30,000 tons lost). Management says roofing EBITDA is currently INR6,000-7,000/ton, with a roofing line starting in APL adding about 20,000 tons of ramped-up volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guidance of 15-20% reiterated; management says 15% is achievable with confidence and 20% needs tailwinds.
FY27 absolute EBITDA growth of 20% or more; FY27 EBITDA per ton expected in the INR5,000-5,500 range.
