533758|2026-09.headline: APL Apollo Q2 FY27 volume hit 960,000 tons with EBITDA near Rs 6,000/ton; management guides FY27 EBITDA up 20%, with the 15% volume target conditional on Dubai and steel supply.
533758|2026-09.overview: Management called Q2 FY27 its best quarter on volume, EBITDA and net profit, with volume of 960,000 tons despite UAE operations being disrupted, steel shortages in the domestic market and container disruption affecting exports. Growth came from the APL Apollo brand and roofing sheets, where pricing and EBITDA spreads improved, while low-margin SG Premium and export volumes were deliberately not pursued. Management guided FY27 EBITDA growth of about 20% on an absolute basis and said Q2 EBITDA per ton of about Rs 6,000 is sustainable. Working capital days were stated as zero, and cash rose 15% QoQ to Rs 16 billion. Several answers on Dubai, SG Premium and volume guidance were non-committal.

segments.name: APL Apollo brand
segments.commentary: Management says brand products get better pricing and EBITDA spreads; APL Apollo and roofing volume grew about 20% YoY in H1, with double-digit growth expected in H2. Analysts were told the brand targets 15-20% YoY growth.

segments.name: Roofing sheets
segments.commentary: Capacity cited at 7 lakh tons per year (about 175,000 tons per quarter); Q1 volume was about 135,000 tons and the target for the current quarter is 175,000 tons. Mix is 50% housing, 25% commercial/industrial and 25% other industrial; thickness 0.4-3.5 mm; no commission paid to third parties.

segments.name: SG Premium
segments.commentary: Low-margin product; management declined to give volume guidance due to steel shortage and low margin. Management said it can sell about 200,000 tons if steel prices fall and that absolute EBITDA would rise as volume increases.

segments.name: UAE (Dubai) operations
segments.commentary: Volume at about 40% of past levels; current run rate about 100,000 tons per year against about 300,000 tons capacity. Brownfield expansion to about 500,000 tons by March 2027, with EBITDA of Rs 8,000-10,000/ton expected on new mills. Management says no losses there.

segments.name: Defence, aerospace and specialised tubes
segments.commentary: New specialised tube mill can produce up to 250x250 mm with 16 mm thickness; samples sent to agencies, with results expected in 2-3 months. Development items for ISRO and DRDO are in progress.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA growth of about 20% on an absolute basis by March 2027; management says it may beat this if UAE operations recover in H2. Management said absolute EBITDA should cross Rs 2,200 crore this year (one analyst cited Rs 2,200-2,300 crore; Shaleen Kumar's Rs 2,400 crore reference was given by management as possible if Dubai performed).

Apollo brand and roofing volume growth of about 15% for FY27 (about double-digit in H2); management also cited 15-20% YoY growth for these two segments. Company-wide volume guidance not committed due to Dubai and SG Premium uncertainty.
Q3 FY27 EBITDA per ton expected to be above Rs 6,000; October described as good and above guidance.

Management said FY28 EBITDA could reach about Rs 2,500 crore; in response to an analyst's Rs 3,000 crore scenario, management agreed it is achievable if Dubai, domestic steel supply and container freight stabilise. Management said that if it targets Rs 6,000-6,500/ton, it will update guidance after another quarter of evidence.
Capex target of 7 million tons greenfield plus brownfield capacity and 1 million tons de-bottlenecking within two years. Capex outflow in H2 expected to be about Rs 200 crore.
Net cash of about Rs 1,600 crore expected to rise to about Rs 2,300 crore; Rs 200-300 crore of this is earmarked for capex, and management will decide the use of the remainder later.

Greenfield additions described as small, limiting fixed-cost impact; brownfield expansion said not to hurt existing fixed costs materially.

Management said steel plant shutdowns are causing shortages, with November also weak and volumes expected to recover to about 400,000 tons per month from December.

Management said Q2 margin expansion came from three sources: exiting non-profitable volumes, roofing capacity additions and cost/innovation. It declined to give product-level EBITDA; the disclosure has been discontinued.
Exports affected by very high container freight; UAE exports blocked.

533761|2026-03.headline: GPT Infra FY26 consolidated revenue rose 8.6% to INR1,290 crores, below guidance, while consolidated EBITDA grew 28.5% to INR174.2 crores; FY27 revenue growth guided at 27-30%.
533761|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 1.3% YoY to INR373.9 crores, while consolidated revenue grew 8.9% to INR414.7 crores; management attributed the March shortfall to West Bengal elections and labour migration. Margins improved, with standalone Q4 EBITDA up 27% to INR53 crores at 14% margin and consolidated Q4 EBITDA up 53% to INR59.2 crores, helped by the Ghana factory. The Alcon signalling EPC acquisition (INR151.83 crores cash) closed in the quarter and is being merged into GPT Infra with an appointed date of April 1, 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 27-30%, order inflow of about INR3,000 crores and consolidated EBITDA margin of around 14%.

segments.name: Concrete sleepers
segments.commentary: Management said the segment was profitable in FY26 on domestic demand and African operations. Q4 was loss-making in South Africa, Namibia and Ghana, which management attributed mainly to currency mark-to-market effects; Ghana production has started.

segments.name: Signalling (Alcon, acquired)
segments.commentary: Margin of about 20% vs 13-14% for traditional infra; FY27 revenue expected at INR120-130 crores. Order book is about INR90-100 crores; FY27 order inflow expected at INR150-200 crores against about INR500 crores of bids.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract assets rise from INR336 crores to about INR514 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60-65 crores is from Alcon (retention, unbilled revenue, escalation), with the rest from EPC milestone-based billing; contract assets are typically 6-8 months old and are targeted to fall to 3-4 months of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the QIP proceeds go, given limited debt reduction?

qa_highlights.question: Did West Bengal elections cause the revenue guidance miss, and does Alcon's INR140 crores contribute?

qa_highlights.question: Is labour back and is there execution risk to FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: April was again subdued by elections, but May execution is strong and labour is back on site; new contracts won in December and January are expected to contribute heavily in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material inflation from the war affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts carry escalation formulas; NHAI now pays escalation monthly, so a lag is possible, but management expects full-year margins to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and is Alcon consolidated separately?

533761|2026-06.headline: GPT Infra Q1 FY27 standalone revenue fell 9% to INR282 crores on West Bengal labour disruption, while consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 15.7% on Alcon signalling.

Consolidated revenue fell 3.4% to INR302 crores, but consolidated EBITDA rose 28.4% to INR47.5 crores (15.7% margin), helped by the Alcon signalling business and African operations. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of about 30% and raised its FY27 EBITDA margin expectation to 14-15%, with 13-14% as the long-term range. Order book stood at INR4,303 crores and Q1 order inflow was only about INR130 crores against a INR3,000 crore annual target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q1 standalone execution slip and when does it recover?

533761|2026-09.headline: GPT Infra Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 5% to INR291 crores and EBITDA margin hit 14.2%; management now guides FY27 revenue of INR1,600 crores plus.

533941|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 63% YoY to Rs 78 crore and FY26 revenue reached Rs 255 crore (+58%), with PAT of Rs 19 crore.
533941|2026-03.overview: Thomas Scott reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 78 crore (+63% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 11 crore (14.14% margin) and PAT of Rs 6 crore (7.71% margin), its 10th consecutive quarter of revenue growth. For FY26, revenue was Rs 255 crore (+58%), EBITDA Rs 33 crore (13.1% margin, +105 bps) and PAT Rs 19 crore (+51%). Management said some own-brand sales shifted to outright wholesale sales to marketplace distributors at 30-40% below retail, lowering reported revenue per unit while EBITDA margin was said to be neutral. Working capital, short-term borrowings and receivables drew the most scrutiny, with management attributing much of the stretch to a fire-related inventory loss and March-clustered sales.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Womenswear has early traction and footwear entered in Q4 FY26 via manufacturing partners, with premium licensed brands (Rs 2,500-3,000 price points) expanding, though no revenue split is disclosed.

533941|2026-06.headline: Thomas Scott Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 66 crore and EBITDA margin was 13.07%, as management chose to hold prices over discounting.
533941|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 66 crore (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR 9 crore (+43% YoY, margin 13.07%) and PAT about INR 5 crore (+54% YoY, margin 8.21%). Management said subdued price elasticity led it to protect realisations and shift spend from discounts to performance marketing, which it said lifted gross margins. Wholesale-style aggregator sales now make up about 40% of Thomas Scott brand revenue. Finance costs rose sharply on working capital tied to a fire-related insurance claim that is still pending.

segments.name: Thomas Scott (own brand)
segments.commentary: Revenue close to INR 25 crore, up 34% YoY, driven by online-first approach, rapid launches and data-led merchandising. About 40% of brand revenue came via aggregator bulk orders booked at wholesale prices under marketplace channel.

segments.name: Licensed and other brands
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 38 crore, up 14% YoY, supported by marketplace relationships and premiumisation. Dockers licence agreements expected to contribute meaningfully in coming quarters.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 4 crore, up 33% YoY, on higher capacity utilisation and marquee customer relationships.

segments.name: Women's wear (newer category)
segments.commentary: Piloted for about two quarters; management says most revenue so far came from testing. Cited as a growth pillar at around 13% of Q1 revenue per analyst question, not disputed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: continue the growth pace of the last two years, with similar margins (confirmed on Q&A).

Management expects healthy margins and aims for consistent EBITDA margin improvement through the year, but may reinvest margin in growth; the 12-15% EBITDA margin range was cited by an analyst and not disputed.
Price discounting may return in Q2-Q4, particularly festive H2, where management expects better ROI.
Women's wear could reach 2x to 3x current revenue in about a year, with gradual scaling rather than sudden growth.
Insurance claim (fire incident, about INR 21 crore of stock insured) expected to settle soon; debt and interest cost expected to normalise after realisation.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity is fully utilised for the last few quarters; the company uses job work and rented capacity to meet demand.
Manufacturing footprint across Sholapur, Bangalore and Gurgaon, with fulfilment centres across India.
Target manufacturing mix: about 50% in-house, 35-40% outsourced (per-piece labour charges, with in-house quality control), and about 5% bought-out goods.
Capex is consistent each quarter but described as modest; the main effort is workforce hiring, training and line efficiency.
Offline stores (Bangalore) are EBITDA positive but ROCE is below online opportunities, so capital is directed online; new stores will be selective.
demand_pricing: Price elasticity was subdued in Q1; management says demand exists but price cuts did not earn adequate ROI, so it chose performance marketing over discounts.
Management attributed cautious sentiment partly to global macro conditions, including LPG shortages; said August sentiment is positive.
Customer acquisition cost is about 4-6% of GMV, with the quarter at the higher end; no precise CAC or payback figure was given.
Wholesale-style aggregator sales booked at B2B price, about INR 10 crore in Q1, equivalent to about INR 15 crore NSV per management; management says these are EBITDA-margin neutral.
Management claims demand exceeds supply capability.
Q1 is an end-of-season sale quarter in which the company chose not to discount heavily.

qa_highlights.question: How do women's wear unit economics and repeat purchases compare with men's wear, and what share is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said unit economics are neutral to favourable versus men's wear, with better return-cost control. Core products such as bottomwear and basic tops show repeat behaviour similar to men's; no share target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Quick commerce strategy and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Main partner is M-Now (Myntra) at neutral unit economics with no extra fee. Broader quick commerce strategy is still nascent; core categories to be evaluated over the next six to nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Bangalore store performance and expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Stores are EBITDA positive but ROCE is lower than online, so capital goes online. Offline may scale in FY28; new stores will be selective.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth slow in ROI for licensed and own brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is a margin-pressured end-of-season sale quarter; it chose not to match discounts and invested in marketing instead. Lost revenue could be recovered in festive H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still on track for prior revenue run-rate and margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets unchanged: same growth rate as the last few years and healthy margins, with margin improvement sought while reserving margin for growth investment.

qa_highlights.question: Fire insurance claim and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance claim (about INR 21 crore of stock, fully insured) is in process; elevated working-capital loans raised to fund inventory are expected to fall once the claim is realised. Exception provisions are small (INR 3-4 lakh).

qa_highlights.question: Dockers deal: B2B or B2C, and effect on premiumisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Dockers agreement is B2C-focused; B2B is used for long-run sourcing orders. More than 94% of revenue is B2C. Dockers fits the premiumisation strategy.

risks_watch: Finance cost rising sharply on working capital; normalisation depends on timing of the insurance claim settlement, which is still in process.
Revenue growth is dependent on the timing of price reinvestment in H2 festive; if festive demand is weak, the growth catch-up may not happen.
Rising other expenses (marketing) and a higher CAC in Q1; watch whether gross margin gains hold as marketing spend rises.
Aggregator/wholesale channel share (about 40% of brand revenue) and its effect on reported revenue vs. NSV; the company reports B2B value, which understates headline sales.
Women's wear is still in a test-and-scale phase; scaling could strain returns and inventory.
Capacity is fully utilised, so growth depends on job-work and rented capacity.
533941|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the platform and long-term ambition, but defensive on Q1 growth, which management framed as a deliberate trade-off to protect price and margin. Evasive on specific CAC, payback, and insurance claim timing, citing process constraints.

financial_highlights.change: almost 3x YoY (per analyst; not contested by management)

financial_highlights.metric: Wholesale/aggregator revenue booked in Thomas Scott brand
financial_highlights.value: about INR 10 crore (approx. 40% of Thomas Scott revenue)

key_quotes: We chose to protect price realizations and margin quality. We view this as the right choice for long-term brand equity and profitability.
We would not like to blindly scale at the cost of margins.
So, Dockers is in line with our overall bet on premiumization.
The unit economics was largely neutral to favorable in comparison to men's wear. So, there is no trade-off in that manner.
So, our trade receivables have decreased this quarter.
Yes, similar margins.
We want to be the number one multi-brand online retailer globally. That is very clear to us.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: Management targets the same growth rate as the last few years (no numeric rate given), Q1 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 66 crore, and management says demand exceeds supply capability.

rows.why: Women's wear is a pilot of about two quarters with management targeting 2x to 3x current revenue in about a year, and Dockers licence agreements are expected to contribute meaningfully in coming quarters.

rows.label: Insurance claim settlement (about INR 21 crore of stock) to normalise finance co
rows.why: Finance cost rose almost 3x YoY to about INR 1 crore on working capital loans; management expects the claim to settle soon and borrowings to fall once realised, though timing was not given.

rows.label: Women's wear scale-up
rows.why: Management says women's wear could reach 2x to 3x current revenue in about a year, but revenue is ~13% of Q1 and most so far came from testing, so scaling is conditional.

rows.label: Offline store expansion in FY28
rows.why: Bangalore stores are EBITDA positive but ROCE is below online, so capital is directed online and new stores will be selective; offline may scale only in FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on the platform, women's wear and Dockers, and on holding margins, but defensive on Q1 growth framed as a deliberate choice to skip discounts; analysts pushed on CAC, payback, insurance claim timing and the wholesale/aggregator share, which management largely did not quantif

533941|2026-09.headline: Thomas Scott Q2 FY27 revenue rose 39% YoY to INR79 crore and PAT 34% to INR6 crore, with festive sales shifting out of the quarter.
533941|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 39% YoY to about INR79 crore, with EBITDA of about INR11 crore (13.31% margin, up 24% YoY) and PAT of about INR6 crore (7.98% margin, up 34%). H1 FY27 revenue rose 31% to INR145 crore and PAT rose 43% to about INR12 crore. Management said the quarter had no Dussehra sales because the cut-off was 30 September, so margins are not comparable YoY. The company also signed Forever 21 and Dockers licensing and global designated supplier agreements for South Asia and began targeting export revenue, to be reported separately from Q3.

financial_highlights.metric: Thomas Scott own brand revenue (Q2 FY27)
Licensed and other brands revenue (Q2 FY27)

financial_highlights.change: down from INR24 in FY24, about 25% lower

segments.name: Thomas Scott (own brand)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR28 crore, up 28% YoY, driven by brand acceptance, online-first approach, rapid launches and higher push to online distributors and aggregators.

segments.name: Licensed and other brands
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR49 crore, up about 52% YoY; H1 revenue INR87 crore, up 33%. Licensed portfolio is largely sold through Myntra and Flipkart.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing (B2B)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR2 crore, down 29% YoY; H1 B2B revenue stable at INR6 crore. Management said domestic contract manufacturing has plateaued over the last 2-3 years.

segments.commentary: No revenue yet; export platform set up in Q2 and sales made in Q3, to be reported as a separate segment from coming quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: Export revenue not yet booked; a separate segment will be reported from Q3. Management expects at-par or better margins because inventory is shared with India and buyers can order from as few as 20-30 units per design, with no added India-type selling costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall in Q2 and other expenses rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Dussehra sales that fell in Q2 last year moved into October this year, so Q2 had no festive sales and margins are not comparable; some margin may shift into Q3.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is difficult to separate base effect from underlying growth; growth targets are unchanged.

qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days fell to about 94 from about 124 in March; inventory days rose on INR20-30 crore of added finished and trade goods for festive and winter sales; payable days about 60.

qa_highlights.question: What is the related-party exposure and approval size?
qa_highlights.answer: Vedanta Creations is a wholly owned subsidiary of Bang Overseas. Purchases of fabric and garments are at arm's length. The INR100 crore approval was a blanket compliance approval, and future approvals will be rationalised.

Management declined to give channel-wise margins, marketing spend percentage and FY27/FY28 revenue targets.

534076|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 9% to INR 4,000+ crores, a record, but Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 12.1% and goodwill on Dalmia assets was impaired.
534076|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew 9% YoY to INR 4,000 crores on 5% higher shipments of 523 kilotons, the company's highest ever. Q4 revenue was INR 932 crores, hit by geopolitical disruption and a soft cement cycle, with adjusted EBITDA of INR 113 crores (12.1% margin) and adjusted PAT of INR 39 crores before exceptionals. Full-year adjusted EBITDA was INR 477 crores at 11.9% margin versus 13.7% in FY25, and a goodwill impairment on the RHIM IR (Dalmia) assets was booked in the quarter. Management guided to about 13% EBITDA margin for FY27, with price increases of 1-3% from May and a strong coke oven order book.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT before exceptional items (Q4 FY26)

segments.name: Dalmia assets (RHIM IR)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 1,153 crores vs INR 1,013 crores in FY25 (+14%); EBITDA margin 10.8% vs 11.5%. Goodwill impairment booked in Q4 on these assets only.

segments.name: Cement
segments.commentary: Cement fell to about 11% of revenue in FY26 from about 13% in FY25 as management chose not to chase low-margin business amid competitor overcapacity (Calderys, IFGL).

segments.name: Iron making / coke oven and DRI
segments.commentary: Secured a 30,000+ tonne order for 2 coke oven batteries with a large integrated steel customer, covering about 15-18 months; mines now transferred into company name, which management says lowers input cost versus buying at roughly double mining cost.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Largest segment; growth driven by ladle solutions, EAF projects, tundish and ladle slide gate solutions. India-wide steel capacity cited at about 165 million tonnes.

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guided at about 13%, with Q1 FY27 expected to be stronger than the FY26 average.
Volume growth to outperform the market by 1-2 percentage points (management cited 6-7% market growth, implying about 9% company volume growth).
Price increases of 1-3% sought from May 2026 onwards, depending on segment, to offset input cost inflation; some double-digit increases reportedly secured in certain products.
FY27 capex of about INR 150 crores, of which maintenance capex is INR 40-50 crores; to be funded from balance sheet, with no large transactions planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is the restructuring complete, what was the goodwill impairment, and what is the FY27-FY28 roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said restructuring is complete and only the Dalmia assets were impaired, citing lower export volumes, INR/USD volatility on USD-denominated raw materials, and new competitor capacity. Growth is expected to outperform the market by 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the coke oven order a one-time project or recurring supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said coke oven work is project-based but needs no capex; the 30,000+ tonne order covers 2 batteries, and at least 2 of 5 upcoming batteries are expected to follow, supporting the next 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Did inventory cost benefits show up in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the benefit from high-cost alumina inventory was used up, but higher-cost magnesia inventory (fused magnesia, DBM) offset it; double-digit price increases in some cases are expected to offset this and add margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA outlook and how is the 2% outperformance measured?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 full-year EBITDA margin guided at about 13%, with Q1 expected to be strong. Outperformance is measured on volume, not price.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dalmia FY26 revenue and margin, and what is the cement strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Dalmia revenue was INR 1,153 crores (+14%) with a 10.8% margin. Cement share fell to about 11% from 13%; the company is shifting to solution-based selling to large cement customers.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the fixed-cost benefit from iron making is in the margin, and where does margin settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify the iron-making fixed-cost absorption separately. On margin, it said 13% is achievable with mines, order book and 4PRO levers, and that without these it could have dropped to 10-11%.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the price increases and what drives Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases sought are 1-3% versus cost increases, effective from May. Q1 is also supported by pending price increases and the start of the cement season (May-September).

534076|2026-06.headline: RHI Magnesita India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR1,014 crore and EBITDA rose 42% to INR147 crore, a 14.5% margin; management keeps the 13% FY27 margin guidance.
534076|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR1,014 crore, up 9% QoQ and 6% YoY, led by the steel business on favourable realizations and healthy demand. EBITDA grew 42% YoY to INR147 crore and margin expanded to 14.5% from 10.8%, which management attributed to steelmaking execution, price realisation and operating leverage. PAT nearly doubled to INR65 crore from INR35 crore. Management said price increases were largely war surcharges, and it kept FY27 guidance of 13% EBITDA margin and 7-8% volume growth, while stating 9% is a stretch. A leadership change was announced with Pankaj Malhan as MD and CEO, and Parmod Sagar continues as Chairman.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Main driver of Q1 revenue growth on favourable realisations and healthy demand; flow control business cited as the growth engine, with one large group's market share up almost twofold in about 6 months. Management said Dalmia business is flat and growth came from RHIM India.

segments.name: Cement
segments.commentary: Recovered in Q1 on seasonal maintenance demand; management said cement season is almost over by end-September.

segments.name: Industrial (non-ferrous, glass)
segments.commentary: Described as weak in Q1 with few projects in H1; silica and glass project orders expected in Q3-Q4.

segments.name: Coke oven project (PSU)
segments.commentary: Final-stage negotiation with pricing adjustment pending; production to start next month, with a 14-16 month project life.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 13% for FY27 reaffirmed; management said upside possible only if raw material costs ease.
Volume growth guidance of 7-8% for FY27 (management said 9% is a stretch); long-term volume guidance of steel/cement market growth plus 1-2%.
Management said the EUR45 million group pricing and mix benefit is already reflected in Q1 and that India will contribute proportionately.
Capex guidance of INR80-100 crore per year maintained, covering Dalmia plant modernisation, 4PRO machinery, robotics and maintenance.
MINPRO JV (51% RHIM, 49% Khemka) targeted to start production around Q4 FY27; initial investment about INR35 crore over two years, EBITDA 8-10%, payback under 3 years after production.
Quartzite mines (Chiraipani and Bhikampali) expected to open by end of Q1 FY27, with cost benefits from Q2.
Magnesite prices up 6-8% over the last two months; company is working on recipe optimisation and price pass-through.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR8 crore in Q1 vs INR150 crore guidance cited by an analyst; management kept the INR80-100 crore annual run-rate.
MINPRO greenfield mineral processing facility in Odisha, via JV with Khemka Refractories; roughly INR35 crore initial investment over two years.

demand_pricing: Management cited steel production growth, high capacity utilisation and blast furnace/steelmaking investments as demand support; Indian steel grew 7-8% in H1 and steel capex of INR50,000-60,000 crore is expected this financial year.
Cement demand strong, but cement margins under pressure from fuel, energy and raw material costs.
Competitive pressure from domestic and multinational players, with greenfield and brownfield capacity additions and some excess capacity.
Exports reduced QoQ in Q1 per CFO; management expects isostatic flow control export growth over a year.
Alumina prices stable over the last six months; magnesite up 6-8% recently.
Realisation rise attributed mostly to war surcharges and product mix; no price/mix/FX split disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Split of ~12% realisation growth into price, mix and currency; sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: No split given. CFO said most price increases were war surcharges, so growth is primarily product-mix driven.

qa_highlights.question: Q1 capex only INR8 crore vs INR150 crore guidance; will guidance change?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term capex of INR80-100 crore a year unchanged; covers Dalmia modernisation, 4PRO robotics and maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Can volume growth of about 9% be achieved for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 7-8% is achievable but 9% is a stretch unless large high-volume orders come in.

qa_highlights.question: How should medium-term margins be viewed; split between Dalmia and RHIM India?
qa_highlights.answer: Dalmia flat; growth from RHIM India (flow control heavy, Bhiwadi and Jamshedpur). Medium-term margin supported by MINPRO and captive mines; no numeric range given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the EUR45 million group pricing benefit flow into India?
qa_highlights.answer: Benefit is group-wide across six regions; India contributes proportionately and it is already in Q1 numbers. FY27 margin guidance held at 13%.

qa_highlights.answer: No project revenue in Q1. Coke oven project to start next month; glass and silica projects expected in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the quartzite mine and MINPRO JV deliver quantified savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Quantification still in progress by FP&A; management will share later. Mine opening expected by end-Q1 with benefits from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Auditor resignation and goodwill impairment?
qa_highlights.answer: Auditor change aligned with group auditor rotation; Dalmia goodwill fully written off, non-cash and below EBITDA, with headroom. No reversal planned.

Execution on MINPRO (Q4 FY27 start) and quartzite mine (cost benefit from Q2).
CEO transition to Pankaj Malhan and auditor change at the AGM.

534076|2026-09.headline: RHI Magnesita India Q2 FY27 revenue ₹1,030 crore with EBITDA margin of 14% (up 332 bps YoY) on value-over-volume strategy.
534076|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about ₹1,030 crore, the second consecutive quarter above ₹1,000 crore, and EBITDA was ₹144 crore at a 14% margin, up 332 bps YoY. PAT rose 62% YoY to ₹62 crore. Management said it deliberately stepped away from low-margin orders, which kept volumes lower but supported realisations. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹2,044 crore (+2% YoY), EBITDA ₹291 crore (+36%), margin 14.2% (+353 bps), and PAT ₹127 crore (+72%). Working capital rose to 38% of revenue on inventory build, and H1 operating cash flow was ₹99 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Second consecutive quarter above ₹1,000 crore; QoQ change not quantified
Stated as positive despite working capital build

segments.name: Flow control products
segments.commentary: Management said flow control sales grew in pieces rather than tonnes, lifting realisation and masking raw-material cost increases in the material cost percentage. Mix shift toward flow control was described as more than 3 bps QoQ, which appears to be a transcription error.

segments.name: Cement
segments.commentary: Management chose not to bid on some cement opportunities it judged low value, which the company said explains the large YoY gap in this segment. It said it still won some large maintenance and project orders.

segments.name: Silica / cocoon (co-pro)
segments.commentary: Company says it received its largest co-pro order in history to supply silica production lines for 18 months; management said it will take more than a year to execute and will lift utilisation of its silica and quartzite plants.

guidance_outlook: No revenue or realisation guidance given; management said Q2 realisation is likely an anomaly from stepping away from low-margin orders.
FY28 medium-term outlook reiterated: volume growth of about 7% and margin around 14%, per an analyst's summary. Management did not confirm a 15-18% revenue growth target.

Captive raw material: Chirya Pani quartzite mine (40,000 tpa) is operating; Vikampalli mine is expected to start next quarter. Dolomite / DBM backward integration is in its initial phase, with full captive supply targeted in about a year.
Project orders are expected to return in H2 FY27, with a healthy pipeline and higher margins than standard orders.
No dividend guidance given.
capex_capacity: Quartzite / Chirya Pani mine operational at 40,000 tpa annual capacity; Vikampalli mine start-up expected next quarter.
Captive raw material via the new raw-material facility started operations near quarter-end; savings estimated at 3–3.5% of raw-material cost, with full captive supply targeted in about a year.
Minpro joint venture with Khemka Refractories started invoicing in August 2026; capacity expansion planned next quarter.
Capacity utilisation is in the low 60s%. No volume guidance given.
Capex is directed at equipment reliability upgrades, technology transfers from the global parent, and compliance; figures were not given.
demand_pricing: Realisations rose as the mix shifted to flow control and the company declined low-margin orders, mainly in cement. Management declined to guide on realisation.
Raw material costs are rising: magnesia, DBM and fused magnesia have sharply increased, with a recent steep rise in DBM and FM prices, alumina-based inputs also up, and ocean freight higher.
Indian steel demand grew about 7.2% in H1 while crude steel output grew about 2.8%, per management.
Competition: Chinese suppliers remain a concern in cocoon; management expects India's refractory overcapacity to persist for a while.
Export: management said North America is not feasible; Europe is uncompetitive due to CBAM; Middle East and Africa are the only near-term export opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key focus areas for the new CEO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new steel product opportunities (CSP trial with a large Indian account), penetration of leading partner markets, domestic sourcing shifts, the recycling business, and digital customer reach.

qa_highlights.question: How will the captive raw-material (quartzite) facility affect costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said savings are estimated at 3–3.5% of raw-material cost, with full captive supply expected in about a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the volume growth guidance of 7–9% be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is balancing value and volume and did not give a new number, but acknowledged the need to improve volumes and expects project orders to contribute in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise and working capital intensity increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose due to raw-material cost inflation, building stock for large silica orders, industrial project orders, and resilience buffers.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue grow 15–18% from FY28 while margins hold at 14–15%?
qa_highlights.answer: No forward revenue guidance was given. Management reiterated growth drivers in glass, gasifiers, industrial segments and technology transfers, and said it is working toward FY28 growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company losing market share given flat revenue around ₹1,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the flow control business is gaining share and some orders will flow through later. It said cement was deliberately under-bid, and it pointed to a plan to rebuild share through solution-based selling.

Working capital intensity at 38% and inventory build need to unwind for cash conversion to improve.

Chinese competition in cocoon and industry overcapacity may keep pricing under pressure.
CFO transition to Abhishek Bajaj; the Vikampalli mine start and project-order timing in H2 are key items to monitor.

534091|2026-03.headline: MCX FY26 consolidated revenue more than doubled to INR2,302 crore and PAT crossed INR1,300 crore, with ADT up ~2.5x.
534091|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a very strong year, with consolidated revenue from operations more than doubling to INR2,302 crore and EBITDA of INR1,774 crore. Average daily turnover across futures and options rose about 2.5 times, with bullion growing more than 4 times and energy growing strongly off a high base. Management said growth was both structural and cyclical, but declined to comment on April and May participation and said not every quarter will be a big jump over the prior quarter. Cost lines (product licence fees, other expenses, SGF contribution, software support) rose faster than revenue in Q4, and management said the focus is on efficiency rather than spending less.

segments.commentary: Early stage; about 50 commercial participants onboarded and UCC numbers rising month on month. Revenue not tracked separately.

Mutual funds were cited as a future channel for commodity exposure after a regulatory change allowing more flexibility.

qa_highlights.answer: Management wants democratic, steady growth rather than aggressive push. Digital brokers, the consolidated ledger and UX improvements are cited; mutual funds and wealth channels are expected to add participation later.

qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed there were no one-offs. Costs are for growth, technology and people. Q4 other expenses were attributed to market development and professional charges.

qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 interest income was INR59 crore, up from INR22 crore in Q4 FY25, due to higher cash placed with the subsidiary. The full-year figure was not given.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said SGF is comfortable with a good cushion. No percentage of transaction charges has been published; SGF needs depend on volatility, margins, volume and OI together.

qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 55% to 60% BG share cited by the analyst and said FDs are the largest portion and fully funded. Interoperability is harder in commodities because products are not identical to equity instruments; the regulator decides.

Management described Q1 as a consolidation after an exceptionally strong Q4 FY26, with ADT at INR10.5 lakh crores and futures ADT up 47% YoY. Bullion options premium ratio fell sharply as volatility normalised, while notional volumes rose, and management said bullion volumes were softer in the quarter. Management said the RBI bank guarantee rule (in force from July) is not expected to be significantly detrimental, and that it is more a Q2 issue.

534139|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 order intake hit a record INR 915 crore (+0.5% YoY, double-digit QoQ) but EBIT fell to INR 32 crore on gross margin pressure and negative operating leverage.
534139|2026-06.overview: Management reported a record quarterly order booking of INR 915 crore, with sales growing about 5% YoY in a seasonally soft Q1 and an order backlog of about INR 2,100 crore entering Q2, up around 33%. EBIT was INR 32 crore, lower than last year, as commodity inflation (copper, aluminium, steel, transformer wire) and legacy fixed-price contracts compressed gross margin, while employee and other costs rose faster than sales. Management attributed the margin dip largely to Q1 operating leverage and FX-driven import costs, and said pricing actions are underway but will take time to flow through. No numerical guidance was given; management said the balance three quarters should be good.

534139|2026-09.headline: Schneider Electric Infrastructure H1 FY25 sales rose 20.3% to INR 1,193 crore and PAT 32.1% to INR 103 crore, with orders up 17.5% to INR 1,104 crore.
534139|2026-09.overview: H1 FY25 sales grew 20.3% YoY to INR 1,193 crore, driven by execution against backlog, with Q2 sales up 21% to INR 600 crore. Gross margin widened about 3 points to 39.5% in H1, but other expenses rose 38.8% on CSR, customer support and risk provisions, which held EBITDA growth to 44.2% and PAT growth to 32.1%. Q2 PAT of INR 54.3 crore included a INR 5.8 crore deferred tax reversal tied to the revised long-term capital gains tax rate.

+38.8% YoY, incl. higher CSR and specific provisions

segments.name: Order intake mix (Q2)
segments.commentary: Equipment 47%, projects 13%, transaction 23%, services 17% of Q2 order intake. Intergroup orders are not captured as orders; indicated at about INR 125 crore.

segments.commentary: Exports were about 14% of total sales.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the strong cash flow and how is export and services performance?

534309|2026-06.headline: NBCC standalone Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 62% to INR 160 crore (8.77% margin) on 10% revenue growth to INR 1,823 crore.
534309|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to INR 1,823 crore, while EBITDA rose 62% to INR 160 crore and PAT rose 32% to INR 151 crore, helped by marketing fees from the Bharat Business Park sale. Consolidated revenue was INR 2,260 crore, with a consolidated order book of INR 1,27,000 crore and INR 1,600 crore of orders secured in the quarter. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore and expects INR 18,000-20,000 crore of new awards over the next 2-3 quarters, but several large awards (GPRA 5 colonies, J&K, MAHAPREIT, Supertech) have slipped repeatedly. Management also announced the HSCC merger into NBCC and an SPV for a proposed CPSE REIT.

segments.name: PMC / redevelopment (standalone order book)
segments.commentary: Standalone order book split is about 60% redevelopment and 40% PMC. Management says redevelopment and Amrapali contribute more than 60% of total revenue, and PMC fees are 8% plus 1% marketing on Amrapali.

segments.name: Real estate
segments.commentary: Management expects about INR 500 crore of real estate revenue this year from land, completed inventory and WIP sales. Bharat Business Park was fully sold, raising about INR 10,000 crore across three auctions.

segments.name: HSCC (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue dipped because HSCC foreclosed a Maharashtra health project quoted at about 2% margin, which management says cost about INR 300 crore of top line. Management is merging HSCC into NBCC.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore reiterated; management referred to INR 16,000-17,000 crore in parts of the call.
Standalone FY27 revenue guided at INR 13,000-14,000 crore; FY28 revenue around INR 21,000 crore; FY29 INR 24,000-25,000 crore (consolidated basis per management).
PAT guidance of INR 1,100-1,200 crore for FY27, INR 1,300-1,400 crore for FY28 and about INR 2,000 crore for FY29, on a consolidated basis.
Margin guidance: EBITDA at least 6.5-7% and PAT 6-6.5%.

Awards guided at INR 20,000-25,000 crore this year (including Supertech about INR 10,000 crore, J&K about INR 3,500 crore, Rajasthan Mandapam about INR 3,500 crore), against an earlier INR 30,000-32,000 crore target.
GPRA 5 colonies (Lodhi Colony, Andrews Ganj, DIZ, Lakshmi Bai Nagar) order of about INR 30,000 crore expected; management says cabinet approval is pending.
Redevelopment fund generation of INR 30,000-35,000 crore expected this year, sale-linked and construction-linked, with cash collected over about two years.
capex_capacity: Phase 2 Amrapali is awarded and in execution, with one tower at the 20th floor using Mivan shuttering and others at the 13th floor; Phase 1 has 23 of 24 projects completed.
Standalone order book: about INR 10,000 crore of balance work across GPRA 7 packages, to be completed within about 18-24 months.
Gurugram Sector 37-D: contractor mobilised and test piles done; revised plan and EC approval pending, with sales expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27.
Ghitorni: final lease agreement in process; consultant tender expected to be finalised this quarter; revenue after handover in about two years.
Business Park Tower purchase is construction-linked; only 10% first instalment paid so far, with the balance tied to construction milestones over about two years.
Dubai: 66 housing units under construction on a purchased land parcel; developer licence in hand; construction tender expected in October.
Goa redevelopment: four packages ordered, site mobilised and work started; two more packages pending tender.
demand_pricing: Africa Avenue auction for 262 residential units drew about 2,900 participants; auction postponed on a technical issue and expected in August. Vinayak Mandir auction targeted for September and Palanji area for September-October. Management expects INR 5,000-6,000 crore from Africa Avenue sales.
Amrapali: about 8,800 units in total, with roughly 4,000-4,500 sold; management expects to sell about INR 4,000-5,000 crore of inventory.

Pipeline: Supertech tender to be floated this quarter (16 projects in Noida and Greater Noida, about INR 10,000 crore); J&K infrastructure tender of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore to be floated this month after an initial INR 100 crore package drew about 15 bidders; MAHAPREIT (about INR 25,000 crore) expected in Q3; Naveen Nagpur infrastructure tender after DPR approval.

Recent wins: Odisha schools INR 253 crore, J&K campus INR 171 crore, New AP Bhavan INR 106 crore (Q1); Seychelles housing about INR 620 crore, RBI Amravati about INR 780 crore, Rajasthan science labs about INR 431 crore (July-August).
International: Seychelles has awarded a further 1,000 houses after about 2,000 in Maldives; management cites prospects in Australia, Saudi Arabia and Fiji, none included in projections.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the large orders (about INR 50,000 crore GPRA 5 colonies plus other large orders) delayed, and when will they come? Is FY27 and FY28 revenue still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: GPRA 5 colonies (about INR 30,000 crore) has cleared the group of ministers and PIB and is with Cabinet; management says it is a matter of time. At least one or two contracts expected in Q2 and major ones in Q3. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore and said it is adhering to it.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins move over the next two to three quarters, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will rise because redevelopment and Amrapali contribute more than 60% of revenue. Guided EBITDA minimum 6.5-7% and PAT 6-6.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA rise sharply while work and consultancy expenses fell from INR 3,412 crore in Q4 FY26 to INR 1,536 crore in Q1 FY27 (standalone)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the jump to marketing fees from the Bharat Business Park sale, which carry low associated expenses. Further marketing fees are expected from Africa Avenue, Vinayak Mandir, Sarojini Nagar (7 GPRA) and 1% on Amrapali inventory sales of about INR 4,000-5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone and PMC revenue growth look slow, and what are the FY27-FY29 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited HSCC dropping a low-margin (about 2%) Maharashtra health project, costing about INR 300 crore of top line, and said Q1 is seasonally slow. Standalone FY27 revenue INR 13,000-14,000 crore; FY28 about INR 21,000 crore; FY29 INR 24,000-25,000 crore. PAT guidance INR 1,100-1,200 crore FY27, INR 1,300-1,400 crore FY28, about INR 2,000 crore FY29 (consolidated).

qa_highlights.question: Is the Business Park tower purchase a cash drain, and what are the cash timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the first 10% instalment is paid; the rest is construction-linked over about two years. Management said cash will go out as CapEx and cited an auction price rise from a base of INR 39,100 to about INR 66,000 on the ground floor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CPSE REIT plan, timeline and investment needed?
qa_highlights.answer: NBCC approved an SPV in principle, subject to ministry and DIPAM approval, to hold three rentable assets totalling about 75,000 sq ft. No timeline was given; management said a national REIT will be launched only after a considerable portfolio (across CPSEs, est. INR 40,000-50,000 crore across five or six REITs) is assembled.

qa_highlights.question: Why have big awards (J&K, MAHAPREIT, Supertech) slipped, and is funding the constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited government clearances, DPR approvals, seed money and about 18-20 statutory approvals. Seed money is being arranged by NBCC on some projects and by clients on others; a HUDCO MoU is in place. Management revised awards guidance to INR 20,000-25,000 crore this year from an earlier INR 30,000-32,000 crore.

risks_watch: Repeated slippage of large awards: GPRA 5 colonies (about INR 30,000 crore, Cabinet pending), J&K (about INR 3,500-4,000 crore tender), MAHAPREIT (about INR 25,000 crore, now Q3) and Supertech (about INR 10,000 crore). FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore against standalone Q1 revenue of INR 1,823 crore; analysts questioned the run rate and Q3 Delhi GRAP construction curbs.
Earnings quality: Q1 EBITDA gain driven partly by one-off marketing fees from Bharat Business Park; FY27 PAT guidance of INR 1,100-1,200 crore needs roughly 2x the Q1 run rate of INR 151 crore.

Cash and seed money: cash of INR 666 crore at 30 June; the comparison to INR 6,500 crore last quarter was not reconciled. Seed money needs for new projects and the construction-linked Business Park payments are open questions.

Real estate and REIT execution: Gurugram 37-D sales depend on revised plan and EC approval; Ghitorni lease is still being finalised; the REIT has no timeline. Revenue from Ghitorni and 37-D comes only after about two years.

So, due to various approvals, the project got delayed. Two reason. One is fund. Other one is various approvals.
Definitely, it is going to happen. We have the figures; I am not making commitments casually.
I am still committing to these figures, and whatever I am saying, those figures will be achieved.

534309|2026-09.headline: NBCC Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 38% YoY to INR 2,890 crore and standalone PAT rose 31% to INR 225 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the monetisation plans for land parcels and the associated tax and market value?

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected revenue conversion timeline for new orders?

534392|2026-03.headline: Vardhman Special Steels posted record FY26 profit of about INR122 crore on 225,000 tons volume; EBITDA/ton guidance raised to INR8,000-11,000.
534392|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a record year, with profit of about INR122 crore and sales volume of 225,000 tons, in line with budget. The Iran-US conflict pushed raw material prices up in Q4 and raised gas costs, but gas supply was not disrupted. Management raised FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance to INR8,000-11,000 from INR7,000-10,000 and set a 2-year target of INR9,000-12,000. The call centred on a reheating furnace commissioned in March, a solar plant, a new 210x210 section, a forging project, and a planned greenfield steel plant with capex of about INR2,000 crore.

segments.name: Automotive special steels (existing plant)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 225,000 tons; FY27 sales target about 250,000-255,000 tons, with 250,000 tons to be used for modelling. Rolling capacity about 180,000 tons was supplemented by outsourced rolling; rolling capacity rises to 270,000 tons after the reheating furnace.

segments.name: Forging (ring gears, Aichi technology)
segments.commentary: Project budget INR475 crore, now expected to come in below that; about INR80 crore spent so far. First line targeted for Jan-Mar 2028 start, with ramp-up in FY29; plans for at least 3 lines.

segments.name: Greenfield steel plant
segments.commentary: Capacity 500,000-600,000 tons; commissioning targeted July 2029; land acquisition expected to close in May 2026. Ramp-up budgeted at 5-6 years to full utilisation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance INR8,000-11,000; INR9,000-12,000 targeted in about 2 years, with management saying this could be a more confident range.
FY27 rolled volume target about 250,000-255,000 tons; for modelling, management asked analysts to use 250,000 tons, with a static 270,000-275,000 tons thereafter for the existing plant.

Melt shop currently under 300,000 tons licence; expansion to about 360,000 tons needs environmental clearance (50-50 chance, decision expected before March 2027); if approved, commissioning late CY27.
Price increases sought from Q1 FY27 to pass through higher scrap costs; discussions ongoing.
Government incentives expected at about INR12-13 crore in FY27, as the GST refund scheme ends Aug 2026 and electricity duty exemption runs to Aug 2029.
Equity infusion of about INR1,200 crore (INR385 crore already in, about INR800 crore to come), plus about INR1,200 crore debt; peak debt/equity below 0.75, comfort at 0.5.
capex_capacity: Reheating furnace commissioned March 2026, lifting rolling capacity to 270,000 tons; 9 crore units/year solar plant commissioned in Q4; new 210x210 section added to improve cast productivity and reduce rework.
Heat size raised from 37 tons to 40 tons; new NDT line and new peeling line in progress; Kocks Block commissioned.
Melt shop: plan to raise melting from 300,000 to about 360,000 tons, subject to environmental approval; equipment lead time 1-1.5 years.

Capex FY27 about INR100 crore (mostly land and development for the new plant, plus normal/replacement capex); FY27-28 expansion capex about INR700-800 crore, plus about INR100 crore for the existing plant and INR80-100 crore more if environmental approval comes.

Committed investment about INR2,600 crore through FY30: about INR2,000 crore for the steel plant and INR475 crore for forging; further specialised-alloy investments (ESR, VAR, VIM) still to be planned.
demand_pricing: Pricing works on spreads, not commodity prices; alloy steel prices rise less than commodity steel when scrap rises and fall less when scrap falls. Management said average selling price fell in FY26 versus FY25 despite higher volume.
Exports to be mainly indirect, via components from India to global OEs and EU FTA/CBAM benefits; direct export share to stay low. Luxury OEs such as BMW and Mercedes-Benz may give better prices.
Forging customer validation: Maruti Suzuki wants to see the factory running before validation; Aichi-linked approvals may be faster.
Management sees tool and die steel imports of about INR1,000 crore/year as an opportunity for future ingot-casting products.
Product mix expected to stay similar for the foreseeable future; a dip is likely when the new plant ramps up.

qa_highlights.question: What volume should be modelled for rolled products and is 250,000 tons sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said keep 250,000 tons for FY27 (target 255,000), with 270,000-275,000 tons from the following year and static at that level for existing plant modelling.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA/ton be in the 8,500-11,000 range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed guidance of INR8,000-11,000 for this year, moving to INR9,000-12,000 in about 2 years; FY26 averaged above INR8,500.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakup of FY26 capex and how much will the forging project cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Kocks Block, reheating furnace, warehouses and land were the main items. Forging budget INR475 crore, spend so far about INR80 crore; expected to finish below budget, with more precise figures in about 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected FY27/FY28 capex and funding plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR100 crore; FY27-28 about INR700-800 crore for expansion. Debt/equity to stay below 0.75; about INR1,200 crore equity (INR385 crore in, Vardhman Group INR300-400 crore, Aichi, possible QIP) and about INR1,200 crore debt.

qa_highlights.question: What are government incentives and will the new plant get PLI?
qa_highlights.answer: No PLI for the new plant; it will be under the Punjab scheme. Incentives about INR12-13 crore in FY27 versus INR24 crore in FY26, as the GST refund ends Aug 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What ROCE is expected after the new plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes EBITDA on capital employed stays above 20% once plants reach full utilisation; below 20% it would not make sense to keep investing.

qa_highlights.question: What components will the forging plant make and what is its capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Ring gears for cars, using an Aichi process; one line initially versus Aichi's 9 lines. Management declined to give asset-level detail.

risks_watch: Environmental approval for the melt shop expansion to 360,000 tons is uncertain (management puts it at 50-50); Ludhiana is in a critically polluted zone.
Forging ramp-up depends on customer validation; Maruti Suzuki will validate only after seeing the factory operating; FY29 is the first year of meaningful forging volume.
Greenfield plant timeline (July 2029) and 5-6 year ramp-up carry execution and cost risk; capex figures are described as rough ballpark estimates.
Raw material and gas cost volatility from the Iran-US conflict; management flagged possible global recession and high oil prices as factors affecting the EBITDA range.
Dilution and funding: about INR800 crore equity still to come, including a possible QIP, and about INR1,200 crore debt to raise.
Expiry of the GST refund incentive in Aug 2026 lowers FY27 subsidy income to about INR12-13 crore.

Management avoided project-level returns and firm timelines beyond FY28.

So we are very clear, we will remain only in the area of special steels and automotive forgings.
So after the plants are established and running towards full capacity utilization, EBITDA on capital employed, we hope to continue to be above 20%.

534392|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% to INR486 crore and EBITDA reached INR68 crore (INR10,760/ton), with PAT at INR41 crore.
534392|2026-06.overview: Sales volume was 59,000 tons, up 6.5% YoY, with revenue up 12% on higher volumes and OEM price revisions tied to input cost increases. EBITDA was INR68 crore (INR10,760/ton, management says excluding treasury income from Aichi surplus funds, the figure is near INR10,700/ton), and PAT was INR41 crore versus INR34 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR20 crore a year ago. Management said demand exceeds what it can supply, the 3 lakh ton licensed capacity is the binding constraint, and it has applied for an increase to 3.6 lakh tons. Forging project with Aichi Steel is tracking on schedule with capex now below the INR475 crore estimate, and the greenfield 5 lakh ton plant scope and cost are being revised upward.

financial_highlights.value: INR10,760/ton (INR10,700 excluding treasury income from Aichi surplus funds)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR34 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR20 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Automotive steel (core)
segments.commentary: Volumes were good and prices were revised upward on cost pass-through; Q1 settlement is complete with some OEMs and pending with others, where the price is expected to rise further. Maruti is about 10% of business.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Direct exports are about 6-7% of sales and indirect exports via the Aichi trading arm about 5%; management guides total exports to 7-8% (max about 10%), with Aichi roughly 40-50% of exports.

segments.commentary: Ingot casting is due in Q3 FY27 and to stabilise in Q4; die steel production is expected to be regular in FY28. Die steel imports into India are about INR1,000 crore a year, and die steel sells at about INR2.5 lakh/ton (non-ESR) versus average realisation of about INR85,000/ton.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target about 255,000 tons; FY28 target above 270,000 tons, rising to about 290,000 tons if the environmental approval for 3.6 lakh tons comes through, and 330,000-340,000 tons in FY28-29 with new capex.
EBITDA/ton range is INR8,000-11,000 currently; management intends to move to INR8,000-12,000 for next year and to INR9,000-12,000 after the new solar plant and value-added products ramp up (FY28-29).
Q2 FY27 realisations are expected to be higher than Q1 after a 1 July price increase request; Q3 is expected broadly flat to slightly up or down depending on raw material prices.
Rolling mill has reached 3 lakh tons input capacity and is expected to reach 330,000 tons of input, about 10% higher, within the current licence constraint.
Forging project with Aichi Steel: commissioning by Q4 FY28, with 6-12 months to fill; revenue from around end FY29 to FY30; capex below INR475 crore estimate (more than 10% saving).

New greenfield steel plant (about 5 lakh tons, to be enlarged): commissioning on track for FY29-30; land and machinery to be finalised by mid-September 2026; cost likely a little higher than earlier per ton due to metals inflation and rupee depreciation.
capex_capacity: Existing licensed capacity is 3 lakh tons; application for 3.6 lakh tons (360,000 tons melting) is pending with the Environment Ministry, with approval expected in about 3-4 months but not assured.
New reheating furnace has stabilised; new NDT (testing) line and new peeling line to be commissioned September-October 2026 to remove bottlenecks and reduce job work.
Solar: about 50% capacity addition planned in roughly 1-1.5 years; savings will be lower than phase one because local cell manufacturing rules raise panel cost.

Greenfield plant being reconfigured (scrap preheating, extra continuous testing and automatic testing lines), so capacity and cost will rise; a refined project is due at the next Board meeting, with details in next quarter.
Funding: internal cash is in hand; a capital raise is planned in FY28 with commitments from Vardhman Group and Aichi; Punjab government support is assured.
demand_pricing: Demand is strong and the company is turning away orders; there are no long-term orders, all business is repeat, and customer volumes drive supply.
Next volume lift comes from commercial production for import substitution for Maruti, expected from Q4 FY27.
Tie-ups with Aichi and Toyota Kirloskar (TKM) support approvals; TKM's new Aurangabad plant needs green steel, where the company claims to be the only Indian player with the approvals.
Price revisions follow raw material cost changes; OEMs can reverse or move prices, and the company operates within a band.
Non-auto product mix is a planned margin lever; die steel is high-price, low-volume and carries higher heat-treatment cost.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue is from exports, and how is business concentrated by customer?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct exports are about 6-7% and indirect exports via Aichi's trading arm about 5%; Maruti is about 10% of sales, and management says there is no concentration risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the 3 lakh to 3.6 lakh ton expansion and the 5 lakh ton greenfield plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The EC application is filed and approval is expected in 3-4 months; the greenfield land and machinery are to be finalised by August end to mid-September, and the plant will be larger than 5 lakh tons with cost likely a little higher.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the EBITDA/ton range rising from INR8,000-11,000 to INR8,000-12,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites higher volumes spreading fixed costs, lower operating costs, reduced job work from Q3 FY27, and the new solar plant; the range floor is to move to 9,000 after the solar addition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume target and what drives growth beyond the licence limit?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is about 255,000 tons, FY28 above 270,000 tons; growth beyond that needs the EC approval and new capex, and non-auto products (ingot casting, die steel, railway axles, windmill shafts) are the next growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aichi forging project cost and timeline on track?
qa_highlights.answer: The project is on schedule for commissioning by Q4 FY28, cost is more than 10% below the INR475 crore estimate, and revenue begins around end FY29 with a 6-12 month fill-up period.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a partner for the advanced metals / aerospace JV?
qa_highlights.answer: No partner is selected; management is talking to several parties, the JV will be a separate company that is not Aichi, and it is expected to take a couple of years, so the numbers are outside the forecast horizon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book and realisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has no formal order book and says it is fully booked; Q2 realisations are expected to be higher than Q1 after a 1 July price increase, while Q3 is expected broadly flat.

risks_watch: Licence cap at 3 lakh tons constrains volume; the 3.6 lakh ton EC approval is pending and not assured.
Pending OEM price settlements for Q1 and Q2 realisations depend on OEM acceptance and raw material costs.
Greenfield project cost is rising (metals inflation, rupee depreciation, added testing lines), and the refined project and cost are due in the next Board meeting and next quarter.
Solar savings in the next phase will be lower because of local cell rules, which affects the planned EBITDA/ton uplift.
The reported EBITDA of INR68 crore includes treasury income from surplus Aichi funds; management excluded it to get INR10,700/ton, so the operating figure should be tracked separately.
Direct export share was over-estimated earlier; the company will start estimating indirect component exports from next quarter.

534392|2026-09.headline: Vardhman Special Steels Q2 FY27 PAT rose about 50% YoY on sales up 27%, with EBITDA per ton at the top of the INR9,000–12,000 guided range.
534392|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly sales, with total sales up 27% YoY, revenue from operations up 39% and EBITDA and PAT each up about 50%. Strong automotive demand and tight supply after unscheduled shutdowns at a large competitor drove price increases over the last two quarters, and management said EBITDA per ton is currently at the high end of its range, partly due to inventory gains it called non-sustainable. The greenfield steel plant (INR2,000 crore cost, now expected to be higher), the forging plant and the brownfield expansion from 300,000 to 360,000 tons remain in progress, with the environmental approval still pending. Management also flagged a possible shift to 1:1 debt-equity, a rights issue in 2H CY27, and a possible dividend suspension for 3–4 years, to be decided at the April board meeting.

Target segments include tool and die steel, oil and gas, railways and bearings, with aerospace and defence later. Management said near-term volumes are very limited given full capacity.

segments.commentary: Foundation stone laid in July 2026, with the plant expected by March 2028. Full capacity is about 15,000 tons per year, with the first line of about INR450–475 crore, and the Japanese partner Aichi will drive the business. Forging capex is expected to come in below budget.

Greenfield steel plant: completion targeted for September 2029 and stabilisation by March 2030. Environmental approval filing expected by December 2026, with the land for the melting part complete and the rolling-part land due by January 2027.

Project cost will exceed the earlier INR2,000 crore estimate. The project design will be finalised by March/April 2027; scope is being built to take output beyond 500,000 tons to at least 700,000 tons in phase 2.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is an element of inventory gains but did not quantify it; it is not sustainable. Since the July 2025 move to SAP S/4 HANA, costing is batch-wise, with no period-end revaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume growth continue above guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is seasonally strongest for festive stocking; FY27 volume now expected at about 260,000 tons, at the higher end of the budget.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings and receivables rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowings rose to INR162.93 crore due to Ind AS reclassification of LC-discounting creditors; combined with creditors, debt has not risen. Receivables rose with the 11,000-ton incremental sales in August–September, with receivable days up 4–5 days.

qa_highlights.answer: Approval is still awaited; the timeline is about a year or December 2027, whichever is later, with capex of about INR100–115 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give the revised greenfield capex, saying a figure will be shared around April 2027. Forging costs will be lower than budgeted, and initial absorption is about 15,000 tons per year at full capacity.

534425|2026-03.headline: Speciality Restaurants Q4 FY26 revenue up 13.65% YoY and PAT up 44.20%, with SSG of 2.25% for the quarter and 11.57% in April.
534425|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue growth of 13.65% YoY and PAT growth of 44.20%, helped by 2.25% same-store sales growth and gross margin expansion from 69.1% to 70.4%. Full-year SSG was 1.49%, and April SSG reached 11.57%, which management attributed to higher dine-in covers and refurbishments of older restaurants. Management guided to about 15% top-line growth in FY27 and about 15-16% EBITDA growth on revenue, with 32 new outlets planned. On the cost side, the company took a 4% price increase and moved 78% of its kitchens off LPG/PNG to induction, targeting 100% within 20 days.

segments.name: Mainland China / Asia Kitchen / Gong (Asian brands)

segments.name: Haka (digital QSR, delivery-first)
segments.commentary: Haka operates from hybrid sites, with about 40-50% of new Mainland China stores co-locating a Haka and Oh! Calcutta cloud kitchen. Management expects Haka to reach a 'decent number' within two quarters; no figure was given.

segments.name: Walters and Sweet Bengal
segments.commentary: Walters AOV is about INR 700 and Sweet Bengal about INR 400 per cover. Plans include 15 new Walters (to 20 total) and 10 new Sweet Bengal outlets in FY27, with Sweet Bengal rebranding and FMCG packaging planned.

Walters commissary set up in Maharashtra, geared for 20-25 stores.
Induction conversion: about INR 1.12 crores spent on induction woks since 4 March; 78% of the restaurant chain off LPG/PNG, with 100% targeted within 20 days.
Average occupancy is about 2 times installed cover capacity on an average basis, according to management.
demand_pricing: April 2026 SSG of 11.57%; management said there was no sign of consumer slowdown as of late May, citing a planned redemption-coupon scheme (for example INR 200 or INR 150 off a INR 1,000 meal) launching at the end of May.
Price increase of 4% taken in FY26, with management stating it would not take more than 4% and is not seeking extra margin from price.
Management said there is no significant reduction in spend historically during high inflation or domestic shocks other than COVID, and none currently.
Franchisees: 11 earlier, 7 remaining, each paying 6% of revenue as royalty with no capex by the company; management said Indian partners need 'skin in the game'.
Competition: management sees Panda Express as a fast QSR format different from Mainland China, so no threat to the business.

qa_highlights.question: What were same-store sales growth for Q4 and FY26, and why is the company lagging peers like Barbeque Nation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 SSG was 2.25% and full-year FY26 was 1.49%. Management said April SSG was 11.57%, driven by more dine-in covers, and blamed slow growth on unrenovated restaurants, with refurbishments now under way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the restaurant-level economics for top brands?
qa_highlights.answer: For a 2,500-3,000 sq ft store, revenue is INR 8-9 crores a year with 22% restaurant EBITDA before rent. Rent is about 20-21% of revenue (revenue-share triggers at 17-18%), leaving about 15% post-rent EBITDA. Breakeven takes 4-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company managing LPG and fuel supply, and what does induction cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The company started the transition on 4 March and imported wok-based induction sets (around 300). It has 78% of the chain off fuel, targeting 100% in 20 days. Management said induction cost is the same or lower, with a 6% saving in a pilot restaurant from avoiding pilot-flame wastage.

qa_highlights.question: Why not focus on fewer brands, given that the bottom 8 brands contribute under 10% each?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed seven focus brands (Mainland China, Asia Kitchen, Haka, Gong, Siciliana, Walters, Sweet Bengal). Other brands are profitable and will not be shut, but no further expansion is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback under consideration, given the cash pile and the share price correction?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the question would be taken up by the Board and it was too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: How can FY26 cash flow (about INR 80 crores CFO less about INR 50 crores rent) reconcile with a 15% EBITDA margin claim?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the 15-16% figure is at restaurant level after rent. Cash-flow EBITDA is after corporate costs, which fell to about 4% of revenue from 6-7% as the company resumed expansion.

Consumer wallet pressure on discretionary dining if inflation or geopolitical uncertainty deepens; management reports no current impact.

Execution risk on 32 new outlets, Gong expansion in Pune and Delhi, and Haka scaling.
Corporate cost and new-store front-end costs may slow EBITDA growth to about 15-16% against revenue growth of about 15%.
Management's FY27 revenue of about INR 600 crores and FY28 of about INR 700 crores are forward-looking and dependent on macro conditions.
Gross margin and EBITDA reconciliation: an analyst said cash-flow-implied EBITDA margin was about 7-8%, against management's 15-16% restaurant-level figure; this gap was not fully resolved.

534425|2026-06.headline: Speciality Restaurants Q1 FY27 same-store sales grew 11.35% and gross margin rose 1.2pp to 71.1%, with management declining to give a INR600 crore revenue target.

Gross margin improved to 71.1% from 69.9%, attributed to portion control, reduced inefficiencies and vendor negotiations, despite inflation. rows.why: Rising input, staff, power and licensing costs could force price increases, and trained manpower shortages may slow store additions, though management gave no explicit cut signal.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Walters, Sweet Bengal (Kheer Kadam shelf life extended to 30 days) and Haka delivery formats are scaling, and older brands are being phased out, but no specific new launch dates were given.

rows.label: Odisha F&B plot joint development (Speciality Hotels India)
rows.why: Joint development is progressing and expected to complete by FY27 year-end, with the company holding about 34% of the demerged entity post completion.

rows.label: Gas-to-induction kitchen conversion and rate contracts
rows.why: Gas-to-induction shift and six-month or full-year rate contracts helped lift gross margin 1.2pp to 71.1%, and the 11 cloud kitchens and gas shortages make the switch a continuing lever.

rows.label: Cash balance held near INR162 crore by year-end
