tone.note: Management was confident on margins (gross margin up 1.2pp to 71.1%), 11.35% same-store growth and July demand, but evasive on the INR600 crore revenue target and store counts, and defensive on delivery mix and the brand portfolio, while analysts pressed on those points.

534425|2026-09.headline: Speciality Restaurants Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18.24% YoY to INR 129.78 crore, with operational EBITDA up 39.44% to INR 10.24 crore.
534425|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 18.24% YoY to INR 129.78 crore and PAT rose 45.75% to INR 6.94 crore. Operational EBITDA margin expanded to 8.03% from 6.81%, and same-store sales growth was 8.1% in Q2 (11.32% in Q1; 9.8% in H1). Delivery mix rose to 32% from 27.4% a year earlier, and the network stood at 125 outlets at September 30, 2026. Management flagged a pipeline of 2-3 openings in Q3 and a 200-outlet target by FY2030, with restaurant-level EBITDA of 22-23% post Ind AS as the internal benchmark.

financial_highlights.change: +18.24% YoY vs INR 109.76 crore in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Company-level EBITDA margin (pre Ind AS, ex lease accounting)

financial_highlights.value: 32% of Q2 FY27 sales (management also cited ~29% elsewhere in call)

segments.name: Asia Kitchen (illustrative unit economics)
segments.commentary: Monthly throughput of INR 60-75 lakh (about INR 2-2.5 lakh per day), gross margin ~76%, staff cost 20-22%, rentals 18%, opex 11%, restaurant EBITDA ~22%, depreciation 4%, restaurant-level profit ~18%.

segments.name: Network by brand
segments.commentary: 125 outlets at September 30, 2026: 118 company-owned and operated plus 7 franchise-owned company-operated (including one under a subsidiary). Brands: Mainland China, Asia Kitchen (mall format), Gong (premium Asian), Haka (delivery), Siciliana (Italian all-day cafe), Sweet Bengal (sweets, QSR), Walters (burgers, QSR).

guidance_outlook: Target of about 200 physical outlets by FY2030 (excluding kitchen-within-kitchen units); current count was 207 per the question, versus 125 outlets stated by management, which needs reconciliation.
Restaurant-level EBITDA target of 22-23% post Ind AS for new restaurants.
Revenue growth expected at about 20-22% a year from new openings and existing stores.
Capex of about INR 4-5 crore per restaurant; roughly INR 50 crore spend per year, with management expecting the business to become cash flow positive in coming years.
Q3 FY27: 2 new Gong openings (Delhi, Pune Koregaon Park), 3 Walters openings, and one more Siciliana, taking Gong to 4 and Siciliana to about 6 outlets.
Delivery mix expected to reach 30-35% over 2-3 years, with dine-in growing alongside.
capex_capacity: H2 FY27 openings planned across Mumbai, Delhi, Pune, Bangalore, Kolkata and Dubai, alongside renovations and brand conversions at select existing sites.
Gong re-entry into Delhi this quarter; expansion focus shifts to Delhi, Hyderabad and Bangalore alongside existing core markets of West Bengal, Mumbai, Bangalore and Pune.
Capex of about INR 50 crore a year; management said per-restaurant spend is INR 4-5 crore.
Kitchen-within-kitchen model lets one unit serve multiple brands (e.g., Mainland China, Asia Kitchen, Haka) with no extra capex or staff cost, giving three points of sale from one kitchen.
demand_pricing: Delivery is structural: management described a shift to a hybrid model in which dine-in is occasional and delivery lets brands reach consumers about 4 times a week; aggregator offers and campaigns are used to drive delivery.
Per aggregator data, about 75% of delivery customers are new to the brands and 25% are loyal customers (management does not track delivery customer data directly).
Price increases have been limited; management attributed margin protection to vendor renegotiation and buying power from multi-chain, multi-brand scale and future unit commitments.
Conversions of Mainland China to Asia Kitchen reportedly grew sales 25-30%; management targets same-store growth of 10-15% for Oriental brands.
Q3 is seasonally the strongest quarter; seasonal and marketing plans are in place.

qa_highlights.question: Company-level EBITDA and margin on pre-Ind AS basis (ex lease accounting)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said company-level EBITDA margin was 7.90% in Q2 FY27 versus 6.52% a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Unit economics for Asia Kitchen, Mainland China, Gong and Walters?
qa_highlights.answer: For Asia Kitchen, monthly throughput is INR 60-75 lakh (INR 2-2.5 lakh per day), with restaurant-level EBITDA of about 22% and restaurant-level profit of about 18% after 4% depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for the seasonally strong next quarter and new openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is optimistic on Q3 with 2-3 new restaurants launching, including 2 Gong, 3 Walters and 1 Siciliana.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term delivery mix and how the company will grow customer reach?
qa_highlights.answer: Delivery is about 29-30% of business and is expected to reach 30-35%; growth will come through kitchen-within-kitchen formats and aggregator campaigns.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material inflation and margins managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not taken a large price hike and has relied on vendor renegotiation and scale-based buying power.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for the 200-outlet target by FY2030 and per-outlet economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is mainly physical outlets across the Oriental, Siciliana and QSR brands; target restaurant EBITDA is 22-23% post Ind AS and revenue growth of 20-22%.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of rising delivery mix on margins (QSR lens)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dine-in growth should offset delivery cost pressure, so net margins should improve; 70% of business is dine-in based.

qa_highlights.question: Capex per restaurant and funding from operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-restaurant capex is INR 4-5 crore, roughly INR 50 crore a year; management expects the business to turn cash flow positive in future years.

risks_watch: Delivery mix growth may dilute restaurant margins; management's claim that dine-in growth offsets this is unverified.
Raw material inflation: price increases are limited, so margin protection depends on vendor terms.
Execution risk on about INR 50 crore annual capex and the 200-outlet FY2030 target; the outlet count (125 vs 207) needs clarification.
Same-store sales growth decelerated from 11.32% in Q1 to 8.1% in Q2.
Operating cash flow of roughly INR 50 crore cited by an analyst; cash flow positivity is pitched for future years only.
Entry into Delhi, Hyderabad and Bangalore and new brand conversions carry ramp-up risk.
534425|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, delivery and expansion, with clear quantified targets. Less specific on margin pressure from delivery and on the outlet count, and some answers were deferred or partial (e.g., competitor brand comparisons declined).
key_quotes: What we have witnessed during this particular quarter is the same-store sales growth which had been 8.1% in the quarter 2, which was 11.32% in quarter 1 and is 9.8% in H1 of FY27.

This is a complete trend because we've seen a complete shift of diner habits to more of a hybrid model where dine-in is something that people feel is achievable may be probably once a week or twice in a month.

The best plan that has worked magically for us is kitchen within kitchen concepts, where, for example, if we have an Asian kitchen, we also do deliver our other Asian brands from the very same kitchen without having any extra capex or staff costs or any other costs added to it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operational EBITDA margin rose to 8.03% from 6.81% and company-level margin to 7.90% from 6.52%, driven by vendor renegotiation and scale, but management gave no firm margin guide and delivery mix (32%) is a dilution risk.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Q3 FY27 openings are 2 Gong, 3 Walters and 1 Siciliana, and H2 FY27 openings span six cities, with a 200-outlet FY2030 target; the outlet count (125 stated vs 207 cited in the question) is unreconciled, so the base is uncertain.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides revenue growth of 20-22% a year, and same-store sales were 8.1% in Q2 (11.32% in Q1, 9.8% in H1), so growth depends on openings and some slowing in SSSG.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is about INR 50 crore a year at INR 4-5 crore per restaurant with no new capacity beyond the stated pipeline, and the 200-outlet target implies continuing spend; utilisation was not disclosed, so this rests on the stated plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 growth of 18.24% sits below the 20-22% guided, and SSSG slowed from 11.32% to 8.1%, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Same-store sales decelerated from 11.32% in Q1 to 8.1% in Q2, and delivery-led cost pressure is unresolved; the 20-22% revenue guide is above the 18.24% Q2 print.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Q3 openings include 2 Gong, 3 Walters and 1 Siciliana, and the kitchen-within-kitchen model adds brand points of sale without extra capex, but no new product line was named.

rows.label: Entry into Delhi, Hyderabad and Bangalore
rows.why: Gong re-entry into Delhi this quarter, with expansion focus shifting to Delhi, Hyderabad and Bangalore, though ramp-up risk is flagged.

rows.label: Limited price increases, margin via vendor terms
rows.why: Management has not taken a large price hike and relies on vendor renegotiation, so pricing is not a near-term margin lever.

rows.label: Kitchen-within-kitchen multi-brand model
rows.why: One kitchen serves three brands (Mainland China, Asia Kitchen, Haka) with no extra capex or staff cost, giving three points of sale per kitchen.

tone.note: Management was confident on openings, delivery growth and the 20-22% revenue and 22-23% restaurant EBITDA targets, but was vague on delivery-driven margin pressure and the outlet count (125 vs 207), and some competitor questions went unanswered; analysts pressed on margins and cash flow.

534600|2026-03.headline: JTL Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47.5% YoY to INR693 crore on a record 1,23,262 MT quarterly volume; FY27 guided to about 30% volume growth.
534600|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR693 crore (up 47.5% YoY, 47.2% QoQ), with EBITDA of INR58 crore and PAT of INR38 crore, and the company reported record quarterly and annual volumes. Management attributed the volume jump mainly to higher utilisation at the Mangaon facility and DFT structural steel pipes, with no channel-inventory gain. FY26 totals were revenue INR2,136 crore, EBITDA INR166 crore, PAT INR103 crore and volume 3,95,900 MT. Management guided to about 30% FY27 volume growth, while the 2 million tonne capacity target by FY27 was reiterated but the Aryan Bhatia question flagged that the earlier 6 lakh tonne FY27 guidance has effectively been reduced after capex delays.

financial_highlights.change: Management says Q4 EBITDA/ton ~INR4,700 per analyst question; about INR150 higher QoQ

segments.name: Mangaon facility (Maharashtra)
segments.commentary: Utilisation at about 35-40% currently; Q4 volume uplift of about 20,000-25,000 MT came entirely from Mangaon, versus a usual run rate of about 1 lakh MT a quarter. Management targets 60-70% utilisation at Mangaon this year.

segments.name: DFT structural steel pipes
segments.commentary: Main growth driver in Q4 and exports; being empanelled with customers, and ACRS certification obtained for Australia, with US and Canada being explored.

segments.name: JTL Defence (formerly RCI Industries; copper, brass, phosphor bronze alloys)
segments.commentary: Taken over in December; Q4 revenue of about INR15 crore with a stated 20% EBITDA margin, which management called not a fair steady-state number due to inventory gains. Production about 100 MT in Q4, 150 MT/month run rate now, and 500 MT/month targeted by exit FY26; FY27 revenue target INR150-200 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume growth of about 30% YoY, described as achievable on current capacity; management said it may revise upward once new capacity comes on stream.
EBITDA per ton growth of 10-15% in FY27, taking it from INR3,900 to about INR4,500-4,800; longer-term aspiration of INR5,000/ton.
Capacity target of 2 million tonnes by FY27 reiterated (from 1 million tonnes today); cold rolling/color-coated complex at Mangaon with 7 lakh tonne outlay to be fully running by end of H1 FY27.
FY27 capex of about INR100-120 crore: INR60-70 crore in H1 for remaining expansion and INR30-40 crore maintenance in H2.
ROCE expected to recover to about 25-30% in coming years as CWIP assets are capitalised; operating cash flow expected positive by FY28 (next financial year).
JTL Defence: 10-15% EBITDA margin targeted in coming quarters; defence capacity of 700-800 MT/month by FY29.
capex_capacity: Mangaon cold rolling complex (color-coated pipes, GT pipes) with 7 lakh tonne outlay; nearing completion, full running by end of H1 FY27.
Company capacity to rise from 1 million tonnes to 2 million tonnes; majority capex done, remaining about INR60-70 crore in H1 FY27.
All further capacity addition is at Maharashtra; no other facility additions planned.
Utilisation guidance not given for FY27 because new products keep starting at different rates; to be updated next quarter.
Capacity delays attributed to rains and complexity of the color-coated capex; the outlook timeline has slipped as a result.
demand_pricing: Management says market is on a good track after the November duty introduction led to price corrections, then price rises and stocking; a slowdown in the first week of the quarter due to state elections, followed by a pick-up.
Seasonality: H1 typically slower due to monsoon and new project announcements; H2 typically stronger, though the pattern has weakened in recent years.
Revenue per ton is driven by HRC cost, which has risen; color-coated products will carry higher revenue per ton once volumes start.
DFT pipes were priced at discounts in some places to push the new product, which pressured margins.
Management said there is no import steel pressure in Q1 FY27, and no inventory gain in Q4 FY26.
Export margin is not superior to domestic; export premium is roughly INR6,000-8,000/ton at the general level, with the benefit being volume scale rather than margin.

qa_highlights.question: What was the value-added share in Q4 sales mix and what drove Mangaon volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added products were about 27% of Q4 sales; Mangaon accounted for the entire 20,000-25,000 MT uplift above the usual ~1 lakh MT/quarter run rate, with DFT pipes the driver.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 volume growth guidance reliable given the Q4 run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to about 30% YoY growth on current capacity, and said it would revise the target after the new capacity comes on line; a 1-2 month slip is possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the earlier 6 lakh tonne FY27 / 9 lakh tonne FY28 guidance implied to be lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed capex delays for the color-coated complex, including rains and other factors; the outlook has been pushed out and a clearer picture is expected by end of next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is JTL Defence's margin and revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 margin of 20% was called not fair due to inventory gains; 10-15% margin is targeted, with FY27 revenue of INR150-200 crore and a 500 MT/month exit run rate.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to the end of the heavy capex cycle and expects positive operating cash flow by next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised EBITDA/ton and ROCE outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 EBITDA/ton expected at INR4,500-4,800 (10-15% growth); ROCE expected at 25-30% over the coming years as assets are capitalised.

risks_watch: Delays in the Mangaon color-coated/CRM capex: management has already slipped the timeline and the FY27 volume and capacity outlook depends on it.
Margin pressure from DFT discounting and steel price volatility (HRC cost rising); EBITDA/ton guidance is qualified as hard to pin down.
Mangaon utilisation at 35-40% now versus 60-70% target for FY26-end; DFT panel empanelment and export certifications need to keep converting.
Operating cash flow has been negative for 2-3 years and debt rose in FY26; positive OCF is only expected by FY28.
JTL Defence margin of 20% in Q4 was inventory-driven; the sustainable margin is still unproven, and the business is at an early stage after the NCLT-linked acquisition.
Q1 FY27 demand may be seasonally weak in the monsoon period; the second quarter is guided by monsoon conditions.
534600|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand, volume and the DFT and export story, but noticeably defensive on timelines: several answers conceded capex delays and declined to give utilisation or precise EBITDA/ton guidance. Management was most evasive on the revised capacity timeline and on the 6 lakh tonne FY27 figure from the prior quarter.
key_quotes: 30% is something that we'll definitely achieve.
So as the capex is delayed, the outlook is delayed as well.
There is no absolute inventory gain in this quarter.
We should be drifting close to 25% to 30% ROCE for the next years, given that a lot of our assets are not sweating and a lot of capex is happening.

rows.when: after the new capacity comes on stream, next 2-3 quarters

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Colour-coated and GT pipes from the Mangaon cold-rolling complex start ramping as the complex comes up, with value-added products already ~27% of Q4 sales mix and management noting starts at different rates.

rows.label: JTL Defence scale-up to 500 MT/month
rows.when: exit FY26 target, FY27 revenue INR150-200 crore
rows.why: Run rate is about 150 MT/month now against a 500 MT/month exit target, and a 20% Q4 margin was inventory-driven, so the 10-15% margin target is unproven.

rows.label: Export share to 15% from ~10%
rows.why: Exports are ~10% of sales with a 15% target, ACRS certification obtained for Australia and US/Canada being explored, but export margin is not superior to domestic.

rows.label: Positive operating cash flow by FY28
rows.why: Operating cash flow has been negative for 2-3 years and debt rose in FY26; management expects positive OCF as the heavy capex cycle ends, with ROCE recovering to 25-30%.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the 30% FY27 volume growth and the DFT/export story, but defensive on the colour-coated capex timeline, the 6 lakh tonne FY27 figure and utilisation and EBITDA/ton precision; analysts pushed on the slipped capacity timeline and the Defence margin.

534600|2026-06.headline: JTL Industries Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR722 crore with EBITDA INR59 crore (8.1% margin) and volumes up 17.8% YoY to 118,513 MT.
534600|2026-06.overview: JTL Industries reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA in Q1 FY27, with revenue of INR722 crore, EBITDA of INR59 crore and PAT of INR35 crore (4.9% margin). PAT absorbed INR2.8 crore of extra non-cash depreciation from the March 2026 revaluation at JTL Defence. Operational EBITDA per ton excluding other income was INR4,954, which management attributed to product mix and efficiency; it said JTL Defence added about INR200 per ton to consolidated figures. Management reiterated FY27 volume growth of at least 30%, with Mangaon capacity expansion of about 1 million tons targeted by end H1 and capex of about INR100 crore left to reach 2 million tons.

financial_highlights.change: Margin 4.9%; after INR2.8 crore extra depreciation from JTL Defence revaluation

financial_highlights.metric: Operational EBITDA per ton (ex other income)

segments.name: JTL Industries (steel tubes and pipes)
segments.commentary: EBITDA per ton about INR4,750 excluding JTL Defence; DFT structural pipes now running at 20,000-25,000 tons per quarter, roughly double the prior ~10,000 tons. Mangaon facility utilisation about 42%.

segments.name: JTL Defence (ex-RCI Industries & Technologies)
segments.commentary: Run rate about 100 MT/month in Q1, with about 120 MT in the first month of Q2. Q1 EBITDA margin about 12%, versus about 20% in Q4 which included inventory gains. Management targets 500 MT/month by Q4 FY27 and INR150 crore top line this year.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA per ton: JTL Steel tube and pipe segment ~INR4,750 seen as sustainable; management confident of reaching INR5,000 consolidated in coming quarters; FY27 target had been ~INR4,500.
FY27 volume growth of at least 30% reiterated; H2 expected stronger than H1, and management aims to exceed 30%.
Company utilisation ~55% now, targeted ~65% by year-end FY27; Mangaon utilisation to rise toward ~60%.

JTL Defence EBITDA margin long-term 15%; 10-15% band expected over time, with near-term wavering likely.

July 2026 described as an all-time high month; management expects another record quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR5,000 per ton EBITDA a one-off or structural, and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said JTL Defence added about INR200/ton; ex-Defence EBITDA was about INR4,750/ton, and INR5,000 consolidated is expected in coming quarters on the back of product mix and normalised HRC.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% volume growth guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said H2 will be stronger and it expects to exceed 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity ramp and utilisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: 7 lakh tons by end H1; the remaining 3 lakh tons (API pipes) by about the same time next year. Utilisation 50-60% in FY29; peak about 70%, possibly FY29 or FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential at peak utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1.4 million tons at INR65,000-66,000/ton, roughly INR9,100 crore on the current capex cycle.

qa_highlights.question: JTL Defence guidance and run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Run rate about 100 MT/month in Q1, about 120 MT in the first month of Q2; target 500 MT/month by Q4 FY27. Long-term margin 15%, with 10-15% expected over time.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Cycle down to about 75 days from 90; target 35-40 days by FY28, helped by dealer financing and a shift away from government receivables.

risks_watch: Export lag: exports fell to 5% of sales in Q1 on Hormuz-related container and logistics shortages; management targets 10% of sales and says the delayed INR75 crore export order book will be shipped in coming quarters if logistics improve.

Secondary-market dependence: management says demand and margins rely on the primary-secondary spread staying at INR8-12/kg versus a normal INR4-5/kg; a narrowing spread would reduce the secondary demand tailwind.

Capacity ramp timing: 7 lakh tons due by end H1 FY27, with the remaining 3 lakh tons of API pipes about a year later; management said FY29 utilisation depends on when that last leg is completed, and the 70% peak could come in FY29 or FY30.

key_quotes: Definitely, that remains intact.
So, we are very confident that consolidated level, INR5,000 is something that we'll definitely see in the coming quarters as well.
It's too soon again to maintain the exact 15% margin going ahead, but the long -term margin is 15%.
So, it's safe to say that 30% will be automobile and dealer network, 35% will be defense and the remaining will be mint factories.

rows.why: Export share fell to 5% (target 10%) on Hormuz-related container shortages, JTL Defence Q1 margin was 12% vs 20% in Q4, and the ex-Defence margin depends on HRC prices and a primary-secondary spread of INR8-12/kg versus a normal INR4-5/kg.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: JTL Defence coin and bullet shell lines (INR15 crore capex this year) change product mix, and API pipes (3 lakh t) come later, but no firm launch dates were given.

rows.label: Export order book and 10% export share target

rows.label: Working capital cycle down to 35-40 days by FY28
rows.why: Cycle fell to about 75 days from 90 days, with a target of 35-40 days by FY28, helped by dealer financing and a shift away from government receivables.

rows.why: ACRS certification (mainly Australia) is in hand and shipments have started to the US, Mexico and Canada, but volumes are not quantified and logistics remain a constraint.

534600|2026-09.headline: JTL Industries Q2 FY27 revenue rose 43.0% YoY to INR 613.8 crores, with EBITDA per ton up 19% to INR 5,053 and volume up 23.2% to 1,00,484 tons.
534600|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 43.0% YoY to INR 613.8 crores, with EBITDA up 46.5% to INR 50.8 crores at an 8.3% margin and PAT of INR 29 crores (4.7% margin). H1 delivered record volume of 2,18,997 tons (up 20.2%) and record half-year EBITDA and PAT, though reported PAT includes a INR 2.78 crore non-cash depreciation charge from the JTL Defence asset revaluation. Management is pinning H2 on new GP/colour-coated capacity in Maharashtra, which depends on an electricity connection, and on export recovery after container shortages. Working capital days rose to 83 in Q2 from about 75 in Q1, which management attributed to material stuck on the floor during monsoon and festivals.

segments.name: JTL Industries (core steel pipes)
segments.commentary: Q2 volume of 1,00,484 tons with value-added products about 28,000 tons; value-added share of sales about 30-35% in H1. Exports about 12,000 tons in H1, with about 5,000 tons shipped so far in November.

segments.name: JTL Defence
segments.commentary: Q2 volume about 356 tons, with run rate about 140 tons in October, up from about 40 tons a month at launch. Management targets 250 tons a month by December and about 750 tons in Q4; capacity mandate is 1,000 tons a month, reached by FY29. Contributes about INR 200 per ton to EBITDA per ton.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target about 4,80,000 tons (about 30% growth on about 4 lakh tons in FY26). Base case H2 about 2,60,000 tons, which is 20% above H1; an analyst read the guidance as 5.15 lakh tons, which management did not confirm.
Exit run rate of about 65,000 tons a month by year-end, from about 40,000 tons a month today, once the GP line and colour-coated complex are running.
Exports expected at about 50,000-55,000 tons in FY27, with new trial orders in Canada and the US.
EBITDA per ton of about INR 5,000-5,250 targeted for FY28, with a similar level to FY27 because new capacity will ramp up slowly.
FY28 capacity utilisation target about 55% on 1.7 million tons capacity.
Value-added share of sales expected to rise from about 30-35% to about 50% in FY28.
Working capital cycle expected to fall to about 60 days by FY28 and about 35 days by FY29, as dealer sales rise and government sales fall (from about 20% to 3%).
Capex of INR 125-150 crores expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27. Maintenance capex of INR 40-50 crores in FY28, plus about INR 75 crores for the API pipe line, with the balance in H1 FY28.
capex_capacity: GP line at Mangaon (Maharashtra): cold trials of pickling and GP lines are done; commercial production expected by end of Q3 FY27 (December). Delay blamed on monsoon and material production; the line is awaiting an enhanced electricity connection. Expected to add about 10,000 tons once running, with about 25,000-30,000 tons expected from the new capacities in Q4.
Colour-coated/CRM complex: about 4 lakh tons capacity, expected to commission in December 2026; adds about 15,000 tons a month once it starts.
API line: now expected to commission by H1 FY28 (not Q1 FY28), serving both export and domestic markets, near Nhava Sheva port.
JTL Defence: entering coin blanks and bullet cups using existing raw materials; machines expected by end of FY27.
FY28 is expected to add new capacity to a total of 1.7 million tons, and management expects utilisation of about 55%.
demand_pricing: Secondary coil priced around INR 64,000 per ton, after an INR 600-750 increase in early November. HRC prices are high, but maintenance at Tata, SAIL and AM/NS is tightening supply.
Primary-secondary gap is INR 12-20 per kg depending on gauge (2.5 mm to 1.2 mm).
Demand latency ahead of Diwali; management expects demand to pick up after 15 November and a good H2 overall.
Exports hit by container non-availability and higher freight costs. The Strait of Hormuz disruption has affected the Gulf route for 6-8 months; management said the situation is dynamic.
Working capital days rose as material built up on the floor during monsoon, Ganpati and container delays. Management is exploring a vendor finance scheme with banks for dealers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GI/GP coil capacity (due August 2026) commissioned, and is the 4 lakh ton colour-coated capacity on track for December 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: GP capacity has cold trials complete and should start commercial production by end of Q3 FY27, delayed by monsoon and material production. Management expects 25,000-30,000 tons from the new capacities in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth is expected in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Base case H2 about 2,60,000 tons, 20% above H1 of about 2,20,000 tons, giving FY27 about 4,80,000 tons, which management said is on track for 30% growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the H2 step-up depends on Maharashtra capacity timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Start depends on the electricity connection, then about 15 days of setup. Management said the GP line could add about 10,000 tons, which could start within 15 days or as late as December; run rate could reach about 65,000 tons a month by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation is targeted for FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: About 55% utilisation in FY28 on 1.7 million tons, because new capacity comes on line.

qa_highlights.question: Will the API line focus on export or domestic markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is now expected by H1 FY28; it will serve both export and domestic markets, with the choice depending on which is more viable at the time.

qa_highlights.question: What are export volumes and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 12,000 tons exported in H1, with weak Q1 due to container shortages and freight costs. About 5,000 tons shipped in November; target 50,000-55,000 tons for FY27, with new trial orders from Canada and the US.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added product share, and what is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 value-added volume about 28,000 tons; share of sales about 30-35% to rise to about 50% in FY28. Working capital days expected at about 60 by FY28 and 35 by FY29, with government sales falling from about 20% to 3%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex in H1 and H2?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 70 crores spent in H1 by the company (vs INR 76.5 crores consolidated in the prepared remarks); INR 125-150 crores expected in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA per ton is targeted for FY28-FY29, and what is the JTL Defence outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY28 EBITDA per ton of about INR 5,000-5,250. Defence adds about INR 200 per ton now and is expected to add more than INR 200 later. Defence run rate about 140 tons in October, targeting 250 tons in December and 750 tons in Q4, with 1,000 tons a month by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What are maintenance and API capex needs for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance capex INR 40-50 crores in FY28 across Industries and Defence, plus about INR 75 crores for the API pipe line, with the remainder in H1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How is demand, and what is the primary-secondary spread?
qa_highlights.answer: Secondary coil around INR 64,000 per ton after a INR 600-750 hike. Primary-secondary gap INR 12-20 per kg; demand latency before Diwali, with a good H2 expected.

534618|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 131.31% YoY to INR 1,102.40 crore with EBITDA margin of 18.76%, while FY26 order book stood at 2.83 GW peak.
534618|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 execution of 2,727 MWp, with FY26 revenue of INR 3,331.42 crore (+108.51%) and PAT of INR 478.65 crore (+109.09%). Q4 benefited from a higher share of module-inclusive orders (about 50% of execution revenue), which lifted realisation to roughly INR 20 million per MW. Order inflow was flat-to-lower (about 2.3 GW vs 2.4 GW in FY25) and the order book fell from about 3.2 GW to 2.8 GW year on year. Management guided to a sustained EBITDA margin above 15%, with FY26 margin above 19.24%, and is self-funding a 54 MWp IPP fleet plus about 227 MWp under construction.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M portfolio of 1.18 GWp, described as a recurring revenue base. No revenue figure disclosed.

segments.name: IPP
segments.commentary: 54 MWp operational, generating about INR 26 crore in FY26. About 227 MWp under construction, funded through internal accruals with no debt tied up; capex guided at INR 3-3.5 crore per MWp.

segments.name: BESS EPC
segments.commentary: Early stage: one relatively small BESS project under execution, with management expecting the revenue stream to open in FY27. Inquiries are rising.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall from about 3.2 GW to 2.8 GW, and what is the inflow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 inflow was about 2.3 GW vs 2.4 GW in FY25, with negotiations taking longer on large orders; about 36 GW of pipeline is under bilateral discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins sustainable at 19-20% vs the historical 25% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly margin depends on the customer order mix, FY26 EBITDA margin exceeded 19.24%, and 15% is a guiding threshold rather than a calculated floor.

qa_highlights.question: Does the CTUIL substation clarity issue in Rajasthan threaten new EPC awards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EPC contracts are awarded only after developers complete connectivity and land studies, so existing backlog is not affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding and IRR of the IPP strategy, and what is the 227 MWp capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IPP is funded entirely from internal accruals with no debt, and indicative capex is INR 3-3.5 crore per MWp; IRR was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is BESS cost per MW and is there any data centre revenue?

534618|2026-06.headline: Waaree Renewable Q1 FY27 revenue rose 53.23% YoY to INR924.25 crore, with PAT of INR118.97 crore (+37.7%) and unexecuted order book of INR5,300 crore.
534618|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR924.25 crore, up 53.23% YoY, with EBITDA of INR173.48 crore and PAT of INR118.97 crore. Management executed 888.81 MWp of projects in the quarter and reported an unexecuted order book of INR5,300 crore including T&D, with O&M portfolio at 1.15 GWp. The quarter included completion of a 55% stake acquisition in Associated Power Structures Private Limited (APSPL), a Vadodara T&D EPC and tower maker, which consolidated for about 12 days; management said consolidated margin dipped on lower-margin T&D while standalone EPC margin improved. Management declined to give formal guidance on most items.

segments.name: Solar EPC (standalone)

segments.name: APSPL (T&D, 55% stake)
segments.commentary: Integrated substation and transmission EPC plus fabrication and galvanisation, capacity 108,000 MT per annum, executed over 10,461 circuit km of transmission line. Consolidated margin dilution attributed to this business; T&D pipeline cited at about INR20,000 crore, with typical execution of 18-24 months.

segments.name: BESS EPC
segments.commentary: Order of about 1.5 GWh (reported as roughly 300 MW / 1,400-1,520 MWh across combined orders); unexecuted BESS value about INR200 crore. Margin to be in line with company average at order intake.

segments.name: IPP
segments.commentary: 82 MWp of IPP assets in financials; pipeline of about 198 MWp of small plants (20-25 MW each), for Waaree Renewable Technologies itself.

534618|2026-09.headline: Waaree RTL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 36.53% YoY to INR1,057.84 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.12% as solar EPC execution dropped to 456 MWp.
534618|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was INR1,057.84 crore, up 36.53% YoY, with EBITDA of INR159.98 crore (15.12% margin) and PAT of INR81.48 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,982.09 crore (+43.84%), with EBITDA of INR333.46 crore (16.82%) and PAT of INR200.44 crore. This quarter was the first full consolidation of Associated Power Structures (APSPL), the T&D subsidiary, which added debt-funded acquisition finance costs and depreciation. Solar EPC execution slowed to 456 MWp in Q2 from about 889-922 MW in earlier comparison periods, which management attributed to land and connectivity handover delays on the developer side; 1.7 GW of new orders were booked in the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: approx. 30% decline per analyst question; not stated by management

financial_highlights.change: as cited by analyst; not disputed by management

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Executed 456 MWp in Q2 FY27 and 1,345 MWp in H1 FY27. Management says solar EPC should remain the key growth driver and expects margin above 15%.

segments.name: T&D (APSPL)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from Q2 FY27; margin currently about 9-10%, below solar EPC. Management said FY26 revenue was close to INR2,000 crore and the order book is INR2,200 crore plus as of Q2; order pipeline above INR20,000 crore.

segments.name: IPP and O&M
segments.commentary: Operational IPP portfolio is 82.82 MWp; O&M portfolio has reached 1.5 GWp, which management says adds recurring revenue.

segments.name: BESS EPC
segments.commentary: Management cites rising inquiries to add BESS to existing solar plants and in new orders; no BESS revenue or margin figures given.

Solar EPC EBITDA margin expected to stay above 15%, per management's estimate.
T&D margin expected to improve from 9-10% as scale and synergies with Waaree Renewables and APSPL build; visibility expected from the coming quarter.

demand_pricing: Management says India had about 299 GW of renewable capacity and about 171 GW of solar as of 30 Sep 2026; India added about 44 GW of solar last year and over 20 GW in H1 FY27.

Green Energy Corridor Phase 3 approved with about INR1.86 lakh crore outlay, targeting 135 GW RE evacuation and 50 GWh BESS by FY32-33.

Management says the majority of solar orders are utility scale and that most customers are repeat group companies via bilateral discussions. No pricing or realisation figures were disclosed despite analyst questions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did solar execution fall to about 456 MW in Q2 versus about 889-922 MW earlier, and what is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited land and connectivity handover delays at the developer end on some projects, which it said are customer-side. Projects will be executed over the next 3-4 quarters. No FY27 execution target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why are T&D margins lower and when will they improve?
qa_highlights.answer: T&D margin is currently about 9-10%, below solar EPC. Management expects improvement in coming quarters from scale, efficiency and synergies with Waaree Renewables and APSPL.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost and depreciation rise sharply, and when will APSPL offset them?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation is mostly from the acquisition. Finance cost rose because the acquisition was debt-funded. Management said APSPL's contribution should cover the loan over time, without a date.

qa_highlights.question: Is the debt level permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the loan was taken for the APSPL acquisition and it will look to reduce debt as operations progress. No target leverage level was given.

qa_highlights.question: Are there working capital, bank guarantee, or NFB constraints on bidding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no constraints; limits are available for new bids. No specific limit amounts were disclosed.

risks_watch: Solar EPC execution reliance on developers' land and grid connectivity readiness; the Q2 slowdown was attributed to this.
Margin dilution from the lower-margin T&D business (9-10%) and higher debt-related finance cost and depreciation after the APSPL acquisition.
Q2 PAT down about 30% YoY as cited by analyst, despite 36.53% revenue growth; management did not dispute the figure.

Order conversion: INR5,500 crore order book depends on developer readiness and conversion over 3-4 quarters; the solar EPC book of INR3,300 crore is smaller than the INR5,300-crore book cited in the prior call.

534680|2026-03.headline: SRG Housing Finance Q4 FY26 PAT rose 50% YoY to INR 9 crore; FY26 AUM crossed INR 1,000 crore at INR 1,042 crore, up 37%.
534680|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 net interest income of about INR 28 crore (up 33% YoY) and NIM of 11.28%, with PAT of about INR 9 crore (up 50%). For FY26, NII was INR 98.26 crore (up 31%), PAT INR 32.49 crore (up 33%), and disbursements INR 443.54 crore (up 45%). Asset quality was stable, with GNPA at 1.77% and NNPA at 0.65%, and the company was upgraded to A- Stable by Acuité. Management guided to FY27 disbursements of about INR 600 crore and AUM of INR 1,400 to 1,500 crore, and flagged a possible equity raise later in the year.

financial_highlights.change: vs about 46.6% a year earlier (per analyst)

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: About 94% of the loan book is from rural and semi-urban markets; Rajasthan and Gujarat together make up about 77% of AUM per an individual investor's calculation, which management did not dispute. Operations span six states and one union territory with 96 branches. Expansion is focused on the southern states (Tamil Nadu, Telangana) with 10 to 15 new branches planned by year-end.

segments.name: Customer mix
segments.commentary: About 79% of customers are self-employed (one analyst cited about 75% of the loan book). Around 97% of EMI collections come through the banking channel, and cash collections are 4% to 5%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target of about INR 600 crore (per CEO), against INR 443.54 crore in FY26.
AUM expected at INR 1,300 to 1,400 crore, with an INR 1,500 crore stretch target by the end of FY27.
Cost of borrowing expected to fall from 10.88% to about 10.70% over the next one to two years. The call initially cited 63% to 61%, which was corrected by a company note.
ROE guidance of 12% to 13%, with a longer-term aim of about 18% per management, depending on the housing market.
Two-year AUM target of about INR 2,000 crore, and INR 2,000 to 2,500 crore within two and a half to three years. Long-term vision of INR 10,000 to 20,000 crore.
Equity raise considered in Q4 FY27 if the year progresses well; otherwise in Q1 or Q2 FY28, once leverage crosses 5x to 6x (bank comfort level, versus 12x NHB limit).
capex_capacity: Branch expansion of 10 to 15 new branches in Tamil Nadu and Telangana by end of FY27; no new branches planned in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan or MP.
Target AUM per branch of about INR 25 crore, implying about INR 110 crore per branch at scale (management target, not a stated timeline).
Ongoing ERP overhaul and digital transformation (SRG SRAJAN); AI-based calling in development, with no cost incurred yet per management. IT headcount increased.
Capital adequacy of 38.62% gives headroom for growth, but leverage is expected to rise toward the 5x to 6x bank comfort limit as AUM grows.
demand_pricing: Average ticket size rose 41% YoY to INR 15.44 lakh in Q4, which management attributed to higher land and construction costs and changing customer aspirations rather than a shift in customer profile.
Average LTV rose to about 50.7% from about 46.6% a year earlier; management said this reflects product nature, not a deliberate strategy.
Management said there is no meaningful competitive pressure from larger lenders on pricing, as the customer profile is unchanged.
Management said the West Asia conflict and weaker monsoon are not materially affecting the book, citing diversified, small-ticket self-employed borrowers.

qa_highlights.question: Would the new branches' scale-up and the INR 500 crore disbursement guidance hold for the next 12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Disbursement target was raised to about INR 600 crore for FY27; AUM expected at INR 1,300 to 1,400 crore, with INR 1,500 crore as the stretch. New branches focus on Tamil Nadu and Telangana (10 to 15 branches).

qa_highlights.question: How will the rating upgrade affect cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects borrowing cost to decline; the call's 63% to 61% figure was a transcription error. The corrected expectation is a fall from 10.88% to about 10.70% over one to two years, with no firm guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: What ROE is the company targeting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 12% to 13% for the coming period, with about 18% over time as the housing market improves.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GNPA high in Rajasthan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no specific cause; Rajasthan is the largest state by portfolio size, so its share of GNPA is higher, and no concern was seen in the state.

qa_highlights.question: Is capitalisation adequate for AUM growth, and how is equity being raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding access has widened after the upgrade (banks, equity markets, NCDs). Leverage can reach 12x under NHB rules, but banks cap it at 5x to 6x, so equity may be raised in Q4 FY27 or Q1/Q2 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Stage 1 about 93% of the book, and how does collection work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Stage 1 is 93.05%, Stage 2 5.18% and Stage 3 1.77%. About 14% to 15% of cheques bounce, about 90% of which are recovered within the month, and around 97% of amounts are recovered within 30 days of a bounce.

risks_watch: Rajasthan GNPA trend: the company said portfolio size, not credit issues, explains the figure, but the state remains a large share of AUM.

Execution of the southern expansion (10 to 15 branches) and new management hires, which could raise costs and cost of borrowing in the near term.
Concentration: Rajasthan and Gujarat together account for about 77% of AUM per an investor calculation; management expects this to even out over two to three years.

534680|2026-06.headline: SRG Housing management denies Rs 400 crore siphoning report and NHB red flag; no hard financials or audit timeline given on the 16 Sep 2026 call.
534680|2026-06.overview: This was a clarification call, not an earnings call, held after an Economic Times article (10 Sep 2026) alleged Rs 400 crore of promoter-linked diversion and NPA manipulation. The MD denied all allegations and said the NHB red flag is part of a routine supervisory audit that began in July 2026, with no reasons yet shared. He cited a 39.21% capital adequacy ratio, 25% QoQ PAT growth, and no delays on lender obligations, but gave no amount for collections or liquidity. New disbursements have been slowed, the board has resolved to convert from a housing finance company to an NBFC, and promoters raised their stake by 1%.

segments.name: Housing loans (core)
segments.commentary: Management says part disbursements continue but new business is slow and sanctions from banks are pending. Management said it has not shared exact disbursement or sanction figures.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a slowdown in Q2 FY27 from fresh sanctions and disbursements, with Q3 and Q4 'good'.

Management expects the NHB audit to close 'soon'; asked whether it would close in 1-2 months, the MD said '100%'. He also said the audit could take 15-20 days, while the timeline was not firmly committed.
Board has resolved to convert the company from a housing finance company to an NBFC; management said this takes at least 6 months and needs NOCs from all lenders.
Management said the company has no shortfall in operations and that promoters can infuse 100% of capital if needed.
capex_capacity: Slowdown in fresh sanctions and disbursements; part disbursements of existing sanctions continue, and the MD said he is slowing them further if needed.
Pending sanctions from banks are held until the red flag is removed.
Proposed NBFC conversion: management rejected a subsidiary route, saying the same work should not be done in two companies.
demand_pricing: Management said there is no shortage of demand and the slowdown is precautionary.
Management said there are zero promoter-related or related-party loans in the book.
No pricing, yield, or competitive commentary was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the account red flagged, and can a third-party re-inspection be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD said the company does not know the reasons; NHB does not share them until the audit closes. He said a third-party re-inspection after the audit is 'not an issue'.

qa_highlights.question: Liquidity: what are monthly collections and cash balances?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections exceed obligations, but no figure was given. The MD said there is a 2-3 month repayment buffer, and that liquidity data was sent to the rating agency.

qa_highlights.question: Have lenders been told or has any recall happened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it met each lender individually, that none has sought a recall, and that there has been no delay on any obligation.

qa_highlights.question: Did NHB communicate specific observations?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The MD said there has been no formal communication on the findings, and that observations from the last audit are internal and not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Can the promoter infuse capital if needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the MD said promoters can put in '100%' of required capital, but there is no current shortfall.

qa_highlights.question: Will you share collection efficiency and liquidity data regularly?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD said a liquidity statement was sent to the rating agency from March 2020; he declined to give the monthly collection amount and said he would send the liquidity position only up to March.

risks_watch: NHB red flag remains open; reasons and audit findings are not yet disclosed and no completion date is committed.
Acuite has placed the rating under watch; management says there is no downgrade.
Management provided no audited data on collections, NPAs, or the Rs 400 crore allegation; the 1,100 crore and 130 crore book figures given on the call are inconsistent.
Several lenders requested a group lender meeting; management said only 'we will see'.
Sanctions are on hold, and an RBI-mandated 90-day disbursement timeline was raised but not confirmed.
The NBFC conversion needs at least 6 months and lender NOCs; management gave no product or funding details.

534748|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19.45% QoQ to INR 287.70 crore and EBITDA margin to 17.41%, with net profit at INR 12.37 crore.
534748|2026-03.overview: Total income for Q4 FY26 was INR 287.70 crore, up 19.45% QoQ from INR 240.86 crore. EBITDA rose 118.12% QoQ to INR 50.10 crore, with margin up 788 bps to 17.41%. Net profit was INR 12.37 crore versus INR 2.28 crore in Q3, with a 4.30% net margin. For FY26, total income was INR 1,066.42 crore, EBITDA INR 138.03 crore and net profit INR 26.99 crore. Management said it redeemed INR 43.19 crore of NCDs in one tranche and cut debt by nearly INR 68 crore over the last two quarters.

segments.name: TMT rebar / long products (Simhadri brand)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 rebar volume was 49,760 tonnes, up from about 39,000 t in Q3. Management said the average EBITDA per tonne was about INR 9,000-9,500 in the last quarter versus about INR 6,000 in earlier quarters, and about INR 6,800-7,000 on a yearly average.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Power segment revenue fell in FY26. Management attributed this to kiln refurbishments; it expects data-centre tie-ups and capacity expansion to improve consumption.

segments.name: Logistics (SEIL Logistics and Infra Company)
segments.commentary: A subsidiary formed to run a private freight terminal and logistics at Visakhapatnam, with railway sidings. MoUs with the Andhra Pradesh government cover about 150 acres adjacent to the existing land.

guidance_outlook: Management said Q4 FY26 is 'fine' but later years should be better; it expects steady margins while the market stays buoyant.
Management expects FY27 volumes to roughly double once the reheating furnace and capacity expansion come on stream from Q2 FY27, with capacity mostly doubled.
Sustainable EBITDA guidance given as about INR 7,000 per tonne on average volumes of 40,000-50,000 tonnes per quarter.

Finance cost is expected at about INR 12-13 crore per quarter, not below 10, after the new loan costs and trade finance charges fall away. Refinancing is targeted to bring the cost of debt to about 9%.

Existing capex (reheating furnace, furnace refurbishment, kiln work) is to be completed in FY27. New greenfield capex for the 1 million tonne green steel plant is about one year away, pending groundbreaking and the strategic investor's inputs.
Pledged shares are expected to be released once refinancing is complete and IMR funds are received.
capex_capacity: A reheating furnace is being installed, expected to start from Q2 FY27 and to add about 50,000 tonnes of new bar capacity. Management said it will raise rolling mill efficiency by 30-40%.
Billet and rebar capacities were raised by about 44-45% at the end of FY25. Utilisation is about 46-47% for rebar and 55-56% for billet, with a target of 70-75% in FY27.
Expansions already under way are expected to be operational by end-July 2026.
Land bank: about 400-450 acres existing; another 150 acres targeted for the logistics park and 150 acres for steel manufacturing. MoUs cover a 1 million tonne green steel plant.
Planned capex and debt paydown are to be funded from INR 300 crore of share warrant money from IMR Group and internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Management said the Indian steel outlook is strong, citing infrastructure, housing, railways, defence and import substitution. It also said Andhra Pradesh and Visakhapatnam projects (Google AI hub, ArcelorMittal, Amaravati) are sources of demand, and that the company is an approved vendor for them.
April 2026 sales were described as 'great' and May as slightly weaker due to heatwave and the war situation. Management expects a June recovery.
Management said the company is largely insulated from the ongoing war, except for some diesel cost in transport. Coal, iron ore and scrap are sourced locally.
The company was re-empanelled under MES for TMT bar supplies to the Ministry of Defence.

qa_highlights.question: What does the company plan to fund its capacity growth and reduce its debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has MoUs with state governments for expansion and a 1 million tonne green steel plant. Project reports are pending, and the plan is to announce them once formalised.

qa_highlights.question: When is the balance payment expected from IMR on the share warrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 300 crore warrant subscription is expected within about six months and will fund growth, including green steel.

qa_highlights.question: What is the finance cost trend, and why did it rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 finance cost was INR 7.50 crore, not INR 17 crore. The analyst then cited Q3 at INR 13 crore and Q4 at INR 17 crore; management attributed the difference to new loan processing costs and supplier trade finance. Term debt has fallen from about INR 350 crore to INR 250 crore, and current debt is about INR 270 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What were rebar volumes and what is the FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 rebar sales were 49,760 tonnes. Management said FY27 capacity is expected to roughly double from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity utilisation and when will it reach 85-90%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebar utilisation is about 46-47% and billet about 55-56%. Management expects 70-75% in FY27 after the reheating furnace is commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the company's shares 100% pledged, and will this change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pledge is linked to past bank exposure. It expects the pledge to be released after refinancing, to a debt cost of about 9%, and once IMR funds are received.

risks_watch: Debt and funding: the IMR INR 300 crore warrant money has not yet been received and is expected in about six months. Refinancing to about 9% is planned but not yet closed.
Finance cost: management guided to INR 12-13 crore per quarter, which is well above the analyst's expected single-digit level.
Margin sustainability: the EBITDA margin of 17.41% is above the earlier 11-12% range, and management called the steel market 'buoyant' but cyclical.
Execution: FY27 volume doubling depends on the reheating furnace and expansions running from Q2 FY27.
Demand softness in May 2026 due to heatwave and war-related conditions.
Governance: management agreed to consider quarterly investor calls, which are not yet in place.

534816|2026-03.headline: Indus Towers Q4 FY26: reported EBITDA INR 44.6bn (+1.6% YoY, 55.1% margin) and FY26 final dividend of INR 14/share distributing full-year FCF of INR 37.6bn.
534816|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 81bn (+4.8% YoY) and core rental revenue INR 53.1bn (+5.4% YoY), with co-locations up 5.6% YoY. Reported EBITDA was flat-to-up YoY but down 1% QoQ, held back by a Q4 one-time settlement hit to revenue, a Q3 positive one-off in other expenses, and higher seasonal maintenance spend. Full-year PAT fell 28.1% YoY to INR 71.4bn because FY25 carried a INR 51bn receivables write-back; normalised EBITDA and PAT grew 11.4% and 13%. The Board recommended a final dividend of INR 14/share, distributing the full FY26 free cash flow, with management guiding to a steady and progressive payout going forward.

financial_highlights.value: INR 11.1bn in Q4; INR 37.6bn in FY26

segments.name: Towers and co-locations (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 added 4,892 macro towers and 6,192 co-locations, taking the base to about 264,500 towers and 428,000 co-locations (+6.1% and +5.6% YoY). Tenancy ratio stable at 1.62; leaner-tower co-locations exceed 14,000, portfolio about 442,000 including leaner towers.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: Energy revenue fell QoQ on cost optimisation and seasonal energy cost decline; energy margin -3.6% in Q4 vs -5.2% a year earlier. Solar access added at about 2,500 sites in Q4, taking the total to about 42,400; diesel consumption down about 7% YoY.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Operating licence secured in Zambia with on-ground execution starting; Uganda and Nigeria in final regulatory stages. Commercial frameworks and initial orders in place with the anchor customer; capex for Africa described as not significant initially.

segments.name: Non-tower / DAS / IBS
segments.commentary: Company says it reached leadership in IBS in Q4; DAS deployments picked up in metros, tunnels and highways. No figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Final dividend of INR 14/share recommended; management says the endeavour is steady and progressive distribution, with no minimum payout formula (dividend policy: FCF distributed at year-end, subject to working capital).
Management does not give forward numbers; says order book is healthy for the next few quarters with growth-oriented capex (about 70% of capex is growth, about 25% replacement/maintenance).
Full-year EBITDA margin said to be in line with the 55%-plus expectation.
Africa tower deployment expected to begin soon in Zambia, with ramp-up as approvals come through in Uganda and Nigeria.
capex_capacity: Q4 tower additions 4,892 and co-location additions 6,192; FY26 full-year additions about 15,200 towers and 22,500 co-locations.
Over 85% of sites digitally connected (fuel sensors, backhaul monitoring, smart meters, power equipment).
About 531,000 5G BTSs installed in the base; growth expected from loading on existing towers, with selective tower footprint expansion later.
Management flagged supply-side tightness in tower materials linked to LPG availability and West Asia conflict, affecting deployment timelines and costs.
demand_pricing: Core revenue growth muted by Q4 FY25 one-time reconciliation benefit (about 2.1pp of base) and a Q4 FY26 one-time settlement; management cited organic service revenue growth of about 5-5.5% YoY after adjusting for an Airtel tower acquisition.
Annual escalations of about 2.5% cited as a revenue driver.
Management said a major customer's contract expiries affect only a very small portion of the portfolio; some Jio tenancies have expired but are still operating, with minor churn.
Management expects tenancy ratio trend to change as second anchor customer ramps; cannot give a directional outlook.
Diesel-price pass-through is said to be billed on actuals with no lag; industrial (bulk) diesel price rise does not affect the company's retail diesel purchases.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about the FCF from last year's VI dues reversal, now that FY26 FCF is almost fully distributed, and what capex guidance applies?
qa_highlights.answer: Board evaluated FCF and desired debt levels and chose to distribute FY26 FCF; capex about 70% growth, 25% replacement, and no forward numbers given, with a healthy order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a formal dividend policy, and is there a minimum payout?
qa_highlights.answer: Policy is on the website: the Board considers distributing year-end FCF, subject to working capital and other conditions; no minimum payout amount is specified.

qa_highlights.question: Why has FY25 cash not been released, given earlier comments about distributing it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Board did not compartmentalise cash by year; it assessed full FCF and debt levels, with total distributions of about INR 37-38bn.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 maintenance spend a one-off or a structural reset as towers age?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonality (clear-weather Q3/Q4 and pre-monsoon preparation) plus a deliberate tower-strengthening programme; said cost per tower has fallen over 3-4 years and the base is not reset.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the sequential EBITDA decline and per-tower drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 revenue hit by a one-time settlement; Q3 had a positive one-off in other expenses; network maintenance up 5.6% QoQ; full-year margin still on track at 55%-plus.

qa_highlights.question: Why are single-tenancy tower additions rising and what is the Vodafone rollout impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said co-location additions exceeded tower additions in Q3 and Q4; some towers move from other tower companies to Indus (net addition), so a direct split is not possible.

qa_highlights.question: When will Africa operations start, and will NOC be local or in India?
qa_highlights.answer: First tower in Zambia expected very soon, well within six months; NOC location not yet decided.

qa_highlights.question: Do the Jio tower contract expiries lead to churn, and were renewals at the same terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Some expired tenancies still operate; very minor percentage churned; renewals continue on the same terms, with no incremental concessions mentioned in response.

risks_watch: Customer financial health and non-renewal of expired tenancies (management says a small portion of the portfolio), and tenancy ratio trend as second anchor customer ramps.
Supply-chain tightness and cost inflation from the West Asia conflict and LPG availability, affecting tower deployments and costs.
Maintenance cost trend on the aging portfolio, and whether Q4 maintenance spending repeats.
Dividend sustainability versus capex and Africa investment, plus debt levels after the Airtel tower acquisition funding.
Energy margin (-3.6% in Q4) under diesel and grid price changes; smart meter mandate by CEA.

534816|2026-06.headline: Indus Towers Q1 FY27 gross revenue rose 4.6% YoY to INR 84.3 bn; EBITDA up 3.0% to INR 45.2 bn, margin 53.6%.
534816|2026-06.overview: Gross revenue grew 4.6% YoY to INR 84.3 bn, with core rental up 5.2% YoY to INR 53.7 bn on tower and colocation additions. Reported EBITDA rose 3.0% YoY to INR 45.2 bn, but margin fell 1.5 pp YoY to 53.6%; adjusting for a prior-year INR 0.9 bn write-back, EBITDA grew 5.2%. Energy margin was -4.6% (seasonal, plus past-period settlements), while diesel consumption fell 13% YoY. Management reiterated a firm order book for 3-4 quarters and began Africa rollouts guidance for next quarter, with economics still undisclosed. The CFO also announced his departure after five years.

segments.commentary: Added about 4,200 colocations, taking base to about 432,300 (+5.1% YoY). Incremental tenancy ratio about 1.3-1.4 over the last 2-4 quarters.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: Energy revenue rose 9.5% QoQ on seasonal diesel use and higher diesel prices; diesel consumption down over 13% YoY; solar access on about 46,000 sites (about 3,700 added); solar installed base 259 MW.

qa_highlights.question: Is Airtel in-sourcing towers a risk to tenancies on existing towers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it executes whatever order book it gets, sees no net tenancy loss from the strategy, and sees Africa anchor tenancy and synergies as value-creating.

qa_highlights.answer: Growth capex includes replacement, maintenance, solar and battery spend, so dividing total capex by towers added is misleading; offline walkthrough offered.

qa_highlights.question: Why is energy margin under pressure and how do battery investments earn returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Seasonality and past-period settlements drove the energy margin decline; battery capex is recovered through customer payments that replace diesel pass-through, so the revenue continues in a different form.

qa_highlights.question: Why is maintenance capex roughly doubled?

534816|2026-09.headline: Indus Towers Q2 FY27: EBITDA up 2.5% QoQ to INR46.3bn (54.4% margin); tenancy ratio improved to 1.63 on 7,900 co-location additions.
534816|2026-09.overview: Revenue rose 1% QoQ to INR85.2bn and core rental revenue rose 1.3% QoQ to INR54.5bn, with YoY growth of 4% and 3.9% respectively. Reported EBITDA grew 2.5% QoQ to INR46.3bn, and the margin expanded 80bps QoQ to 54.4%, though Q2 FY26 included about INR2bn of write-backs (YoY EBITDA growth adjusted for this was 5.2%). Energy margin improved to -3.6% from -4.6% in Q1 and -4.8% a year ago, helped by an 11% YoY drop in diesel consumption. Management highlighted a strong order book, Africa rollouts starting in Zambia and Uganda, and a strong co-location quarter, while declining to give forward tower or Africa numbers.

segments.name: India towers and co-location
segments.commentary: Added about 2,900 macro towers (+5.6% YoY, base ~270,500) and 7,900 co-locations (+5.9% YoY, base ~440,200). Tenancy ratio rose to 1.63 from 1.62; total co-locations including leaner sites about 454,200.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Towers deployed in Zambia and Uganda in late Q2, with revenue started. Nigeria deployment to begin in the current quarter; Airtel is the anchor customer. Management says early capex per tower is within plan but gave no figures yet.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: Diesel consumption down 11% YoY. Solar sites rose by about 3,000 in Q2 to 49,000; installed solar capacity 297 MW from 259 MW in Q1.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance on tower additions; management pointed to a strong order book for Q3 and beyond across towers and tenancies.
Revenue growth to track tower and tenancy growth; full-quarter revenue from Q2 additions expected to show up in subsequent quarters.
Africa rollouts to ramp up in H2 FY27; metrics to be disclosed in subsequent quarters.
Energy cost initiatives (solar, lithium-ion batteries, diesel optimization) described as structural, with more room to go; management declined to give margin guidance.
New customer onboarding and renewals continue at a minimum 10-year tenure.

535693|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 50% to INR365 crore and PAT nearly doubled to INR59.61 crore, with an INR1,600 crore order book (4.46x FY26 revenue).
535693|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) revenue from operations of INR365 crore, up 50% from INR242 crore, with EBITDA of INR83.45 crore (margin 22.83%, up 280 bps) and PAT of INR59.61 crore (up roughly 100%). Management attributed the gain to Q2 and Q3 monsoon-quarter execution, where revenue reached INR180 crore versus INR70 crore a year earlier. Q4 standalone revenue was INR93.93 crore, PBT INR16.79 crore, PAT INR14.78 crore and EPS INR5.09. This was the company's first earnings call, and Q&A covered order book conversion, real estate plans, promoter pledge, and JV revenue sharing.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR19.58 crore (about 5-7% of total per an analyst's figure; management said about 10%), with segment profit INR16.70 crore vs INR14.75 crore last year. 535693|2026-06.headline: Brahmaputra Infra Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.24% YoY to Rs 110.79 crore, with PAT up 9.57% to Rs 16.48 crore.
535693|2026-06.overview: Consolidated top line crossed Rs 110 crore for the first time in a quarter, up 20.24% YoY and 17.95% QoQ, driven by EPC activity. Consolidated EBITDA rose 13.08% YoY to Rs 25.15 crore, while PAT grew 9.57% YoY to Rs 16.48 crore. Management said Rs 429 crore of orders were booked in the quarter and the order book stands at about Rs 1,600 crore, with roughly 50% yet to start. Management also addressed cash conversion, pointing to Rs 165 crore of OCCPS repayments from June 2027 and arbitration recoveries of Rs 200-225 crore expected over two years.

segments.commentary: Consolidated real estate revenue Rs 6.33 crore, up about 65% YoY from Rs 3.82 crore; real estate PBT Rs 5.40 crore. Management cites 85-90% margins for this segment.

guidance_outlook: Management targets FY27 order book of about Rs 2,500 crore by year-end, against roughly Rs 1,600 crore currently.
Management expects a historic top line and bottom line in FY27 and said it will keep EPC growth at the rate of the last 2-3 years.
Management expects no margin compression for FY28-FY29 and says growth will come from higher order inflow.
Around 80% of the Rs 800 crore-plus order book to be executed over 18 months is expected to bill in the first year, per management.

demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 order inflow of Rs 429 crore across railways, roads and highway maintenance; over Rs 300 crore booked in the last 75 days.

Management says it is selective on bids and avoids hyper-competitive volume work; about 50% of the order book is outside Northeast India.
Wayside Amenities (NHAI land leases, 30-year) bids pending; results expected next month.
Management states that cash-flow issues are concentrated in pre-2020 legacy projects now in arbitration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the executable order book for FY27 and FY28, and what is the bid pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book of Rs 1,600 crore plus, executable over 18-30 months; bid pipeline about Rs 2,500 crore, focused on railways, institutional buildings and flood/slope protection.

qa_highlights.question: How will cash conversion improve given large receivables, WIP, retention and OCCPS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no stuck-up money or slow-moving WIP on post-2020 projects; debtors about Rs 15-20 crore with 45-90 day billing cycles. Pre-2020 legacy projects in arbitration: over Rs 100 crore monetised in five years, about Rs 150 crore still pending, with Rs 200-225 crore expected over two years including bank guarantee releases. OCCPS of Rs 165 crore repayment starts June 2027 and runs to 2034; management plans to swap OCCPS with arbitration awards.

qa_highlights.question: Is real estate a core hedge or to be divested?
qa_highlights.answer: No plans to divest; both segments to operate jointly. Mall development is planned to start by year-end with rental income of Rs 50-60 crore at full three-phase build-out.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Assam floods on ongoing projects?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of works are outside Northeast and unaffected; some Upper Assam projects were affected, but emergency variation works offset this with no negative impact on billing or turnover.

qa_highlights.question: How is pan-India expansion being pursued and does it include light real estate?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is selective, project-by-project; West Bengal is a strategic target. Asset-light real estate via NHAI Wayside Amenities bids is being pursued, with a large Assam bid awaiting results.

qa_highlights.answer: Current 12-15% effective rate reflects Section 43B deductions on past interest; expected to move to 20-22% after 2028.

Plans to repay the INR165 crores OCCPS in quarterly instalments of about INR60 crores a year starting June 2027, targeting full repayment within about 2.5 years.
capex_capacity: Joint venture investment of INR7.9 crores in H1 to support execution of new orders.
Common infrastructure (crusher installations, equipment procurement, branch offices) planned across high-priority states to lower costs.
Consolidation of JV borrowings from 1 April 2026 after the company obtained operational and financial control of a JV that had completed about 50% of its work.
Bank guarantees outstanding INR82.57 crores as of 30 September 2026.
demand_pricing: Order inflow: four projects worth INR317 crores in Q2, including a major bridge over River Ravi (Punjab), Turga Pumped Storage Project (West Bengal, new pumped storage segment), and AHI DMS healthcare renovation (Assam).

Bidding is restricted to technically complex projects with fewer than four to five qualified bidders; the West Bengal pumped storage win had three other qualified bidders. Management says margins outside the Northeast are similar to Northeast margins.
Government tightening of qualification criteria is reportedly disqualifying 30-40% of bidders, which management expects to lift its success rate.
Management says the company has received about INR1,200 crores of new contracts in the last 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H1 cash conversion weak relative to PAT, and what is H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a working capital cycle of about 90 days and reinvestment of receipts into new projects, working capital and capex; it said no fresh debt was raised and cash balances were kept low. Trade payables were reduced by INR50 crores and operating cash flow stayed positive, per the CFO remarks.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost fall and what debt levels are comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Unsecured loans were repaid and the term loan has fallen from about INR32 crores to INR12 crores, expected to be nil by FY27. Fund-based exposure is CC INR104 crores and term loan INR12 crores; the INR165 crores OCCPS is non-cash in P&L terms and repayment starts June 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How much arbitration money is due and when?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR35 crores principal (INR50 crores including interest) decided in the company's favour, of which an INR10 crore award and INR7.5 crore TDA claim were received in H1. An IPL Airport Authority project award of about INR29-30 crores is expected within 6-7 months; about INR115 crores remains pending, with INR40-50 crores expected in the next 10 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings rise between March and September 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects consolidation of JV borrowings from 1 April 2026, after the company took over operational and financial control of a JV that had completed about 50% of its work.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Guwahati mall unit sale dispute?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an arbitrator was appointed over disagreement but is now suspended and discussions are ongoing on a mutual basis; no timeline was given. The units are recorded as investment property.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion beyond the Northeast and margins there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a core share of the order book will stay in the Northeast; new wins in West Bengal and Punjab are the first outside it, with more West Bengal bids pending. It says non-NE margins are similar to NE margins.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of the 31% revenue growth and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 50% of the order book starts in the current month and the working season is favourable, so a sharp H2 revenue rise is expected. It plans to hold margins and does not want to trade margin for volume; it declined to give specific numeric guidance.

risks_watch: Cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow was weak relative to PAT, and the working capital cycle is about 90 days.
Arbitration recovery depends on court and department timelines; about INR115 crores is pending, including a Delhi High Court matter that may take about 2 years.
OCCPS repayment of about INR60 crores per year from June 2027 requires cash generation or refinancing.
Guwahati mall unit sale dispute has no stated resolution timeline.
Revenue ramp-up in H2 depends on execution of about 50% of the order book starting from November 2026.
Annual report for FY26 is expected in the first week of December 2026.
