535754|2026-03.headline: Ambuja Cements FY26: record 73.7 Mt volumes, but Q4 cost ~INR4,500/t; FY27 volume guided ~80 Mt and cost cut of INR250/t targeted.
535754|2026-03.overview: Ambuja's Q4 FY26 call (consolidating Orient Cement for 11 months and Penna from August 2025) showed record FY26 volumes of 73.7 Mt, up 16% YoY, with normalized FY26 EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (INR887/t, up 12%) and PAT of INR2,647 crore (up 17%). Management said Q4 cost per tonne was about INR4,500, above its earlier INR4,000 exit aspiration, due to acquired-asset underperformance, freight, packing, fuel, branding and repairs. Management called the reset partial: FY28 capacity targets slip toward FY30, capex is cut to INR6,000-6,500 crore for FY27, and the company says cost peaked in Q4. Demand is expected to be soft and industry price hikes are small (about INR10/bag).

financial_highlights.metric: Premium cement share of trade sales

financial_highlights.change: up ~INR1 vs Dec quarter; down vs ~INR255 last year

segments.name: Sanghi Industries (acquired)
segments.commentary: Cement capacity utilization about 57%; management targets 65-70% in FY27. Rail link at Naliya is an add-on, not in base case; seven marine vessels ordered for delivery from next year.

segments.name: Penna Cement (acquired)
segments.commentary: Utilization about 46%; management targets 55-60% in FY27. Breakdowns and deferred maintenance cited; Sanghi and Penna together hold 19 Mt capacity, with a 5-10% utilization uplift targeted.

segments.name: Orient Cement
segments.commentary: Management says Orient is running at full capacity; Orient was consolidated for 11 months in FY26.

segments.name: Ambuja and ACC existing assets
segments.commentary: Management expects 75-80% utilization in FY27; consolidated utilization estimated at 70-75%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume guided at ~80 Mt, about 8% growth, versus industry growth of 5-5.5%.
FY27 cost reduction of INR250/t on a full-year average; cost peak of ~INR4,500/t in Q4, Q1 FY27 seen flattish, with savings accelerating over the remaining three quarters.
Minimum cost reduction of INR250/t in FY27 and another INR250/t in FY28 (INR500 cumulative); management says the earlier INR3,650/t target is not abandoned.

Capacity to reach ~119 Mt by end FY27 after ~10 Mt of additions (commissioning Aug-Sep 2026 window); FY28 target capacity slips toward FY30; Maratha adds 4 Mt clinker; Mundra (2 Mt clinker) and Assam (2 Mt clinker) follow in about 24-28 months.
FY27 capex estimated at INR6,000-6,500 crore; project IRR hurdle of 18% stated.
Management did not give EBITDA/t guidance; said it is too early to estimate given volatility.
capex_capacity: Capacity 109 Mt at FY26 end after 10.7 Mt grinding and 7 Mt clinker added (Marwar, Farakka, Sankrail, Sindri, Krishnapatnam, Jodhpur, Bhatapara).
Clinker capacity 69 Mt now, rising to 73 Mt with Maratha (4 Mt).
About INR4,000 crore of capex already under execution (capacity, WHRS, fly ash transport); balance is debottlenecking and maintenance.

Recalibrating growth capex: shutting some grinding units in North UP, Bihar, South Gujarat and Maharashtra to move them closer to markets; a Bihar grinding unit planned; Dahej Line 2 as clinker-plus-cement example.
Management paused new projects until current ones are completed; engineering to be finalized over next 6 months.
demand_pricing: Industry price rise in March quarter was about INR10/bag, INR15-20 only in selected pockets; management says industry cannot pass on costs under relentless pricing pressure.
April-May demand described as subdued and soft; management would be happy if industry recovers half of a price hike.
Q4 FY26 volume growth was muted (Orient-adjusted flat YoY per an analyst); packing bag shortages linked to West Asia conflict cost volume in March.
Premium cement gap versus base product INR50-55/bag for super premium and INR20-25/bag for premium; price gap with the number-one player is INR5-10 in some districts.
Management expects FY27 demand to be soft due to inflation and weak monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 cost about INR4,500/t when management earlier pointed to an INR4,000 exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,000 was an aspiration for the March exit; March averaged ~INR4,100 normalized, with INR250 escalation from West Asia. Causes cited: branding, repairs at acquired plants, freight, packing, fuel and heat consumption, and lower government incentives.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost reduction is assumed for FY27 after Q4 inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,500 is the peak; a INR250/t reduction gives ~INR4,250/t for FY27 on a full-year average, with Q1 FY27 flat at ~INR4,500.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR3,650/t cost target be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said the target is not abandoned; INR500/t cumulative over two years is the committed minimum, with further runway to the earlier target.

qa_highlights.question: Why the reset in capacity and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said performance fell short of commitments, citing cost, wrong contractor choice, projects started without full engineering, and breakdowns at Penna and Sanghi; ~80% of the five KPIs relate to cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a target IRR for capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani stated a project IRR of 18%, all equity-funded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of high working capital and negative ACC operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinod Bahety said ACC has MSA receivables from Ambuja that will be settled via an ICD after shareholder approval; Ambuja's core working capital fell to 20 days from 30 days.

risks_watch: Cost trajectory: whether Q1 FY27 holds near INR4,500/t and the INR250/t FY27 reduction is delivered.
Acquired-asset utilization at Sanghi (57%) and Penna (46%) and reliability of Penna and Sanghi plants.
Pricing power in a soft demand environment; April-May trend described as subdued.
Capex execution delays (Maratha, Chhattisgarh) and capex recalibration; 10 Mt commissioning between now and September.
Non-core working capital, MSA receivables from ACC, and negative ACC operating cash flow, to be resolved via ICD.
Reduced government incentives after GST rate cuts and changed accrual policy.
535754|2026-03.management_tone: Candid and self-critical on execution, with management admitting missed targets and a partial reset in timelines. Confident on controllable cost levers, but evasive on EBITDA/t guidance and on pricing outlook, which they called soft.
key_quotes: Therefore, I strongly believe INR150 to INR200 savings will come from these components.
So we are not shying away from our target.
So we'll be honest with you. Yes, partially, there is a reset.
Yes, we are moving away from the time line.
But I think any guidance on EBITDA will be difficult at this stage.

535754|2026-06.headline: Ambuja Cements Q1 FY27: EBITDA up 331 bps to 16.7% and net cost down INR206/t to INR4,241/t, while total volumes fell (trade -2%, non-trade -21% YoY).
535754|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a value-over-volume quarter: trade share rose to 78% from 74%, and operating EBITDA reached INR1,589 crore on revenue of about INR9,500 crore. Net operating cost fell INR206/t sequentially to INR4,241/t, which management said absorbed about INR110/t of West Asia-related cost inflation. Volumes declined, with trade down 2% and non-trade down 21% YoY, and management attributed the quarter's weakness to diesel shortages, packing material issues and deliberate exits from low-margin South volumes. Management guided to 8% FY27 volume growth, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY, and reiterated INR4,250/t full-year cost guidance.

financial_highlights.change: down INR206/t QoQ; from INR4,447/t in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated cost base cited by analyst

segments.name: Trade / non-trade
segments.commentary: Trade share rose to 78% from 74% QoQ; premium products are 34% of trade sales. Trade volumes -2% YoY, non-trade -21% YoY.

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Trade volumes grew 2% YoY; management calls it the highest-EBITDA cluster. Roughly 25% of volume mix.

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Trade and non-trade both grew positively per management; about 30% of volume mix.

segments.name: East
segments.commentary: Trade volumes sustained with healthy margins; about 25% of volume mix.

segments.name: Central
segments.commentary: Volumes deliberately reduced; blended cement push lifted margins. About 10% of volume mix.

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: Highest YoY degrowth as about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume were cut; about 10% of volume mix. Channel build-out expected to take one to two quarters.

segments.name: RE power and fly ash (other operating income)
segments.commentary: About 45 crore units of RE power sold in Q1 for roughly INR140 crore revenue (vs 24 crore units / ~INR70 crore in Q4); fly ash sales about INR15 crore in Q1 vs ~INR50 crore in Q4. Both are netted in operating cost per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at 8%; July trade volumes reportedly up 8% YoY. Trade share guided to remain above 75%.
Full-year FY27 net cost target INR4,250/t reiterated; FY28 target INR4,000/t or below (about INR250/t further reduction).

Identified cost levers worth INR130-150/t: about INR35/t lead distance cut (15 km), INR30/t from raw material logistics and fly ash sourcing, INR50/t from energy (heat rate, power units, 75 MW new RE), and INR10-15/t other headroom.
Q2 FY27 net cost guided to be slightly better than June-quarter levels, after absorbing potential geopolitical cost rise of about INR100/t.
Capex FY27 about INR6,500 crore; Q1 spend about INR1,500-1,600 crore. FY28 capex similar at INR6,000-7,000 crore on a run-rate basis.
Installed capacity to reach 119 Mtpa by end-FY27 (adding about 10.2 Mt); 8-10 Mtpa of organic additions planned each year thereafter.
Long-term capacity utilisation target 70-75% on a value-focused basis; green power share to reach 60% by FY28 (48% on revenue-plus-consumption basis).
capex_capacity: Trial runs started at Dahej (1.2 Mt expansion); Salai Banwa (UP, 2.4 Mt) started; Bhatinda (Punjab, 1.2 Mt) and Jodhpur (Penna, 2 Mt cement / 3 Mt clinker) commissioned or stabilising, with Jodhpur clinker supplying grinding units from Q2.
Kalamboli (Mumbai, 1 Mt) and Warisaliganj (Bihar, 2.4 Mt) expected in Q2 FY27 (Warisaliganj most likely September).
Maratha clinker line (4 Mt) now expected Q1 FY28; Mundra expected 18-24 months out (around 2029).
RE capacity 973-975 MW (of 1,122 MW target; about 150 MW remaining); WHRS 228 MW rising to about 376 MW.
Three coal blocks in focus; first expected to be operational in about 30 months. AFR (alternative fuel) substitution at about 7%, targeted at 10-15% in FY27.
Sanghi: about INR600 crore jetty expansion for clinker. Penna: INR100-150 crore for AFR and WHRS. About 3.5 Mt of old ACC capacity temporarily closed for around six months.
demand_pricing: Management says cement demand was stable across infrastructure, housing and construction; July trade volumes reportedly up 8% YoY.
Q1 headwinds: diesel availability, packing material shortages and logistics disruption in West and East. Logistics lead distance fell from 269 km to 249 km YoY, yet freight per tonne was flat.
NSP rose sequentially but fell YoY; management attributed the gap to Incoterm and channel-cost netting. Analyst comparison put Q1 NSP about INR100/t below UltraTech's reported NSP.
Blended cement share 85%; clinker factor down about 3% to 64%.
Q2 FY27 cost pressure expected from geopolitical escalation (West Asia, fuel).

qa_highlights.question: Is it fair to expect muted FY27 volume growth if the value-over-volume strategy holds, given Q1 volume loss and earlier ~80 Mt chase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 8% FY27 volume growth, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY; non-trade is a 'well calculated' reduction, with market share said to have held or improved only on trade.

qa_highlights.question: Will green power be consumed in-house, and what is the incremental benefit as captive use rises versus selling power?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45 crore units sold in Q1; roughly 50% (about 20 crore units) expected to be consumed in Q2. Green power share is 34% on consumption basis, 48% on revenue-plus-consumption basis, targeted at 60% by FY28. Grid power costs INR7-8/unit versus the cost of captive green power, and sales are capped at around 10% of output.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 FY27 net cost rise given inventory buffers, and what is the full-year cost path?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 net cost expected to be broadly in line with or slightly better than the June quarter, after absorbing a potential geopolitical rise of about INR100/t. FY27 target INR4,250/t reiterated; FY28 target INR4,000/t or below. Clinker inventory about one month, coal about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade volumes still decline YoY, and how did the regions perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 hit by diesel shortages, packing material issues and logistics disruption. North trade +2% YoY, West grew in trade and non-trade, East sustained, South cut about 1 Mt of low or negative EBITDA volume, Central degrew on blended-cement shift. Capacity utilisation 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the INR206/t sequential cost reduction come from, and what was the gross saving after West Asia cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to fly ash sourcing, RE power price per unit, clinker factor down about 2-3%, marginal logistics gains (INR10/t), and fixed cost optimisation. Management said the INR206/t saving absorbed about INR110/t of West Asia cost, implying gross savings of about INR316/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NSP down about INR100/t versus UltraTech's reported NSP, and what are the Incoterm and netting effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NSP is netted for certain channel and Incoterm costs (ex-works terms), and that channel investment is being expensed against NSP. It did not quantify the gap and said NSP is market-driven.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company keeping plants temporarily closed and treating non-trade differently at acquired assets?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3.5 Mt of old ACC and one acquired-company facility temporarily closed for around six months; management said these are not permanent closures. Karan Adani said non-trade volumes at acquired assets were largely at negative or marginal EBITDA, so the company is prioritising value over volume.

risks_watch: Whether July's 8% trade volume growth holds and whether non-trade volume decline (-21% YoY in Q1) stabilises, given guidance needs roughly 12-13% growth in the remaining nine months.
Geopolitical and fuel cost pressure in Q2 (about INR100/t potential rise) versus the INR130-150/t cost-lever pipeline and the INR4,250/t full-year target.
Execution risk on capacity: Kalamboli and Warisaliganj (Q2 FY27), Maratha clinker slipped to Q1 FY28, Mundra around 2029, and 8-10 Mtpa annual additions thereafter.

Reconciliation gap: management did not provide a breakdown of cement vs RMC vs power vs fly ash cost, and deferred several analyst requests (fly ash/power cumulative P&L, RMC margin drop to about 7%, fixed cost bridge) to offline follow-up.

Accounting items to monitor: O&M cost equalisation across quarters still under discussion with auditors; INR24 crore termination-related exceptional item (VRS in South); depreciation true-up after Sanghi and Penna merger.
Green power transition: grid connectivity for some cement plants expected in two to three quarters, and green power share target of 60% by FY28 depends on consumption rising from about 50% of sales.
key_quotes: Our strategy remains clear and consistent, creating sustainable value ahead of volume.
Net operating cost reduced to INR4,241 per metric ton, a reduction of INR 206 PMT from the previous quarter.
So the operating company, Ambuja has no debt.

535754|2026-09.headline: Ambuja Cements Q2 FY27: consol EBITDA INR1,271 crore (~14% margin, INR770/t) on 16.5 Mt volume; guides FY27 cost INR4,250/t and 149 Mt by FY29.
535754|2026-09.overview: Ambuja Cements (consolidated, including ACC and Orient) reported Q2 FY27 cement volume of 16.5 Mt, revenue of INR9,197 crore, EBITDA of INR1,271 crore and PAT of INR236 crore. Trade volumes rose 8.6% YoY with trade share at 74%, while B2B volumes were still negative, so overall volume was roughly flat. Management announced 14 expansion projects adding about 30 Mt of cement and 10.3 Mt of clinker, with capex of about INR14,500 crore, and said the ACC and Orient mergers will now go to NCLT with completion targeted within FY27. Price held at INR255/bag, with INR10/bag realised in October.

segments.name: Institutional / B2B
segments.commentary: B2B volumes still negative YoY in Q2 after management sacrificed negative-EBITDA volumes; management expects both trade and B2B to turn positive in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Blended cement
segments.commentary: Blended share of sales rose to 82% from 77%; management targets an 80:20 blended to OPC mix.

segments.name: Ancillary (RE power, fly ash, RMC)
segments.commentary: Green power sales revenue ~INR136 crore (352 million kWh) in Q2; fly ash revenue ~INR25 crore; RMC EBITDA margin ~7%. Power sales booked in other operating income.

Industry demand expected at ~6-7% for FY27 per company presentation; H1 growth ~8% by the company's count.
Monsoon deficit and state drought declarations flagged as a lagged headwind for Q3 and Q4 construction activity.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the quarterly performance did not drive the decision; the first capex wave is nearly complete and the second wave is described as value-accretive, largely brownfield, and clinker-backed.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is needed to reach 149 Mt, and how does the debt position evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR14,500 crore for 30 Mt, roughly INR7,500 crore a year; management describes the programme as self-sustaining from cash flows with only interim debt if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence on execution, given ~20 Mt bunched into Mar-May 2028?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited past contractor issues, now resolved, and a tighter schedule of ~14 months for grinding units and ~18 for integrated units.

qa_highlights.answer: Imported spot fuel is INR2.80-2.85 per 1,000 kcal, versus a Q2 blend of INR1.87; the imported share is under 40% and pet coke is ~10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR4,000/t cost target inclusive of new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the INR4,000/t target for FY28 covers the combined existing and new capacity, with 149 Mt in FY28.

535755|2026-03.headline: ABFRL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR1,990 crore; Pantaloons grew 19% and reported loss narrowed to INR164 crore.
535755|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 16% YoY to INR1,990 crore, with Pantaloons up 19% (17% core format) and TMRW up 45%. Excluding a INR97 crore one-time demerger gain in the base quarter and an INR83 crore non-cash derivative gain at WROGN (TMRW associate), management said EBITDA grew 29% YoY at an 11.5% margin. Reported loss was INR164 crore versus INR171 crore a year earlier, and PAT loss narrowed to INR235 crore on an adjusted basis from INR289 crore. Management flagged a weaker wedding calendar, a marginal March slowdown from geopolitical disruption, and 3-4% raw material inflation with 5-8% price increases under evaluation for H2.

535755|2026-06.headline: ABFRL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% to INR2,026 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.2% and reported loss widened to INR249 crores.

EBITDA was INR167 crores (8.2% margin), with the Y-o-Y decline attributed mainly to lower treasury income and investment in new businesses; excluding treasury income, management says EBITDA rose. Reported loss widened to INR249 crores from INR234 crores, driven by higher Ind AS depreciation and finance costs from new stores. Wedding-related demand was hit by Adhik Maas, and TCNS like-to-like growth slowed to about 2%, which management called disappointing.

535789|2026-03.headline: Sammaan Capital's IHC takeover closed 31 March 2026; all three domestic agencies upgraded within 50 days, lifting bonds ~100 bps and targeting FY27 PAT of INR1,400 crore.
535789|2026-03.overview: This was the first earnings call after IHC's strategic investment, with IHC's share allotment completed on 31 March 2026 and IHC holding 28.5% equity (43.5% after warrant conversion within 18 months). Management said INR5,652 crore (USD 592 million) has been received via equity and 25% warrant upfront, with about INR3,200 crore (USD 335 million) due on warrant conversion. CRISIL (9 April), CARE (12 May) and ICRA (23 May) upgraded the company to AA+ across all three, with CRISIL and ICRA up one notch and CARE up two. The call centred on a multi-year plan (FY27 to FY30) with a 4.4% steady-state ROA, cost-to-income falling to about 26%, and a shift to a co-lending and asset-light model, alongside a legacy-book write-off/credit cost discussion. The call also included a correction of the FY30 ROA figure from 8-odd percent to 4.4%.

segments.commentary: Prime mass-market home loans (8.5% to 10% yield) to be sourced for sale to banks; affordable portion (10% to 13%) to be held on balance sheet. Management says mortgages drive growth in FY27 and FY28.

segments.name: Business loans and micro-LAP
segments.commentary: Prime mass-market loans yield 9.5% to 11% and are to be sold; semi-urban and micro-LAP loans yield 11% to 13.5% and are to be held.

segments.name: CRE project loans
segments.commentary: Done only on a co-origination basis with credit funds, pari-passu with no credit guarantee, with the company taking roughly 10% to 15% of disbursements.

segments.name: Gold loans and loans against securities
segments.commentary: Planned as the next secured products; gold needs a separate branch network, with wider product launches from FY28. About 240 branches are already sized for other products.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursements of about INR30,000 crore; Q1 FY27 disbursements to be at least 50% to 60% above Q4 FY26, then a 30% to 40% step-up on that base.

Marginal cost of funds to fall about 160 bps; cost of funds to decline 150 bps over three years; 270 bps total reduction tied to AA to AAA migration (120 to 150 bps on AA to AA+, and the rest on AA+ to AAA).
Portfolio mix target: 60% secured and 20% unsecured or semi-secured, with 80% retail; about 30% of incremental disbursements through co-lending or direct assignment.
Gearing capped at about 3.5x to 4x; liquidity held at the higher of 6 months of repayments or 10% to 15% of borrowings.
Target AUM of INR2 lakh crore and high-teen ROE (about 18%), with the timeline described as 'in no hurry'; FY27 and FY28 growth to be mainly mortgages.
capex_capacity: Branch network to grow fivefold to about 1,600 branches; workforce to rise to 20,000 people, with about 8,000 by end of FY26 per management.
A gold loan branch costs about INR20 lakh to set up and takes about 3 years to become fully productive and profitable; investment is not described as running into tens or hundreds of crore.
Technology spend (CRM upgrade and Salesforce deployment about 6 months ago) is expensed through the P&L, not capitalised; 37 AI use cases identified.
Targets: agent productivity up 30%, mortgage turnaround from 5 to 7 days to 2 to 3 days, loans per person per month from 0.6 to 2-plus.
demand_pricing: Management says productivity rose 2x between March and April 2026 following the shift to an asset-light model.
Disbursals of about INR72,000 crore planned for FY29 versus INR50,000 crore in CY17 and CY18 (as cited by management).
Competition: management says there are few AAA-rated NBFCs and that the market has room for new entrants; it cites AAA players (and 3 to 4 other AA+ players) disbursing around INR50,000 crore a year.
Management says insurance cross-sell reaches over 90% of borrowers.
Management says about 90% of borrowings are onshore; domestic bonds have appreciated about 100 bps since the IHC announcement, with international bonds about 250 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Varun Ahuja (BlackRock): Will offshore rating agencies follow the onshore upgrades, and is the slow cost-of-funds decline due to non-call fixed-maturity debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects international agencies to follow the domestic upgrades. Bonds cannot be renegotiated and have 3 to 4 year maturities, so the cost decline comes with a lag; incremental borrowing at lower cost and bank renegotiation are the levers.

qa_highlights.question: Renish (ICICI Bank): How will the company build non-mortgage portfolios, who will run them, and how will costs be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it has run secured and unsecured products at scale before, that tech and app-based lending help, and that people and tech investment will be made. Growth in FY27 and FY28 will be mainly mortgages, given no rush to hyper-grow.

qa_highlights.question: Bhanu Chauhan (Barclays): What share of growth comes from core versus new products?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 and FY28 disbursals are 80% existing products, falling over time; by FY30 the mix is targeted at 50% mortgage-backed and 50% other products.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash Singh (Emkay): How will competition from AAA NBFCs be handled, and is the FY30 ROA of about 8% correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the FY30 ROA figure was an error and corrected it to 4.4%, with FY27 at 1.8%, FY28 at 3.7% and FY29 at 4.4%. It says the market is large enough and that mortgage front-loading and co-lending support productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Naintara Ghosh (Deutsche Bank): How much investment is needed for the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment is mainly branches and people rather than large capex; technology costs already incurred (CRM, Salesforce) run through the P&L, and product-level ROA can be shared on request.

qa_highlights.question: Vineet Sharma (Param Capital): What drives the NIM rise from 3.5% to 5.8% when cost of funds is not falling as fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the NIM gain comes from the spread on sold-down loans (AUM less loan book rising from about INR30,000 crore to INR45,000 crore in FY28), and that equity adds liquidity without a P&L cost. Cost of funds shown is for on-balance-sheet borrowings only.

537259|2026-09.headline: Suyog Telematics Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 717 million (~INR 71.7 crore), EBITDA INR 431 million, net profit INR 153 million.
537259|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR 717 million, EBITDA of INR 431 million (about 60% margin) and net profit of INR 153 million (21.4% margin), with EPS of INR 13.09. Revenue per tower was about INR 30,000 per month, marginally lower because most Vodafone Idea rollouts landed late in the quarter and will be billed fully from Q3. Vodafone Idea's share of revenue rose to about 31% in Q2 (30% in H1) while BSNL fell to 1.1%. Management said Vodafone Idea and BSNL tenancy adds were slower than the June 2026 order flow implied, and BSNL work worth about INR 30 crore is unbilled pending site integration.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 stated as ~INR 70.95 crore by analyst; QoQ growth ~1%
EBITDA margin ~60%, stated as in line with previous quarter
Slight drop QoQ; management cited ~INR 31,000 per month per tower in its framing

financial_highlights.value: Bharti Airtel ~48.5%, Vodafone Idea ~30%, Jio ~19.5%, BSNL ~1.1%
financial_highlights.change: Vodafone Idea up ~3 pts; BSNL down from 2.5%
Analyst figure, not confirmed by management
Tax provision ~INR 8.5 crore; TDS deducted separately

segments.name: Tower infrastructure (India)
segments.commentary: 6,263 towers and 7,674 tenancies at end Q2; 356 new Vodafone Idea tenancies added in H1 and ~150 BSNL tenancies built but not counted. Revenue per tower ~INR 30,000 per month.

segments.name: Fibre
segments.commentary: Fibre network 6,510 km nationally after 200+ km added in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Government sites
segments.commentary: 20+ government site tenancies added in H1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 CapEx target about INR 200 crore, translating to about 2,000 tenancies, per management; to be updated monthly as operator confirmations arrive.

Management targets a quarterly revenue run-rate of INR 100 crore by September 2027; said current quarterly revenue is ~INR 75 crore, adding ~INR 15 crore per quarter (analyst computed ~INR 71.7 crore Q2 core revenue, management cited a 5-10% growth).
Vodafone Idea 45,000-site rollout over three years; Suyog targets ~5,000 sites in the next 2-3 years. Final Vodafone guidance for the next few quarters was still awaited as of the call.
Management expects ~INR 30 crore of BSNL billing to start in Q3-Q4 FY27 and BSNL pending sites to be completed by December 2026.
FY27 CapEx budget ~INR 200 crore: INR 120 crore from internal accruals and INR 80+ crore from sanctioned ICICI Bank debt. FY28 plans exist but not yet declared.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 CapEx primarily for Vodafone Idea rollout; 356 Vodafone tenancies added and billing started for all of them within about 30 days of RFI.
BSNL: ~INR 30 crore of CapEx spent on ~300 sites that are RFI-ready but not yet billed; BSNL integration delayed by Tejas equipment and fibre issues.
Capital work-in-progress closing ~INR 87-88 crore per analyst; ~INR 20-25 crore capitalised in the period (per analyst reading).
Capacity: management said it can deliver about 1,000+ sites per month across India; ~2,000+ Vodafone sites on list, with 600 Vodafone sites under LOI with site owners.
Management says CapEx is deployed only after a service order is received; MSA lock-in of 10 years with exit charges equal to 10 years of payments.
demand_pricing: Vodafone Idea received a 600+ site order around 15 June 2026; about 150 sites delivered within 15 days and ~200+ tenancies added in Q2 per management, versus ~600-700 expected by analysts.
Business model: IP fee, site rental (reimbursed), loading charges and electricity/diesel (reimbursed) under 15-20 year MSAs with 2.5% annual escalation on IP fee and loading charges.
Loading charges for Bharti Airtel upgrades about INR 2,500 per site; last year's upgrades lifted realisation from ~INR 28,000 to ~INR 30,000 per tower.
Management says Vodafone Idea and BSNL rollout depends on operator monthly and quarterly funding; delivery capacity not the constraint.
Management noted BSNL's delay as a risk: BSNL has not started billing on ~1,800 sites handled in total, with about 50% already billing per management.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR 200+ crore CapEx is for Vodafone vs BSNL, and what if customer commitments do not materialise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CapEx is deployed only after a service order; Vodafone CapEx is billed within ~30 days; ~INR 30 crore of BSNL CapEx (~300 sites) is unbilled pending integration. MSAs have 10-year lock-ins with exit charges equal to 10 years of payments.

qa_highlights.question: Why only ~206 Vodafone tenancies converted in Q2 versus 600-700 ordered, and is the 3,000-3,500 sites per month target confirmed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Vodafone releases orders monthly or quarterly and it cannot build without integration confirmation; 600 sites have LOIs. The 45,000-site three-year rollout is confirmed, but monthly phasing will vary with Vodafone funding. Final near-term guidance was still awaited.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR 200 crore FY27 CapEx funded, and what is the debt?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 120 crore from internal accruals and INR 80+ crore of sanctioned debt from ICICI Bank. FY28 expected debt not given (first FY27 planning).

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 100 crore quarterly revenue target on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue has moved from ~INR 60 crore to ~INR 75 crore per quarter and expects ~INR 15 crore per quarter additions, with INR 100 crore per quarter targeted by September 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will BSNL compensate for billing delay, and when will the 300 sites be billed?
qa_highlights.answer: MSA requires payment from RFI date with at most a 60-day waiver; no compensation decided. Sites expected deployed by December; billing expected Q3-Q4 FY27; rent to site owners on hold until integration.

qa_highlights.question: What is H2 revenue expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to INR 200 crore H2 CapEx (~2,000 sites) x ~INR 30,000 monthly per tower as a rough calculation, with shortfall possible on operator plans.

risks_watch: Vodafone Idea rollout pace depends on its funding tranches; monthly and quarterly phasing not yet confirmed; final guidance awaited.
BSNL: ~INR 30 crore CapEx (~300 sites) unbilled; billing dependent on Tejas equipment and fibre resolution; billing timing shifted to Q3-Q4 FY27.
Balance-sheet and funding: management gave only INR 200 crore FY27 CapEx split (INR 120 crore internal accruals, INR 80+ crore ICICI debt); FY27/28 debt level not disclosed.
Gap between CapEx deployed and tenancy additions: analysts flagged ~INR 150 crore of CapEx since FY26 vs ~400-500 tenancies added.
Quarterly revenue growth has been slow (~1% QoQ in Q2 on analyst numbers) versus the INR 100 crore per quarter target by September 2027.
537259|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the business model, CapEx-to-service-order discipline and contract terms, but evasive and inconsistent on tenancy and revenue timing, with several answers deferred to future operator confirmations. Management repeatedly qualified targets as dependent on operator plans.
key_quotes: We don't invest a single rupee without getting one service order from any of the operators.
45,000 is their confirmed rollout which they have declared on public platform also and that data is also with us also.
BSNL is to pay me from RFI date maximum 60 days waiver is allowed after which my billing starts automatically and BSNL will have to pay me as per MSA.
So, delivery is not an issue for Suyog.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management guided ~INR 200 crore H2 FY27 CapEx (~2,000 tenancies) funded by INR 120 crore internal accruals and INR 80+ crore sanctioned ICICI debt, but CapEx is only deployed after service orders, so timing depends on operator orders.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Only 356 Vodafone tenancies added in H1 versus 600-700 expected from the June order, and BSNL's ~300 RFI-ready sites are unbilled; quarterly revenue grew only ~1% QoQ to ~INR 71.7 crore, so growth hinges on Vodafone and BSNL funding and integration.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says FY28 plans exist but are undeclared, and the 45,000-site Vodafone rollout and ~5,000-site Suyog target over 2-3 years require further capex; capacity is 1,000+ sites a month, so the pipeline is not constrained by delivery.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management cut the INR 100 crore quarterly revenue target timing to September 2027 and Q2 revenue was only ~INR 71.7 crore, far from that run-rate, so an upgrade is not indicated.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Vodafone final guidance is still awaited, BSNL billing has slipped to Q3-Q4 FY27 on ~INR 30 crore of unbilled CapEx, and H2 tenancy target of ~2,000 depends on operator confirmations.

rows.label: BSNL ~INR 30 crore billing start
rows.why: Management expects ~INR 30 crore of BSNL billing once ~300 RFI-ready sites are integrated, with sites due to be completed by December 2026, though Tejas equipment and fibre issues have already delayed it.

rows.label: Realisation uplift from Bharti upgrades
rows.why: Last year's upgrades lifted realisation from ~INR 28,000 to ~INR 30,000 per tower, and loading charges are ~INR 2,500 per site, but Q2 realisation slipped to ~INR 30,000 from ~INR 31,000 as Vodafone rollouts landed late.

rows.label: Debt-funded CapEx from ICICI Bank
rows.why: INR 80+ crore of sanctioned ICICI debt funds part of the INR 200 crore FY27 CapEx, with INR 120 crore from internal accruals; FY27/28 debt level not disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on the business model, CapEx-to-service-order discipline and 10-year MSA lock-ins, but cautious on Vodafone and BSNL tenancy timing; analysts probed the gap between 600-700 expected and 206 converted Vodafone tenancies, plus the slow revenue growth.

537291|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 19% to INR 4,316 million, but gross margin normalised to 56% from 63% and PAT fell about 8% to INR 384 million.
537291|2026-03.overview: Nath Bio-Genes reported FY26 revenue of INR 4,316 million (+19% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 525 million (12% margin) and PAT of INR 384 million (9% margin). Gross margin fell to 56% from 63% in FY25 on richer product and market mix, and the tax rate rose to 11% from 5%. Growth was led by maize (volume +54%, value +78%), paddy (volume +25%, value +37%) and cotton Bt, while plant nutrition fell 18% on China export restrictions. Management guided FY27 top-line growth of 15-20% (calling 15% the base case) with slightly higher EBITDA and net margins, though guidance was qualified as conservative.

financial_highlights.change: down about 8% YoY per analyst question; effective tax rate 11% vs 5%
scaled up ahead of FY27 season

segments.name: Cotton (incl. Bt)
segments.commentary: Flagship hybrids Sanket and Jumbo drove Bt cotton volume up 22% YoY, with average Bt realisation up from INR 275 to INR 293 per unit as stated on the call. Management said supply constraints of the prior two years were resolved this year.

segments.name: Paddy
segments.commentary: Paddy volume grew 25% YoY to 75,619 quintals and value rose 37%. Management said paddy growth exceeded its 20-25% expectation.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: Volume rose 54% YoY to 9,639 quintals and value rose 78%; maize is now 10.72% of revenue and the fastest-growing non-cotton, non-paddy crop.

segments.name: Vegetable seeds
segments.commentary: Value fell about 11%, while average realisation rose 6% from INR 1,178 to INR 1,244 per kg, reflecting a shift to premium products.

segments.name: Plant nutrition
segments.commentary: Segment revenue fell 18% due to China export restrictions that disrupted supply; management expects normalisation in the coming year.

segments.name: Cotton-paddy combined and NCP
segments.commentary: Cotton-paddy share of revenue rose to 58% from 52%. Non-cotton, non-paddy (NCP) segment grew only about 4%; wheat and mustard value grew 10-15%.

segments.name: International (Uzbekistan JV)
segments.commentary: JV contributed about INR 15 crore (INR 150 million) to consolidated revenue for the first time in FY26, mainly cotton seed sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at 15-20%, with management saying 15% is the expected figure, described as conservative.
EBITDA margin to be maintained, with a slight upward trend in EBITDA and net profit margin in FY27.
Gross margin expected to settle around 53-54% per management's earlier view, versus 56% in FY26.
Finance and scheme-related costs expected to stay at about 1.5 percentage points above FY26 levels as a share of sales, per management.
International revenue target: not more than 10-15% of group revenue over 3-5 years; no financial target set for Uzbekistan yet.
Management said it hopes to cross INR 500 crore of top line soon, with no formal commitment.
capex_capacity: Capex policy is asset-light: only land bank and vehicles are capitalised; management is averse to investing in processing plants and storage, preferring rented capacity.
Cumulative cold storage, warehouse and conditioning godown capacity is 25,000 metric tons.
Maize processing need is about 15-20 days a year, which management cited as the reason not to own processing machinery.
Cotton production constraints of the prior two years were stated to be resolved this year, with production of about 70-80% of target versus 20% earlier.
demand_pricing: India's seed market is about USD 4-4.5 billion, growing at a 12-14% CAGR over five years, per management.
Management said cotton area is flat, so share gains come from competitors, and it expects further share gains next year.
Scheme spend fell to 28% of sales from 32% last year (in value terms, schemes rose); other marketing costs rise with inflation at 5-10%.
Central Asia: management cited a cotton market of about USD 100 million in Uzbekistan and about USD 450 million for all crops; the wider Central Asia market could reach USD 1 billion in 5-6 years.
Management said competition is now in-house, with new products such as product 2020 seen as better than Sanket.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Uzbekistan JV structure, crops sold, and revenue target over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Khurana said the JV has been operating for three years and this was the first year sales matched production; no financial targets are set yet. Dr. Kulkarni said the addressable market is about USD 500 million for Uzbekistan, and management will set targets after the next season.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue will international operations contribute over the next 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not more than 10-15% of revenue, which at a INR 1,000 crore top line would equal INR 100-150 crore. It described this as conservative.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue guidance by crop, and how is El Nino factored in?
qa_highlights.answer: Top line expected to grow 15-20%, with cotton around 20%, paddy above 20-25% and maize a key driver. Management said El Nino affects crops differently, but it expects balanced growth through crop, geography and duration diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Are there FY27 capex plans for processing, cold storage or new geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex is minimal, limited to land bank and vehicles, because processing and storage can be rented and maize processing is needed for only 15-20 days a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall and tax rate rise to 11% from 5%? What is the effective tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the PAT pressure to higher finance costs, scheme and marketing spend, and gross margin falling from 64% to about 56%. It said PAT margin dips about 1 percentage point, with costs stabilising.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash flow negative and why is inventory rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said free cash flow by formula is about negative INR 13 crore, but cash and bank balances of about INR 70-80 crore offset it. Stock build-up reflects cotton production recovering to 70-80% of target, and inventory is expected to be sold over the next two years given cotton's 5-7 year shelf life.

risks_watch: Gross margin normalisation to 53-56% could continue to compress PAT, which fell about 8% YoY despite 19% revenue growth.
Inventory of INR 4,446 million and trade payables of INR 1,305 million, with cash flow negative by about INR 13 crore on a formula basis; watch inventory turns and working capital.
Finance costs rose to INR 133 million from INR 96 million, linked to working-capital borrowing.
Monsoon and El Nino risk: management says exposure is mitigated by multi-geography and multi-duration products, but no quantified sensitivity was given.
Non-cotton, non-paddy segment grew only about 4%, so reliance on cotton and paddy (58% of revenue) remains high.
Uzbekistan JV has no revenue target yet; international contribution is about 3-4% of revenue (INR 15 crore of INR 4,316 million) and may take time to grow.
537291|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand and product pipeline, with repeated emphasis on conservative guidance. Cautious and somewhat evasive on margins, cash flow and international targets, which were deferred to next year.
key_quotes: And honestly speaking, this is the first year wherein our product has gone out to a very large scale in different provinces.
So, we expect the top line to be growing between 15 -20% around that time, and I'm again being conservative.
As a matter of policy, as a matter of strategy, Nath has not been investing much in CapEx.
It is always better to under commit and over perform.

rows.why: Management guided gross margin to settle at 53-54% vs 56% in FY26 and finance plus scheme costs about 1.5pp above FY26 as a share of sales, though EBITDA margin is guided to be maintained with a slight upward trend.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capex is asset-light with only land bank and vehicles capitalised, processing and storage are rented, and cold storage/warehouse capacity stands at 25,000 MT with no new capacity guided.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Top-line guided at 15-20% (15% base case) with cotton around 20%, paddy above 20-25%, and FY26 volume up 25% in paddy and 54% in maize, supported by management's expected share gains as cotton area is flat.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said capex is minimal, limited to land bank and vehicles, and that processing and storage can be rented; no utilisation figure was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called the 15-20% FY27 top-line guide conservative and hopes to cross INR 500 crore of top line soon, but gave no formal commitment; FY26 revenue was INR 4,316 million (+19%).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: PAT fell about 8% despite revenue +19% as gross margin dropped to 56% from 63%, and El Nino/monsoon risk is unquantified with cotton and paddy at 58% of revenue.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited a new product 2020 as better than Sanket and expects further share gains next year, but no launch date or count was given.

rows.label: Inventory build-up unwinding over two years
rows.why: Inventory is INR 4,446 million against trade payables of INR 1,305 million and free cash flow about negative INR 13 crore, with management saying stock will be sold over two years given cotton's 5-7 year shelf life.

rows.label: Uzbekistan JV and Central Asia expansion
rows.why: JV contributed about INR 15 crore (about 3-4% of revenue) in its first year of matched sales; management targets 10-15% international revenue over 3-5 years, but no financial target is set yet.

rows.label: Finance cost pressure from working capital
rows.why: Finance costs rose to INR 133 million from INR 96 million, and management guided finance and scheme costs about 1.5pp above FY26 as a share of sales.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, share gains and product pipeline, and called guidance conservative, but was cautious and deferred on margins, cash flow and international targets; analysts pressed on PAT decline, tax rate rise and the FY27 margin outlook.

538268|2026-03.headline: Wonderla Q4 FY26 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR135 crore and EBITDA doubled to INR43.8 crore at 32% margin, helped by Chennai ramp-up and a Labour Code provision reversal.
538268|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever Q4 by income, with revenue from operations up 40% YoY to INR135 crore and footfalls up 30% to 8.79 lakh, driven mainly by the newly opened Chennai park. PAT rose 49% to INR16.4 crore, aided by reversal of certain tax and Labour Code-related provisions created in Q3 FY26. For full FY26, revenue grew 13% to INR518.8 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to INR160 crore, but PAT fell 25% to INR81.7 crore against a deferred-tax credit of INR24.1 crore in FY25. Hyderabad footfall declined 7% for the year, and management guided to no large capex in FY27 apart from sustaining capex of INR35-40 crore.

financial_highlights.change: -25% YoY (vs INR109.3 crore; FY25 included INR24.1 crore deferred tax credit)

segments.name: Chennai Park (commenced Dec 2025)
segments.commentary: December footfall about 75,000 at launch; Q4 footfall about 1.91 lakh per management's figure cited by analyst. Management says first full quarter performance is in line with mature Kochi and Hyderabad parks, with Q4 EBITDA margin about 30%.

segments.name: Hyderabad Park
segments.commentary: FY26 footfall down about 7% YoY, attributed to summer weather and early monsoon, a school-group ban after road incidents (est. 50,000-60,000 footfall impact), and softer Q3 school groups. Management says it is still strong on a two-year basis.

segments.name: Bhubaneswar Park
segments.commentary: Close to 2 lakh footfall in FY26, first full year. Target about 2.5 lakh in FY27 (about 20% growth), with mid-term potential of 3-3.2 lakh.

segments.name: Resort and Hospitality
segments.commentary: Best-ever performance in Q4 on strong demand and occupancy. ISLE gaming pod commenced operations in June 2025 per management; current ADR about INR6,300, with 7-12% ADR uplift expected after Bangalore resort refurbishment.

guidance_outlook: No large capex planned in FY27; sustaining capex of about INR35-40 crore.
Incremental depreciation from Chennai about INR45-50 crore annualised in FY27 (about INR13 crore booked for four months); overall depreciation about INR80-83 crore per quarter currently.
Management expects EBITDA margins to settle around 40% over the next year as launch costs fade, subject to all parks including Chennai delivering.
A&P spend to be maintained at 7-8% of top line; no launch expenses expected in Q1 FY27.
Management aims to add at least 5 more parks, with 2-3 of the next 5 likely done within about 5 years; expects to close 1-2 real estate deals in FY27 across about 4 state governments.
Management says non-ticket revenue share should move towards 50:50 within 4-5 years, with 40:60 near term.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex: no large projects; sustaining capex INR35-40 crore.
CWIP of INR102.9 crore relates to Sky Wheel at Chennai, new attractions and a Bangalore roller coaster; to be capitalised in Q1 FY27.
Chennai park mature in about 3-4 years; management sees Chennai and Bangalore as top revenue parks long-term, followed by Hyderabad and Kochi.
Focus on Tier 1 cities over Tier 2 for new parks; Tier 1 land acquisition and state approvals are slower. Asset-light models being explored in larger cities.
Gross investment in assets about INR1,000-1,200 crore per management.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 trading: Chennai doing very well; some other parks growing, others flat; heat wave has not caused much damage so far.
West Asia tensions noted as a possible supply-chain and discretionary spend risk for April-May.
Management says Chennai is in a category already created by existing water parks, making market entry easier.
Hyderabad softness linked to weather and school-group ban; Ramoji Film City cited as a non-competing film city.
Management guides against predicting footfall or EBITDA until a full year at Chennai is complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Chennai footfall moderate to about 64,000 per month after strong December start, and what is happening in Hyderabad (FY26 footfall down 7%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Chennai: December launch month had higher marketing spend and Christmas seasonality; Jan-Feb are lean months. Hyderabad: early monsoon, Operation Sindoor-linked demand softness in summer 2025, and school-group weakness in Q3; management says two-year growth is still strong.

qa_highlights.question: Why are FY26 EBITDA margins only about 30% when older parks run around 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: corporate cost centre, one-time Labour Code costs, ESOP expenses, Chennai launch expenses and corporate setup costs are absorbed into the parks' margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the QIP-funded expansion been slow, and what is the status of new deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the shift to Tier 1 cities (land scarcity, slower government approvals) is the only cause; it is in talks with at least 4 state governments and hopes to close 1-2 deals this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for depreciation and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Chennai adds about INR45-50 crore annual depreciation; new investments add 8-10% of cost to annual depreciation. Margins expected to normalise towards 40% as parks mature.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bangalore resort ADR move after refurbishment?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects a 7-12% ADR increase from the current about INR6,300 after the refurbishment.

qa_highlights.question: Why do new rides not drive repeat visits?
qa_highlights.answer: MD: day outings need planning and most guests visit once a year or less; repeat rates are structurally low, and the core target is the 10-25 age group.

risks_watch: Hyderabad footfall trend: second consecutive year of decline, with FY26 footfall down about 7%.
Chennai sustainability: management declines to forecast beyond one full year; Q4 Chennai footfall moderated from the December launch peak.
Discretionary spend and West Asia tensions could pressure FY27 demand and supply chains.
Pace of new park additions: depends on Tier 1 land and state approvals; no deal signed yet.
Depreciation step-up of about INR45-50 crore in FY27 from Chennai, plus launch-cost normalisation to test margin recovery.
538268|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and Chennai, but cautious on near-term visibility; management repeatedly declined to give footfall, EBITDA or deal-timing forecasts, citing uncertainty and variability.
key_quotes: During this quarter, we had our highest ever Q4 with an income growing by 32% Y-o-Y, about INR142 crores, supported by footfalls of roughly INR8.79 lakhs.
We don't know EBITDA. 30% is the EBITDA margin for the last quarter.
We are at least talking to at least 4 state governments at any given point in time.
Near term, it will be 40-60 only. But definitely, I think in the next 4, 5 years, it should move to the 50-50 mark.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

538268|2026-06.headline: Wonderla Q1 FY27 income rose 41% YoY to INR252 crore and EBITDA 39% to INR122 crore, with Chennai Park adding INR45 crore revenue in its first year.
538268|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as one of its best quarters, with income of INR252 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA of INR122 crore (+39%) and PAT of INR72.79 crore (29% margin). Existing parks grew revenue about 15% on 7% footfall growth and 8% ARPU growth. Chennai Park, in its first year, contributed INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors, and management said it is tracking like a mature park for a Q1-type quarter. Management kept the new-park pipeline vague, saying an announcement on at least one park is expected before FY-end.

segments.name: Chennai Park (new, first year)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors; EBITDA contribution INR21.86 crore, 64% of EBITDA growth. Management said about 40-50% of land is developed (around 30 of 61.87 acres).

segments.name: Resorts (THE ISLE, Terrea, Wonderla resort)
segments.commentary: Added about INR3.19 crore EBITDA (9% of growth); best-ever quarter for both resorts along with Hyderabad park. Resort EBITDA is not disclosed; resort-related 'other' segment revenue was about INR63-64 crore per the segment data queried.

segments.commentary: Overheads rose INR6.5 crore YoY, mainly investments to strengthen the organisation; about INR1.5 crore incremental digital transformation (new POS from July) and about INR5 crore higher marketing YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7% ex-Chennai footfall growth sustainable, and what margin path should Chennai follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Footfall is unpredictable, but the year has started strongly. Chennai margins should converge to other parks over time, and Q1 is tracking similarly to larger parks.

qa_highlights.question: Will Chennai reach 1 million visitors this year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it would take a couple of years to reach 1 million visitors.

qa_highlights.question: How many parks will be added over the next 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans about 1-2 large parks and 1-2 small ones, with an update expected before FY-end. Parks will be picked based on land and government offers, and no closures were named.

qa_highlights.question: Is ARPU growth at Bangalore and Hyderabad a new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium cohorts and in-park experiences drove non-ticket spend, which is the main ARPU driver. Management said the base is now high, so similar growth may not repeat each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Monsoon effect on Q1 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monsoon had little effect because June is weak and May had no unseasonal rain. Management also cited the Kerala and Tamil Nadu elections and inflation in F&B as factors.

qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to take the resort model to other cities, including standalone resorts such as Goa, but will wait a full year before deciding. Timeshare was ruled out in favour of retail.

538268|2026-09.headline: Wonderla Q2 FY27 income rose 42% YoY to INR126 crore and EBITDA 90% to INR30 crore, with Chennai Park driving about 73% of the EBITDA increase.
538268|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first full quarter of contribution from Chennai Park, which added about INR28 crore revenue on 1.90 lakh visitors. Existing parks (Bengaluru, Kochi, Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar) grew revenue 8% on 6% footfall growth, and resorts grew 57%. Profit was about INR5 lakh versus a loss a year ago, with PAT held back by a INR10 crore rise in depreciation and higher tax. Management said Chennai will take 2 to 3 years to reach optimal utilisation, and that no new park is yet finalised.

segments.commentary: Q2 revenue +8% YoY on footfall +6% and ARPU +2%; contributed INR1.83 crore (13%) of EBITDA increase. H1 revenue +13%, footfall +7%. Bengaluru Q2 footfall 2.13 lakh (+9%), Kochi 2.02 lakh (+6%), Hyderabad 0.99 lakh (+7%), Bhubaneswar about 20,000 (-20%).

Non-ticket spend per guest up 11% in Q2 to INR510 and 16% in H1 to INR559; company says non-ticket share is around 30%+ of ARPU, in line with global trends.

qa_highlights.question: Was Chennai's lower Q2 ticket price (about INR948, 20% below the last three quarters' average) a deliberate push for footfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Dheeran Choudhary said the lower price came from a higher mix of discounted group visitors rather than a strategy, and that Chennai ARPU will grow in line with Kochi and Hyderabad over a year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an update on new parks?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Chittilappilly said there is no update yet and that the team is working on it. Later he said 2 to 3 new locations are being considered, with no final call taken.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Bhubaneswar Q2 decline weather-driven, and how will Chennai handle its first monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Bhubaneswar drop was entirely weather-led, with cyclones affecting about 20 of 30 districts. On Chennai, it said the monsoon will affect footfall but a fuller read needs the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT flat when EBITDA grew 90%, and when will earnings convert better?
qa_highlights.answer: Saji Louiz said the gap is driven by depreciation from large new parks (about 7-8% of roughly INR500 crore investment charged annually), so PAT will soften initially.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add capacity at Bengaluru or extend the resort model to other parks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on Bengaluru capacity additions. Resort expansion elsewhere will wait for one full year of the Bengaluru resort results.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company need equity dilution to fund future parks?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Chittilappilly said no further equity dilution is planned; internal cash flows can fund most capex, with some debt possible.

538446|2026-03.headline: Moneyboxx Q4 FY26 total income rose to INR63.23 crore (from INR52 crore), but Q4 PAT was only INR0.47 crore amid high credit costs and AUM at INR893 crore.
538446|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of transition, correction and strengthening, after MFI guardrails and stress in small-ticket secured lending hit collections and asset quality. Secured loans rose to about 68% of AUM (from 45% a year earlier), and collection efficiency was around 93.5% for the quarter. Gross NPA was 3.59% and net NPA 1.75%, both lower year on year, but Q4 profit was thin and AUM was down versus last year due to an ARC transaction. Management guided to AUM growth of 43-44% for FY27 and a sharp pickup in disbursements from May 2026, while acknowledging moderate growth so far.

financial_highlights.change: 6% growth as stated; management said YoY decline was due to ARC transaction
vs INR52 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Secured lending (MSME, branch-led)
segments.commentary: Secured share of AUM about 68% (5% of this is unsecured backed by first-loss fee guarantee), up from 45% last year. Secured disbursements were 67% versus 49% last year; target is nearly 80% secured AUM by March 2027. Average secured ticket size is INR6 lakh, with run-rate INR8-9 lakh.

segments.name: Renewable energy (solar) loans
segments.commentary: Launched in FY26; disbursements were about INR50 lakh in April, ramping roughly 10x in May to a possible INR5 crore. Management targets about 10% of AUM by March 2027. Average ticket about INR4 lakh, tenure about 4 years, yield about 22-24% including fees, with a second-loss fee guarantee after 3% first loss.

segments.name: Unsecured / digital lending
segments.commentary: Unsecured lending to be restricted to one state; below INR5 lakh secured ticket discontinued in most branches from April. A small digital unsecured lending initiative is planned to start in the current quarter, enabled by the in-house LOS Moneyboxx One.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth of 43-44% projected, as communicated to lenders; management said it has historically met lender-committed numbers.

Net worth considered adequate for FY27 plan; co-lending partnerships in secured space to be pursued; equity raise targeted in second half of FY27.
No new geographies in FY26-27; branch network to decline on a net basis via consolidation of rural branches and openings in Tier 1 cities.
capex_capacity: Branch network across 12 states; management is not seeking to expand branch count, consolidating rural branches and opening a few in Tier 1 areas (2 in Bangalore periphery, 1 in Jaipur).
Many branches are in early vintage (under 24 months); productivity is expected to improve as they mature, supporting operating leverage without aggressive expansion.
Newly launched in-house LOS Moneyboxx One and Sikka app are expected to improve turnaround time and field productivity, with benefits in coming months.
Decentralised credit underwriting model deployed, replacing the earlier centralised credit model.
demand_pricing: Management attributed slower growth to tighter underwriting after MFI stress, a state-head team rebuild and the shift to higher-ticket secured loans; some decline in demand acknowledged, with lenders across the sector tightening norms.
Secured yields will be lower; partnership and FLDG-backed business is expected to offset through lower opex and credit cost, per management.
Resolution rates improved: bucket 1 above 70% and bucket 2 above 75%, versus about 30-35% earlier. Current-bucket efficiency rose to over 99.4% in March from about 99% in January.
Management sees collection stress concentrated in the INR3-4 lakh secured ticket segment; SARFAESI and Section 138 actions started from May 2026.
Management expects a seasonal April-June weakness to be offset by solar loans, which peak in those months.

qa_highlights.question: Why has AUM growth remained moderate despite better collections and disbursements, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the post-MFI-guardrail shift, a senior team overhaul, decentralised credit and removal of sub-INR5 lakh secured tickets. It said top leadership is now in place, and that disbursements and AUM should grow month-on-month from May-June 2026, with FY27 AUM growth of 43-44% projected.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost appears high relative to AUM; how will opex come down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged high cost, attributing it to low AUM and hiring experienced staff; said cost should fall as AUM grows and that 20-25% of monthly business will come through partnerships without a sales team.

qa_highlights.question: Will the shift to secured lending lower yields, and what are the ROA/ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management accepted that yields will fall on secured and partnership business, but said lower opex and credit cost should offset this. It cited peers at 12-15% returns on assets as the benchmark, without giving specific ROA/ROE targets.

qa_highlights.question: Any new geographies or products planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No new states in FY27; the 12-state footprint is considered sufficient. Solar is the new product (about 10% of AUM targeted), with one or two more products and a cattle-loan FLDG partnership planned this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand slowing due to macro uncertainty and inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said appetite exists, but lenders have tightened norms and some demand has declined. Lending to restaurants was paused due to LPG shortage. It pointed to green shoots in the MFI segment and government guarantee support for working-capital loans.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the QoQ rise in GNPA and what is the Q1 FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Stress was concentrated in INR3-4 lakh secured loans and an older stressed book. Management said GNPA is falling monthly since January, with SARFAESI from May; disbursements in Q1 FY27 should beat last year, and Q2 should be far better.

risks_watch: Growth delivery: FY27 AUM growth of 43-44% and the month-on-month disbursement recovery must be shown in upcoming quarters, given two years of slow growth.

538562|2026-03.headline: Skipper Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,666 crore (+29.4% YoY) and PAT rose 70% to INR75.6 crore; FY27 guided to 15% revenue and ~30% PAT growth.
538562|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter to date: revenue INR1,666 crore (+29.4% YoY), EBITDA INR173.4 crore (+40.2%, margin 10.4% vs 9.6%) and PAT INR75.6 crore (+70%, margin 4.5%). FY26 revenue reached INR5,552.8 crore (+20%) with PAT of INR207.3 crore (+42%) and EBITDA margin of 10.3%. Order book closed at a record INR8,501.9 crore on record FY26 inflows of INR5,678 crore, but management flagged a temporary slowdown in domestic bidding and export disruption from the Middle East conflict, and guided FY27 conservatively at 15% revenue growth. Trade receivables rose sharply to INR1,485 crore, which management attributed mainly to a INR260 crore collection slipping into April and higher domestic billing.

segments.name: Engineering (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,248 crore, up over 33% YoY; FY26 revenue INR4,359 crore, up 24% YoY on transmission infrastructure demand.

segments.name: Polymer
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue crossed INR500 crore (about INR507 crore) as a record; volumes grew about 40% while value growth was lower due to lower commodity prices. Margin still low single digit.

segments.name: Infra / non-T&D
segments.commentary: Management said non-T&D is about 14% of the order book, mainly O&M for a BSNL project; infra revenue is largely T&D-driven. Order book has fallen from about INR2,000 crore to about INR1,000 crore over 6-7 quarters, per analyst.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: about 15% revenue growth (conservative, on an elevated base) and about 30% bottom-line growth, which management said is backed by the existing order book rather than new orders.
No explicit FY27 EBITDA margin number; management expects some margin improvement over FY26 but called it a challenging year with higher costs. Long-term aspiration is 12% EBITDA margin.
Management expects a return to 20-25% growth from FY28 as exports reopen and domestic bidding recovers; order awarding expected to approach FY25 levels from FY27.
FY27 capex guided at about INR250 crore, similar to prior years.
Export order book targeted to rise to 25% and eventually 50% of the order book (currently about 10%).
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion of 75,000 tonnes is due for commissioning by June 2026 (spillover from March), taking capacity to 450,000 tpa; utilisation above 85%.
Further 75,000 tpa planned in each of FY27 and FY28, targeting 600,000 tpa by FY28.
Management expects significant use of the new 75,000 tpa from Q3 FY27; full utilisation takes a couple of quarters. Expansion is expected to add about INR1,000-1,200 crore revenue annually.
Test Bed 2 commissioned, giving dual test beds at one location; a 293-tonne tower test set a record and a 350-tonne test is planned next month.
Growing substation business: about 4 high-voltage substation projects currently being executed.
demand_pricing: Order book INR8,501.9 crore (90% domestic, 10% export); FY26 inflows INR5,678 crore; Q4 inflow INR1,029 crore.
Bidding pipeline over INR33,000 crore, about 60-65% domestic and balance export; historical order conversion of 20-25%.

FY26 domestic bidding was well below FY25 because of ROW, forest clearance and transformer/HVDC equipment constraints; several projects (e.g., Krishnagiri REZ Ph-1, Vizag-Kakinada-Tuticorin, 800 kV Barmer HVDC) slipped into FY27. Management said bidding rebounded in April.

Export pressure: Middle East disruption and higher sea freight are slowing decisions in export markets; management said freight is largely passed through via FOB/CIF renegotiation and export is about 10% of the order book.
Pricing: mix of variable- and firm-price contracts; management said firm-price contracts carry buffers for commodity inflation. Raw materials are 100% indigenous.

Market share: Power Grid holds about 50% of TBCB bids and is over 90% of the domestic order book; private developers under 10%. Skipper claims about 50% of transmission-line capex as addressable (about INR50,000 crore on a INR1 lakh crore annual base).

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables almost double to INR1,485 crore despite 20% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a INR260 crore receipt due in late March came in on 1-2 April, and domestic Q4 revenue rose about 45% YoY with longer domestic realisation cycles plus GST; INR600-700 crore was already realised in April. Management said none of the debtors are sticky.

qa_highlights.question: What conversion ratio applies to the INR33,000 crore pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Historically 20-25%; management hopes to maintain that but declined to give an inflow number.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 revenue guidance only 15% if order book is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Export execution is uncertain given geopolitics and export orders are unlikely to execute this year; management called 15% conservative on an elevated base, with effort to beat it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY27 EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No exact guidance; management expects to improve on FY26's about 50 bps gain, with long-term aim of 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company move more capacity to domestic and maintain 20% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic bidding was weak in FY26 and it is pursuing domestic opportunities, but kept guidance conservative; 20-25% growth expected from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned for private-developer HVDC projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Private players are under 10% of the order book; management is in active talks with Tata Power, Adani and Resonia and says it is fully qualified for HVDC, currently executing a couple of HVDC projects.

qa_highlights.question: Are polymer non-Eastern market gains on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes grew about 40%, and presence has expanded outside the East, but the company is still small versus national players and remains focused on the Eastern region.

qa_highlights.question: Is the substation business margin-dilutive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said substation projects carry margins similar to the Engineering business on a project basis, though infra EPC is lower margin in general.

risks_watch: Receivables: confirm the INR260 crore April collection and the remaining receivables in the Q1 FY27 numbers.
Execution: right-of-way and forest clearance delays and transformer/HVDC equipment shortages could push project timelines.
Exports: Middle East disruption and sea freight costs may slow order decisions; export share target of 25% depends on this.
Capacity ramp: 75,000 tpa due by June 2026 and utilisation from Q3 FY27; slippage already happened once.
Margins: 30% PAT growth guidance relies on firm-price buffers absorbing commodity inflation; no EBITDA margin number was given.
Bidding: CEA's FY27 tender timing and the INR90,000-1,00,000 crore PGCIL bid pipeline must actually come through.

Management was evasive on specific numbers: no EBITDA margin guide, no order-inflow target, and no per-km HVDC opportunity size.

So we are planning about 75,000 this year and again, 75,000 next year.
Our bidding pipeline remains strong at over INR33,000 crores, providing strong visibility for future order inflows.
And firm price contracts come with significant amounts -- sufficient buffer to take care of the commodity price increase.

rows.why: 75,000 tpa due by June 2026 takes capacity to 450,000 tpa with utilisation above 85%, and another 75,000 tpa is planned in each of FY27 and FY28 to reach 600,000 tpa by FY28.
